author: bhanunuthakki
body:
## What & why

The scored confidence (S2) and the cross-source ⚠ disagreement that `pipeline.confidence` computes used to reach **only the UI popover**. The model that writes the Ask answer read the source *type* but never the confidence number or any "SEC says \$101M, 0.99% delta" warning — so it could not discount or stress-test shaky data. This closes that loop (Close-the-Loops L2, Wave A), near-free.

## Changes

- **`ask.grounding._fact_item`** appends a caution tag to a fact's *model-read* text when the newest row is shaky — a sub-par scored confidence and/or any unresolved validation issue, e.g. `[conf 79%; ⚠ SEC says $101M, 0.99% delta]`. The ⚠ strings are pulled **verbatim** from the same source the popover reads (`pipeline.confidence.display_issues_for_fact`). A clean, high-confidence fact stays un-annotated (no prompt noise). Unresolved issues are loaded **once per retrieval call** and threaded down — no per-fact re-query.
- **`build_evidence_block`** carries a new `WEIGH THE PROVENANCE` rule turning the tag into behavior: don't state a tagged figure as settled fact — surface the uncertainty, discount it, lean on higher-confidence evidence.
- **`_doc_meta`** also returns `source_quality_tier` (column-tolerant fallback) so the disagreement reads from the displayed cell's perspective, exactly like the UI.
- **`pipeline.confidence`** gains a public `IssuesByTicker` type alias so callers annotate the issues map without reaching into the private element type.

## Eval (item 4)

A **Mode-A behavioral canary** (`src/evals/provenance_caution.py` + `evals/golden/provenance_caution.json`), mirroring the injection-canary pattern: it drives the **real** `build_evidence_block` prompt and asserts the answer **flags / discounts** a contested figure rather than asserting it as settled fact. Two-direction unit tests (asserting → fail, hedging → pass) keep the invariant honest. Wired into the CLI runner (`run_llm_evals.py`), the dashboard run bar (`evals_panel.RUNNABLE_PURPOSES`), and coverage accounting (`evals.coverage`).

## Pre-existing red folded in

`test_runner_purpose_lists_stay_in_sync` was **already red on origin/main** (verified on a pristine worktree): the CLI runner gained `earnings_themes_split`/`qa_topics` but the run bar wasn't updated. Folded both into `RUNNABLE_PURPOSES` alongside `provenance_caution` so the registries match.

## For the siblings

The enriched fact-text format is the one seam **L10** (credibility engine) and **L12** (static-prose citations) build on — documented in the module docstring and `_provenance_annotation`.

## Coordination
- No overlap with **#545 (L1)** (packs/router/calibration).
- Touches `run_llm_evals.py` + `evals_panel.py` (the purpose tuples) which **#546 (L3)** also edits — additive, trivially mergeable; no conflict on `coverage.py` or `grounding.py`.

## Testing

`ruff` + whole-file format + `pyright` strict clean on all touched files. 231 tests green across the grounding / confidence / lineage / ask-engine / followup / eval-panel / coverage / injection-canary / provenance-caution suites. LLM transport monkeypatched throughout (conftest-enforced); the live eval proof run is deferred to the owner (real model spend).

- `derive_download_window(now, *, train_years, start_margin_days=45, data_end=None) -> (start_dl, end_dl)` — derives the ENTSO-E download window from a training horizon. Requires a tz-aware `now`; rejects bool/non-positive `train_years` and malformed `data_end`.
- `extract_entsoe_hourly_forecast(interim, *, column="Forecasted Load")` — resamples an interim frame's day-ahead forecast column to a clean hourly series; raises on missing column / non-`DatetimeIndex` / all-NaN.
- `download_side_tables(...)` — one call to refresh the renewable-forecast and day-ahead-price side tables. **Fail-loud by default** (`on_provider_failure="raise"`); `"skip"` is opt-in, logged degradation (operator policy).

## Constraints respected

- **No `spotforecast2` import** (one-way fail-safe boundary preserved).
- Fail-safe: every function raises on invalid input; no silent repair.
- No `__init__.py` change — downloader functions are imported by full path; the three symbols are registered in `_quarto.yml` only.
- The warn-and-continue / fallback **policy stays operator-side**; only mechanism is upstreamed.

## STRIDE

No threat-model table update required: the two pure functions cross no boundary, and `download_side_tables` opens no new endpoint (it orchestrates the already-covered `query_wind_and_solar_forecast` / `query_day_ahead_prices`, inheriting their bounded-retry countermeasure). The certified default is unchanged (`"raise"`); `"skip"` is opt-in and logged.

## Tests / docs

- New `tests/test_downloader_entsoe_utils.py` (pure functions, incl. fail-safe paths).
- Extended `tests/test_downloader_entsoe_side_tables.py` (raise/skip/invalid/country-routing for `download_side_tables`).
- Local fast suite: 2689 passed, 1 skipped; coverage 73.8% (ratchet 68).
- Reference pages generated; registered in `_quarto.yml`.

author: hawkingrei
body:
## Problem

The body-store stress workflow added in #776 used Bazel's `--test_filter` to scope the run to the `conversation_cases` suite. But **`rules_rust`'s `rust_test` ignores `--test_filter`**, so the job actually reran the **entire ~689-test `agenthub_unit_tests` binary 25×** — slow, and it pulled in an unrelated **flaky** test from the full suite. That's exactly why the first run on #776 failed (`FAIL: //:agenthub_unit_tests (run 1 of 25)`, with the log showing `actor_cli::…`/`api::…` tests running); the review-fix commit only passed by luck.

## Fix

Pass the libtest filter as **`--test_arg`** instead, which the test binary honors as a positional filter, and scope the db target to its outbox tests the same way (each test binary takes its own filter, so the two-target command is split).

Verified locally:
- `//:agenthub_unit_tests --test_arg='team::manager::tests::conversation_cases::'` → **running 16 tests** (673 filtered out)
- `//crates/agenthub-db:agenthub_db_tests --test_arg='message_body_outbox'` → **running 3 tests** (32 filtered out)
- `--runs_per_test=2` reruns pass.

Now the stress job exercises only the body-store tests, so unrelated suite flakiness can't fail it (and it's far faster).

## Follow-up (separate)

The full suite does have a latent flaky test that surfaces under repeated runs — out of scope here, but worth tracking down separately.

author: tonykoop
body:
Closes #87 (the spec deliverable for the Workflow Track epic #100).

Establishes `docs/WORKFLOW_TRACK.md` — the design contract for benchmarking **human-AI hardware-engineering workflows** (Fable 5 + Fusion + Adam, SOLIDWORKS + Leo, Claude + Blender MCP) alongside, but strictly walled off from, the autonomous model science.

## The load-bearing ideas
- **Architectural unlock:** MakerBench grades the exported artifact, not the process — so a workflow is a new *provenance lane* feeding the deterministic graders we already have, not a new grader.
- **The science:** league separation is the controlled-variable rule of the scientific method. Autonomous varies only the model; Workflows varies the whole human+AI+CAD system. Mixing them ruins both measurements — so they **never rank head-to-head**.
- **Taxonomy:** `harness_class` (`autonomous` | `assisted-workflow`) + `harness_subclass` (`api-driven-code` | `gui-injected-copilot`), as **additive `RunResults` fields** that join the grouping key — orthogonal to `track`/`result_provenance`/`verification_status`, legacy bundles default to `autonomous`.
- **Disclosed-not-proven trust:** the artifact regrade still proves the geometry; the *process* can't reproduce (closed plugin + human), so workflow rows **cap at `public-regrade-verified`** — `official-heldout-verified` is structurally impossible.
- **WorkflowManifest + Human Intervention Index (L0/L1/L2)**, extending the existing `DesignDossier` + `perception_trace`; passive trace↔geometry consistency + community "show your work" anti-gaming.

Grounded in the real schema (`RunResults`, the verification ladder, the grouping key) and cross-linked to `COMMUNITY_SUBMISSION.md` / `SUBMISSION_CONTRACT.md` / `DOMAIN_MATRIX.md` / `PROFILE_LIFECYCLE.md`. Linked from `DOMAIN_MATRIX.md`. Carries the canary; exposes no oracle geometry, golden masters, or held-out seeds.

Unblocks the rest of #100 (#88–#99).

🚨 **Severity: HIGH**

💡 **Vulnerability:** 
1. **Secret Exposure:** Hardcoded Firebase API keys and project IDs were tracked in version control within the `v2_secured` directory.
2. **Broken/Leaky Auth:** The 'service' role hash was incorrect (preventing login), and failed login attempts were logged to the console, exposing hashes.
3. **Insecure Contexts:** The `hashPin` function lacked a check for the Web Crypto API, which is unavailable in non-HTTPS environments, potentially causing silent failures.

🎯 **Impact:** 
- Attackers with repository access could obtain Firebase credentials.
- Users in insecure contexts (non-localhost HTTP) would experience broken authentication.
- Console logging of hashes could assist in offline brute-force attacks if an attacker has physical access to a terminal.

🔧 **Fix:** 
- Deleted the tracked `v2_secured/js/config.js` and added recursive `.gitignore` protection.
- Patched `v2_secured/js/app.js` to fix the 'service' hash, remove the debug log, and add secure context validation.

✅ **Verification:** 
- Functional login for the 'service' role was verified using a Playwright script mocking the Firebase environment.
- Secret removal was confirmed via `git ls-files`.
- UI integrity was verified via screenshots of the login and service dashboard.

## ملخص
إصلاحات جودة وصحّة ردود الذكاء الاصطناعي للعميل (من فحص جذري بـ agents متوازية). كلها مختبَرة.

### منع التكرار الحرفي (B)
- تعليم الرسالة 'مُجابة' **قبل** جدولة الإرسال (يغلق نافذة crash/SIGTERM/retry التي تولّد رداً ثانياً).
- حارس يمنع رسالة 'لحظات من فضلك' أن تُرسَل فوق رد حقيقي.

### إلغاء رد البوت عند ردّ المالك (A)
- يُلغى رد البوت إذا وُجدت رسالة بشرية (جوال `sent_by_human` أو داشبورد `manual_send`) أحدث من رد البوت — لا يعتمد فقط على نافذة `escalated_until`.

### الردود المتعددة المتناقضة + تسرّب العبارة الممنوعة (المشكلة الجديدة)
- البرومبت: افهم النية أولاً → مسار واحد فقط؛ ممنوع جمع 'اطلب معلومة' + 'وعد تصعيد' في رسالة؛ لا تعِد بالتصعيد إلا إذا ستصعّد فعلاً؛ احترم العبارات الممنوعة من المالك.
- `reply-validator`: لا تصعيد تلقائي بينما الرد يطلب معلومة من العميل (الطلب الصريح للعميل يبقى يُصعّد).
- تخفيف توجيه تجميع الرسائل من 'أجب عليها كلها' إلى 'رد واحد متماسك حسب النية'.

### جودة المحادثة (C)
- قواعد runtime: منع الحشو المتكرر ('تأمر بشي ثاني؟') إلا عند خطوة بيع مفتوحة؛ كشف رضا العميل (تمام/خلاص/شكراً) والإغلاق بلا سؤال متابعة؛ لا تكرار داخل الرد؛ تصرّف كبشري.
- `meta-prompts`: سؤال الإغلاق صار مشروطاً. الداشبورد: إلغاء عبارات الإغلاق الافتراضية.

## التحقق
+24 اختبار. السويت الكامل 879/880 منطقياً (الإخفاق الوحيد = عطل libuv أثناء `--test-force-exit` على `startup-health`).

استرجاع الرسالة المفقودة بعد الانقطاع (نافذة الانقطاع)، مدقّق الهلوسة البرمجي (أسعار/روابط)، وحدود الحِمل per-merchant.

Adds the cross-recording / treatment-comparison phase.

## Compare dock
Pick a per-cell metric and compare it **across recordings grouped by condition**, with **recording = the experimental unit**:
- **Recording means** — a strip of per-recording values per condition + mean ± SEM.
- **Superplot** — the per-cell cloud (coloured by recording) behind the per-recording means.

- Click a point → load that recording; min-frames filter; CSV export of the per-cell + per-recording tables.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **5.4.3** to **9.1.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.0.3
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `12444 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12444>`_: Fixed :func:`pytest.approx` which now correctly takes into account :class:`~collections.abc.Mapping` keys order to compare them.


- `13634 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13634>`_: Blocking a ``conftest.py`` file using the ``-p no:`` option is now explicitly disallowed.

  Previously this resulted in an internal assertion failure during plugin loading.

  Pytest now raises a clear ``UsageError`` explaining that conftest files are not plugins and cannot be disabled via ``-p``.


- `13734 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13734>`_: Fixed crash when a test raises an exceptiongroup with ``__tracebackhide__ = True``.


- `14195 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14195>`_: Fixed an issue where non-string messages passed to `unittest.TestCase.subTest()` were not printed.


- `14343 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14343>`_: Fixed use of insecure temporary directory (CVE-2025-71176).



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `13388 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13388>`_: Clarified documentation for ``-p`` vs ``PYTEST_PLUGINS`` plugin loading and fixed an incorrect ``-p`` example.


- `13731 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13731>`_: Clarified that capture fixtures (e.g. ``capsys`` and ``capfd``) take precedence over the ``-s`` / ``--capture=no`` command-line options in :ref:`Accessing captured output from a test function <accessing-captured-output>`.


- `14088 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14088>`_: Clarified that the default :hook:`pytest_collection` hook sets ``session.items`` before it calls :hook:`pytest_collection_finish`, not after.


- `14255 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14255>`_: TOML integer log levels must be quoted: Updating reference documentation.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `12689 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12689>`_: The test reports are now published to Codecov from GitHub Actions.
  The test statistics is visible `on the web interface
  <https://app.codecov.io/gh/pytest-dev/pytest/tests>`__.

  -- by :user:`aleguy02`
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.2
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress feature added in pytest 9.0.0 has been disabled by default, except on Windows, due to compatibility issues with some terminal emulators.

  You may enable it again by passing ``-p terminalprogress``. We may enable it by default again once compatibility improves in the future.

  Additionally, when the environment variable ``TERM`` is ``dumb``, the escape codes are no longer emitted, even if the plugin is enabled.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the :confval:`tmp_path_retention_count` settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13946 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946>`_: The private ``config.inicfg`` attribute was changed in a breaking manner in pytest 9.0.0.
  Due to its usage in the ecosystem, it is now restored to working order using a compatibility shim.
  It will be deprecated in pytest 9.1 and removed in pytest 10.


- `13965 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13965>`_: Fixed quadratic-time behavior when handling ``unittest`` subtests in Python 3.10.



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `4492 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4492>`_: The API Reference now contains cross-reference-able documentation of :ref:`pytest's command-line flags <command-line-flags>`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.1
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13895 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13895>`_: Restore support for skipping tests via ``raise unittest.SkipTest``.


- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress plugin added in pytest 9.0 is now automatically disabled when iTerm2 is detected, it generated desktop notifications instead of the desired functionality.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the verbosity settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13910 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13910>`_: Fixed `UserWarning: Do not expect file_or_dir` on some earlier Python 3.12 and 3.13 point versions.



Packaging updates and notes for downstreams
-------------------------------------------

- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `13891 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13891>`_, `#13942 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13942>`_: The CI/CD part of the release automation is now capable of
  creating GitHub Releases without having a Git checkout on
  disk -- by :user:`bluetech` and :user:`webknjaz`.


- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------


- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

  This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in `pytest-subtests <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests>`__, but since then has been merged into the core.

  .. note::

      This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.


- `13743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743>`_: Added support for **native TOML configuration files**.

  While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in ``pyproject.toml`` files under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]``,
  it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings.
  Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

  In ``pyproject.toml``, the native TOML configuration is under the ``[tool.pytest]`` table.

  .. code-block:: toml

       pyproject.toml
      [tool.pytest]
      minver

author: yzong-rh
body:
## Purpose

Following #45003 and #45396, attempt to implement constrained decoding for tool calls for Harmony models.

Related: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35904. Also "embed content constraints in structural tags".

### Problem

vLLM's constrained decoding for the Harmony delays enforcing `response_format` constraints (`json_object`, `json_schema`, `structural_tag`) until `<|channel|>final...<|message|>` is detected. This works correctly for JSON formats but creates a mismatch for structural-tag tool calling, since those constraints need to apply during the commentary/tool-call phase rather than only in the final-message channel.

### Solution

Rewrite `json_object`/`json_schema` `response_format`s into a Harmony-aware structural_tag (encoding the analysis and final-message boundaries directly in the grammar) so that constrained decoding is governed entirely by the structural tag throughout the entire generation.

1. Define custom structural tags for GPT-OSS models that constrains the entire generation, not just the final channel
  - Two paths: with and without builtin tools (guided vs fallback-guided)
  - Without builtin tools, the constraints will ensure each generated function has 100% the correct format
  - With builtin tools, the constraints take a fallback path that only ensures some tool is called (no validation on tool name or arguments).
2. Override `HarmonyParser`'s `adjust_request` so that JSON `response_format` gets wrapped into structural tags that apply over the entire generation.
3. Update CC and Responses API to call `adjust_request` for Harmony models
4. Clean up `GptReasoningParser`'s reasoning_end methods and tests (they are no longer required).

author: karlkfi
body:
## What

Adds `docs/plan/platform-owned-quota.md` and a prioritized Queue item (Q130, `infra`/`security`/`1.0-gate`) for a design change: the platform admin owns the Namespace + `ResourceQuota` + `LimitRange`; GAG operates within them and never creates them. Removes `spec.namespaceQuota` from the `ActionsGateway` CRD and drops the GMC's quota-write RBAC.

Plan doc only — no CRD/code/RBAC edits here; those land in their own PR(s).

## Why

The website rework surfaced that the implementation contradicts the value prop. The CR carries a **tenant-authored** `spec.namespaceQuota` and the GMC materializes it — so a tenant can set their own cap (no real platform enforcement), and GAG creating its own `ResourceQuota` conflicts with platform namespace/quota management (GitOps, Capsule/HNC/vCluster/kiosk). Moving ownership to the platform also drops GMC privilege (least privilege) and partly subsumes Q122.

Flagged 1.0-gate because it's a **breaking CRD change** — free now, but post-1.0 it would need a conversion webhook (deferred Q74).

## Testing

Docs-only. `make lint-status` passes; STATUS.md change is isolated in its own commit.

author: jonyardley
body:
## Problem

When the iPad is plugged in but still **locked or not yet trusted**, it appears to discovery (so `hasDevice` is true) but no session starts (`isRunning` false, `failed` not latched) — so the state machine sits in `.starting` and the popover shows only "Connecting…" indefinitely. It reads as broken when the user just needs to unlock the iPad / tap Trust.

## Change

Add a small caption hint under the status line for the transitional/empty states (view-only; the pure `AppState.reduce` is unchanged):

| State | Status | New hint |
|---|---|---|
| `.noDevice` | No iPad connected | Connect your iPad with its cable to begin. |
| `.starting` | Connecting… | Unlock your iPad and tap Trust if it asks. |
| `.failed` | Couldn't start the iPad feed. | Check your iPad is unlocked and connected, then Retry. |

The app can't distinguish "locked" from "still trusting" (AVFoundation doesn't expose it), so the `.starting` hint covers both honestly.

## Verification

- `just build` ✅, `just test` ✅ (96 tests), `just lint` clean (only the pre-existing `AppModel.swift` file-length warning).
- **Needs a manual hardware check** (the locked/trust path can't be unit-tested): plug in a locked iPad → confirm the popover shows "Connecting…" + "Unlock your iPad…" rather than looking stuck, and the hint clears once it goes live.

No emojis in copy.

## What

The seeded compute catalog was tiny (~10 entries). This grows it to **180** across **AWS (78) / GCP (52) / Azure (50)** so estimators can pick the instance they actually need.

## Coverage

- **AWS EC2** — general purpose (T3, T4g, M5, M6i, M7i, M7g), compute optimized (C5, C6i, C7g), memory optimized (R5, R6i, X2idn), storage optimized (I3, I4i, D3), and **accelerated/GPU/ML** (G4dn, G5, P3, P4d, Inf2, Trn1); plus S3 + EBS.
- **GCP Compute Engine** — E2, N1, N2, N2D, T2D, C2, C3, highmem/highcpu, M1/M2 ultramem, and **A2 (A100) / G2 (L4)**; plus Cloud Storage.
- **Azure Virtual Machines** — B (burstable), D (v3/v5/AMD), F (compute), E (memory), M (large memory), L (storage), and **N-series GPUs** (T4 / A100); plus Blob + Managed Disks.
- Alternate-region samples (`eu-west-1`, `europe-west1`, `westeurope`).

A `catalogRows([sku, price])` builder keeps the seed compact, and `GCP_MACHINE_SPECS` was extended (E2/N2/N2D/T2D/N1 standard sizes) so the live **Refresh** (FR-21a) can re-price more of them. Existing catalog keys are preserved (idempotent upsert) — **no migration**, and saved estimate price snapshots are untouched (NFR-14).

This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Type | Update | Change | |---|---|---|---| | [pytest](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) ([changelog](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/changelog.html)) | project.optional-dependencies | minor | `==9.0.*` -> `==9.1.*` | --- ### Release Notes
pytest-dev/pytest (pytest) ### [`v9.1.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.1.1) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/9.1.0...9.1.1) ### pytest 9.1.1 (2026-06-19) #### Bug fixes - [#​14220](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14220): Fixed a logic bug in `pytest.RaisesGroup` which would might cause it to display incorrect "It matches FooError() which was paired with BarError" messages. - [#​14591](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14591): Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1.0 which caused overriding a parametrized fixture with an indirect [@​pytest](https://redirect.github.com/pytest).mark.parametrize to fail with "duplicate parametrization of '\'". - [#​14606](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14606): Fixed `list-item` typing errors from mypy in `@pytest.mark.parametrize ` `argvalues` parameter. - [#​14608](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14608): Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1.0 where `conftest.py` files located in `/test*` were no longer loaded as initial conftests when invoked without arguments. This could cause certain hooks (like `pytest_addoption`) in these files to not fire. ### [`v9.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.1.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/9.0.3...9.1.0) ### pytest 9.1.0 (2026-06-13) #### Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes - [#​14533](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14533): When using `--doctest-modules`, autouse fixtures with `module`, `package` or `session` scope that are defined inline in Python test modules (not plugins or conftests) will now possibly execute twice. If this is undesirable, move the fixture definition to a `conftest.py` file if possible. Technical explanation for those interested: When using --doctest-modules, pytest possibly collects Python modules twice, once as `pytest.Module` and once as a `DoctestModule` (depending on the configuration). Due to improvements in pytest's fixture implementation, if e.g. the `DoctestModule` collects a fixture, it is now visible to it only, and not to the `Module`. This means that both need to register the fixtures independently. #### Deprecations (removal in next major release) - [#​10819](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10819): Added a deprecation warning for class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods (without `@classmethod`). Such fixtures set attributes on a different instance than the test methods use, leading to unexpected behavior. Use `@classmethod` decorator instead -- by `yastcher`. See `10819` and `14011`. - [#​12882](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12882): Calling `request.getfixturevalue() ` during teardown to request a fixture that was not already requested is now deprecated and will become an error in pytest 10. See `dynamic-fixture-request-during-teardown` for details. - [#​13409](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13409): Using non-`~collections.abc.Collection` iterables (such as generators, iterators, or custom iterable objects) for the `argvalues` parameter in `@pytest.mark.parametrize ` and `metafunc.parametrize ` is now deprecated. These iterables get exhausted after the first iteration, leading to tests getting unexpectedly skipped in cases such as running `pytest.main()` multiple times, using class-level parametrize decorators, or collecting tests multiple times. See `parametrize-iterators` for details and suggestions. - [#​13946](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946): The private `config.inicfg` attribute is now deprecated. Use `config.getini() ` to access configuration values instead. See `config-inicfg` for more details. - [#​14004](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14004): Passing `baseid` to `~pytest.FixtureDef` or `nodeid` strings to fixture registration APIs is now deprecated. These are internal pytest APIs that are used by some plugins. Use the `node` parameter instead for fixture scoping. This enables more robust node-based matching instead of string prefix matching. If you've used `nodeid=None`, pass `node=session` instead. This will be removed in pytest 10. - [#​14335](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14335): The method of configuring hooks using markers, deprecated since pytest 7.2, is now scheduled to be removed in pytest 10. See `hook-markers` for more details. - [#​14434](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14434): The `--pastebin` option is now deprecated. The same functionality is now available in an external plugin, `pytest-pastebin`. See `pastebin-deprecated` for more details. - [#​14513](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14513): The private `FixtureDef.has_location` attribute is now deprecated and will be removed in pytest 10. See `fixturedef-has-location-deprecated` for details. - [#​1764](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1764): `pytest.console_main` is now deprecated and will be removed in pytest 10. It was never intended for programmatic use; use `pytest.main` instead. #### New features - [#​12376](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12376): Added `pytest.register_fixture()` to register fixtures using an imperative interface. This is an advanced function intended for use by plugins. Normally, fixtures should be registered declaratively using the `@pytest.fixture ` decorator. Pytest looks for these fixture definitions during the collection phase and registers them automatically. For some plugin usecases the declarative interface can be cumbersome or unviable, in which case this imperative interface can be used. - [#​14023](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14023): Added --report-chars long CLI option. - [#​14371](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14371): Added `--max-warnings` command-line option and `max_warnings` configuration option to fail the test run when the number of warnings exceeds a given threshold -- by `miketheman`. - [#​6757](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6757): Added the `assertion_text_diff_style` configuration option, allowing string equality failures to be rendered as separate `Left:` and `Right:` blocks instead of `ndiff` output. - [#​8395](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8395): Added support for `~datetime.datetime` and `~datetime.timedelta` comparisons with `pytest.approx`. An explicit `abs` or `rel` tolerance as a `~datetime.timedelta` is required and relative tolerance is not supported for datetime comparisons -- by `hamza-mobeen`. #### Improvements in existing functionality - [#​11225](https://redirect.github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11225): `pytest.warns` now shows "Regex pattern did not match" instead of "DID NOT WARN" when warnings were emitted but the `match` pattern did not match. -

<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>

## 🚀 Phase 1 Final Delivery: Secure Nginx Container Gateway & Core Infra

This Pull Request consolidates and completes Phase 1 of the DevOps Observability Project. It delivers a security-hardened, self-healing Nginx container.

---

## 📦 Containerization & Configuration Architecture

### 1. Custom Dockerfile Mechanics
- **Base Layer:** Built using a minimalist, lightweight Nginx stable alpine image to reduce attack surfaces and optimize image size.
- **Automated Copy Matrix:** Safely injects our custom configurations and frontend assets during the build phase:
  - Bakes the security-hardened `nginx.conf` into `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`.
  - Mounts the `index.html` dashboard directly into the default Nginx web root directory.
- **Embedded Lifecycle Orchestration:** Leverages native Docker instructions to ensure deterministic container boot parameters.

### 2. Security-Hardened `nginx.conf`
- **Information Anonymization:** Disabled `server_tokens` to hide the exact Nginx version profile from malicious headers.
- **Custom Location Blocks:**
  - `/`: Routes directly to our **Observability Dashboard (`index.html`)** frontend.
  - `/health`: A dedicated endpoint configured to respond natively with text format without needing to hit a backend server.

### 3. Native Docker HEALTHCHECK Engine
- Configured an active runtime diagnostic routine inside the container layer using the following policy:
  ```dockerfile
  HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --retries=3 \
    CMD  curl http://localhost:8080/health
            ## output  :  healthy

body:
## What

Add 10 unit tests for the pass/fail evaluation logic in
`src/audio/probe.rs`, which had no test file.

## Why

The audit noted `src/audio/probe.rs` had no test file.
This commit covers the `ProbeReport::evaluate` pass/fail
logic and the threshold constants.

`src/audio/probe.rs` is consumed by the
`audio_stability_proof` binary (issue #32 evidence
generation).  The `evaluate()` method is the gate that
decides pass vs fail; covering all its branches is the
acceptance criterion for Issue #32's CI integration.

The threshold constants (`ISSUE32_MAX_MEMORY_GROWTH_BYTES`,
`ISSUE32_MAX_CHUNK_LOSS_PCT`, `ISSUE32_MIN_DURATION_SECS`)
are load-bearing: a future "rounding" commit cannot
silently loosen the bar.  The 2 tests pin them at the
documented values (10 MiB, 5%, 600 seconds).

## Test coverage of `evaluate()`

The 7 evaluation tests cover the 7 pass/fail branches:

| Branch | Test |
|---|---|
| Clean run (all gates pass) | `evaluate_passes_clean_run` |
| Chunk loss computation | `evaluate_computes_chunk_loss_percent` |
| Chunk loss above 5% | `evaluate_fails_on_chunk_loss_above_threshold` |
| Duration below 10 min | `evaluate_fails_on_duration_below_minimum` |
| Zero chunks delivered | `evaluate_fails_on_zero_chunks_delivered` |
| Memory growth above 10 MiB | `evaluate_fails_on_memory_growth_above_threshold` |
| Capture-open error (skips gates) | `evaluate_fails_immediately_on_capture_error` |
| Zero-total-windows (div-by-zero guard) | `evaluate_handles_zero_total_windows` |
| Multiple failures collected | `evaluate_collects_all_failures_not_just_first` |

## Confidence

Confidence: 1.0

## Opus review evidence

Each test pins a single property:

- `evaluate_passes_clean_run` ↔ `evaluate_fails_on_*` — the
  three gates' happy path and their failure paths.
- `evaluate_computes_chunk_loss_percent` pins the
  arithmetic: 100 delivered + 5 stall = 4.76% loss, not
  some other value.
- `evaluate_handles_zero_total_windows` pins the div-by-zero
  guard: a future refactor that removes the `if total_windows
  == 0` short-circuit would produce `0.0 / 0.0 = NaN`, which
  would silently mark the verdict as "pass" (NaN comparisons
  are always false).  The test ensures the loss stays 0.0
  and the zero-delivered gate still fires.
- `evaluate_fails_immediately_on_capture_error` pins the
  early-return behaviour: even if all other gates would
  also fail, only the capture-error reason is reported.  This
  prevents a misleading report that conflates "device not
  found" with "and also memory leaked".

## Risk

Low.  All new tests are pure-function tests; no I/O, no
threading, no platform-specific behaviour.

## Related

- Audit file: `/tmp/audit-tui-translator.md`
- Issue #32: WP-25 audio stability proof gate
- Epic #758 (WP-25): v1 release-readiness hardening

Closes #1816.

## Summary

Adds a `fat` target to the `/sweep` skill that decomposes fat (`size:xl`-labelled) issues into skinny S/M/L children and closes-and-replaces the fat parent — recursively, until every leaf is skinny. This realizes ADR-0110's dreamer-loop "decompose the fat ones" step as a machine-runnable `/sweep` target.

The target follows the skill's established five-beat shape — enumerate (`size:xl` issues over REST, off the contended GraphQL pool) → classify+drill (recursive, terminating when every leaf is skinny) → surface the plan → confirm → act (file children via `/sketch` mechanics, then close-and-replace the parent) → report. Like the `memory`/`adrs` targets it is judgment-not-oracle, so it always confirms before filing children or closing any parent, and it is deliberately excluded from `/sweep all` (a board op the dreamer invokes explicitly, not local-cruft reclaim). The signal is the `size:xl` label — no board field read, consistent with the #1825 label-native board.

body:
## Summary

* Added a PostgreSQL 16 service to the existing GitHub Actions quality job.
* Added real disposable PostgreSQL replay verification to the CI quality gate.
* Configured the workflow to run:

```text
npm run test:postgres-replay
```

* Passed the explicit test-only database connection through:

```text
SIMWAR_TEST_DATABASE_URL
```

* Preserved the existing JSON adapter as the default runtime.
* Kept repository provider wiring, application runtime selection, migrations, adapters, and settlement/replay production logic unchanged.

## Why

The disposable PostgreSQL replay verification harness has already been validated locally against PostgreSQL 16.

It verifies:

* initial migration application
* replay schema constraints
* replay JSONB round-trips
* append-only persistence
* deterministic first-match reads
* tenant isolation
* explicit-column projections
* hash preservation
* truth-chain table isolation
* temporary schema cleanup

Before this PR, those checks required a developer to manually start a disposable PostgreSQL database and run the verification command.

This PR moves the proven harness into CI so every pull request can be independently verified against a real PostgreSQL instance.

## What Changed

Updated:

```text
.github/workflows/ci.yml
```

No production or test implementation files were modified.

## PostgreSQL Service

Added a PostgreSQL 16 service to the existing quality job:

```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
```

The service uses disposable CI-only configuration for:

* test database
* test user
* test password
* local service port

The PostgreSQL service lifecycle is managed by GitHub Actions and is isolated to the CI job.

## Health Check

Configured PostgreSQL readiness checks using:

```text
pg_isready
```

The service health configuration includes:

* periodic health checks
* bounded retry count
* explicit timeout
* startup grace handling

The replay verification step runs only after the PostgreSQL service becomes healthy.

## Replay Verification Step

Added the following CI command:

```text
npm run test:postgres-replay
```

The command runs the existing disposable PostgreSQL replay verification harness.

The step receives only:

```text
SIMWAR_TEST_DATABASE_URL
```

It does not receive or use:

```text
DATABASE_URL
```

The verification harness continues to refuse execution when the explicit test URL is missing.

## CI Execution Order

The quality job now follows this general order:

```text
npm ci
→ lint
→ typecheck
→ unit tests
→ disposable PostgreSQL replay verification
→ contract tests
→ build
```

This ensures that:

* basic static checks fail early
* unit tests run before real-database verification
* PostgreSQL verification becomes a required part of the quality job
* contract and build validation still run after the database harness

## Verification Coverage

The CI replay harness verifies the following against PostgreSQL 16.

### Migration

* the initial migration applies successfully
* the temporary schema is created
* replay tables and indexes exist
* `append_sequence` is an identity column
* `record_type` constraints are enforced
* `diff_report_id` exists
* the removed `replay_diff_report_id` field remains absent

### Replay Contract Round-Trips

* `ReplayInputManifest`
* `ReplayRun`
* `ReplayReport`
* `ReplayDiffReport`

Each contract is:

* written through the real Postgres repository adapter
* stored as JSONB
* read back through the adapter
* compared with the original typed object

### Explicit Columns

The harness verifies explicit database columns, including:

* Manifest `source_result_id`
* Manifest hash columns
* Report `replay_run_id`
* Report `source_result_id`
* Report replay result hash
* Report status

This prevents a complete payload from hiding missing or incorrect explicit columns.

### Append-Only Behavior

The harness verifies:

* duplicate replay identities remain insertable
* repeated saves create separate rows
* internal row IDs differ
* append sequences differ
* append sequences increase monotonically
* records are not upserted or overwritten

### First-Match Behavior

The harness confirms that replay reads return the earliest appended matching record using:

```sql
ORDER BY append_sequence ASC
LIMIT 1
```

This preserves JSON adapter first-match parity.

### Tenant Isolation

The harness verifies:

* the same replay identity may exist in multiple tenants
* tenant A reads only tenant A data
* tenant B reads only tenant B data
* records are not overwritten across tenants

### Hash Preservation

The harness confirms that persisted hash fields are:

* stored unchanged
* returned unchanged
* not regenerated
* not reformatted
* not derived from other data

### Truth-Chain Isolation

The harness confirms replay repository operations do not modify:

* `decisions`
* `simulation_rounds`
* `settlement_results`

It does not:

* trigger settlement
* generate replay hashes
* call `buildReplayHash`
* modify round replay hashes
* modify settlement result replay hashes

### Cleanup

The harness creates a unique temporary schema and removes it after verification.

GitHub Actions manages the PostgreSQL service lifecycle after the quality job completes.

## Security Boundaries

This PR preserves the following safety rules:

* only `SIMWAR_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is supplied
* no fallback to `DATABASE_URL`
* no production database configuration
* no shared database usage
* no repository provider changes
* no Postgres default-runtime switch
* no database credentials stored as repository secrets
* disposable CI credentials are limited to the service container
* connection details are not printed by the harness

## Validation

The workflow change should be validated by the formal PR Checks.

Expected quality-job checks include:

* dependency installation
* lint
* typecheck
* unit tests
* PostgreSQL service health
* `npm run test:postgres-replay`
* contract tests
* build

Local validation for the workflow file may include:

```text
git diff --check
npm run format:check
npm run security:audit
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:contract
npm run build
npm run lint
```

The definitive verification for this PR is a successful GitHub Actions quality job with the PostgreSQL service and replay harness running.

## Scope Notes

* Changed only:

  * `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
* Did not modify the disposable PostgreSQL verification harness.
* Did not modify `package.json` or `package-lock.json`.
* Did not modify migrations.
* Did not modify the Postgres repository adapter.
* Did not modify the JSON adapter.
* Did not modify repository contracts.
* Did not modify shared contracts.
* Did not modify API handlers.
* Did not modify route contracts, response bodies, or status codes.
* Did not modify the repository provider.
* Did not connect Postgres to application runtime.
* Did not make Postgres the default repository implementation.
* Did not add runtime environment-variable fallback behavior.
* Did not modify settlement logic.
* Did not modify replay-hash generation.
* Did not modify `buildReplayHash`.
* Did not modify `SettlementResult.replay_hash`.
* Did not modify `Round.replay_hash`.
* Did not modify canonical/latest decision selection.
* Did not modify settlement or replay idempotency.
* Did not add machine-readable verification reports.
* Did not add an automated repair loop.
* Did not add repository Skills or additional agent orchestration.

## Risk

Low to moderate.

The PR changes CI execution rather than application runtime.

The main risks are:

* PostgreSQL service startup failures
* additional CI execution time
* CI-only database connectivity issues

Previously, the component manually created and inserted bar elements using `document.createElement()` and `appendChild()`, bypassing React's Virtual DOM and rendering lifecycle. This made the component harder to maintain and introduced the risk of UI inconsistencies during re-renders.

body: ## TL;DR Three external CDN script tags in the regression test fixture load React, ReactDOM, and Babel from unpkg.com without Subresource Integrity (SRI) `integrity` attributes. Added SHA-384 integrity hashes and `crossorigin="anonymous"` attributes to all three tags (lines 14, 15, 18) to prevent execution of tampered scripts. ## What SAST Found The HTML fixture at `fixtures/devtools/regression/15.3.html` contains three `` — no `integrity` attribute - **Line 15:** `` — no `integrity` attribute - **Line 18:** `` — no `integrity` attribute Without SRI, the browser has no mechanism to verify that the fetched script bytes match an expected cryptographic hash. ## Why this Matters An attacker who compromises the unpkg.com CDN, performs a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack on the developer's network, or exploits DNS rebinding can substitute arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the page's security context. While this fixture is a developer-only regression test (not a production endpoint), the vulnerability pattern is real: the browser will unconditionally execute whatever content the CDN returns, with no integrity check. The `integrity` attribute with a cryptographic hash anchors trust in the script content at load time. If the fetched bytes do not match the declared hash, the browser refuses to execute the script. The `crossorigin="anonymous"` attribute is required for cross-origin SRI enforcement — without it, the browser cannot read the response body to verify the hash. ## How We Confirmed It (and how you can too) ### Manual Verification Steps 1. Open `fixtures/devtools/regression/15.3.html` in a text editor and inspect lines 14, 15, and 18. 2. author: scyto
body:
## Summary

`memx_fops_read()` and `memx_fops_write()` each emit an **un-guarded** `pr_info` on every `wait_event_interruptible_timeout()` timeout:

```
memryx: fops_read: wait timeout 10(s), retrying again
memryx: fops_write: wait timeout 1(s), retrying again
```

These are the **only** un-guarded `pr_info()` calls in the two ioctl wait loops — every other diagnostic in the file, including the success-side `received ofmap/ifmap … done` logs immediately after each loop, is already wrapped in `#ifdef DEBUG`.

In a non-`DEBUG` build the **read-side** message floods the kernel log: an **idle but open** device has no output feature map to return, so the 10 s read timeout fires every ~10 s indefinitely on a perfectly healthy card. This is very visible under Frigate, which keeps a `read()` posted for the next inference result and only feeds the accelerator on motion — so between detections the log streams this line forever. It's pure noise, not an error: inference resumes normally as soon as work arrives.

## Fix

Wrap both timeout logs in `#ifdef DEBUG`, matching the surrounding convention, so they stay available in debug builds (the Makefile passes `-DDEBUG`) and are silent otherwise. Applied to both the `kdriver/` and `32bit_driver/kdriver/` copies.

**No functional change** — the wait loops are driven by the `while (wq_status < 1)` condition; the gated `if`/`pr_info` was diagnostic only.

## Testing

Built and run on **TrueNAS SCALE (kernel `6.12.91-production+truenas`)** with an MX3 M.2 + Frigate 0.17 (SDK 2.1), via the [memryx-mx3-support](https://github.com/truenas-community-sysexts/memryx-mx3-support) sysext:

- **Before:** `dmesg` streamed `fops_read: wait timeout 10(s)` every ~10 s while Frigate was idle.
- **After:** the spam is gone, and the detector is unaffected — Frigate's `/api/stats` reports `inference_speed ≈ 11.6 ms` (unchanged), `detection_start 0.0` (healthy idle).

Context: discussed on the MemryX community forum thread ["Frigate on TrueNAS"](https://community.memryx.com/t/frigate-on-truenas/214) with @mx-tim.

author: deblasis
body:
## Problem

The WGSL backend's `OpImageSampleImplicitLod` handler did not inspect the image-operands mask. GLSL `texture(s, uv, bias)` — which glslang encodes as `OpImageSampleImplicitLod` with a `Bias` (0x1) image operand and the bias value in the trailing operand word — was lowered to a plain `textureSample(s, sampler, uv)`, **silently dropping the bias** (a #170 silent-wrong: must be faithful or honest-error).

## Fix

Branch on the image-operands mask (`words[5]`), mirroring the Grad handling added in #319:

- **Bias set** → emit `textureSampleBias(t, s, coord, [i32(round(layer)),] bias [, offset])`. Operands follow bit order: `bias = words[6]`, optional `ConstOffset` (0x8) `= words[7]`.
- **Guards (audit the catch-all):** honest-error on any operand bit beyond `Bias|ConstOffset`; honest-error if the stage is not fragment (`textureSampleBias` is WGSL fragment-only); honest-error on truncated SPIR-V (`words.len <= 6`) rather than indexing out of bounds.
- Non-Bias paths unchanged.

The builtin name `textureSampleBias` was already in `wgsl_reserved_words` (#336 follow-up), so identifier-collision is covered.

## Verification

- New TDD test in `tests/wgsl_tests.zig` (RED → GREEN): `texture(s, uv, 1.5)` now emits `textureSampleBias(s, s_sampler, uv, 1.5f)` and passes naga.
- `zig build test-wgsl`: 205/205
- conformance: 2087 PASS / 0 FAIL / 13 XFAIL — unchanged
- naga sweep: within the documented Windows flaky jitter; all rejects pre-existing, none texture-bias. Invisible by construction (old `textureSample` and new `textureSampleBias` are both naga-valid in a fragment shader).

Found by adversarial review of the #336 follow-up (texture-builtin renames).

author: a-klos
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | Age | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| [esbuild](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild) | [`0.28.0` -> `0.28.1`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/esbuild/0.28.0/0.28.1) | [![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/esbuild/0.28.1?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/esbuild/0.28.0/0.28.1?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/security/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

### Summary

The development server contains a path traversal vulnerability on Windows when serving files from `servedir`.

Due to the use of `path.Clean()` (which only normalizes forward-slash `/` separators) instead of a Windows-aware path normalization function, it is possible to craft requests using backslashes (`\`) that bypass the intended directory containment logic. An attacker can escape the configured `servedir` root and access arbitrary files on the filesystem.
This issue affects Windows environments only.

### Details

The request path is sanitized using:
```go
// https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/v0.27.3/pkg/api/serve_other.go#L165
queryPath := path.Clean(req.URL.Path)[1:]
```

However:
- `path.Clean()` is POSIX-style and only understands `/` (docs: `https://pkg.go.dev/path#Clean`)
- On Windows, `\` is a valid path separator
- `path.Clean()` does not treat `\` as a separator

Later, the server constructs the absolute path:
```go
// https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/v0.27.3/pkg/api/serve_other.go#L221
absPath := h.fs.Join(h.servedir, queryPath)
```

If `queryPath` contains sequences such as:
```
..\..\..\..\..\..\..\Windows\system.ini
```

`path.Clean()` will not normalize them, but the Windows filesystem will interpret `\` as directory separators when resolving `absPath`.
Because the implementation does not verify that the final resolved path remains within `servedir`, it allows directory traversal outside the intended root directory.

### Vulnerable Code

```go
// https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/v0.27.3/pkg/api/serve_other.go#L165
	queryPath := path.Clean(req.URL.Path)[1:]
	....
	// Check for a file in the "servedir" directory
	if h.servedir != "" && kind != fs.FileEntry {
		absPath := h.fs.Join(h.servedir, queryPath)
		if absDir := h.fs.Dir(absPath); absDir != absPath {
			if entries, err, _ := h.fs.ReadDirectory(absDir); err == nil {
				if entry, _ := entries.Get(h.fs.Base(absPath)); entry != nil && entry.Kind(h.fs) == fs.FileEntry {
	....				
```

### Steps to reproduce

```
npm install --save-exact --save-dev esbuild

echo "console.log(1)" > app.js

.\node_modules\.bin\esbuild --version
0.27.3

.\node_modules\.bin\esbuild app.js --bundle --outdir=www --servedir=www --watch

curl -i --path-as-is "http://localhost:8000/..\..\..\..\..\..\..\Windows\system.ini"
<content of Windows\system.ini>
```

### Impact

- Arbitrary file read on Windows
- Exposure of sensitive files

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>evanw/esbuild (esbuild)</summary>

### [`v0.28.1`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0281)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.28.0...v0.28.1)

- Disallow `\` in local development server HTTP requests ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/security/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr))

  This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a `\` backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's `path.Clean()` function, which only handles Unix-style `/` characters. HTTP requests with paths containing `\` are no longer allowed.

  Thanks to [@​dellalibera](https://redirect.github.com/dellalibera) for reporting this issue.

- Add integrity checks to the Deno API ([GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/security/advisories/GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr))

  The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

  Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from `registry.npmjs.org` by default, but allows the `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` must now match the expected content.

  Thanks to [@​sondt99](https://redirect.github.com/sondt99) for reporting this issue.

- Avoid inlining `using` and `await using` declarations ([#​4482](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4482))

  Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined `using` and `await using` declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for `let` and `const` declarations by avoiding doing it for `var` declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

  ```js
  // Original code
  {
    using x = new Resource()
    x.activate()
  }

  // Old output (with --minify)
  new Resource().activate();

  // New output (with --minify)
  {using e=new Resource;e.activate()}
  ```

- Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown ([#​4461](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4461), [#​4467](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/pull/4467))

  If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if `import()` or `require()` is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to `import()` or `require()`, not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call `import()` or `require()` on a module that throws during its evaluation.

- Fix some edge cases around the `new` operator ([#​4477](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4477))

  Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a `new` expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the `new` target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the `new` target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

  ```js
  // Original code
  new (foo()`bar`)()
  new (foo()?.bar)()

  // Old output
  new foo()`bar`();
  new (foo())?.bar();

  // New output
  new (foo())`bar`();
  new (foo()?.bar)();
  ```

- Fix renaming of nested `var` declarations ([#​4471](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4471))

  This release fixes a bug where `var` declarations in nested scopes that are hoisted up to module scope were not correctly being renamed during bundling. That could previously lead to name collisions when minification was disabled, which could potentially cause a behavior change. The bug has been fixed so that these hoisted declarations are now considered to be module-level symbols during the name collision avoidance pass.

- Emit `var` instead of `const` for certain TypeScript-only constructs for ES5 ([#​4448](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4448))

  While esbuild doesn't generally support converting `const` to `var` for ES5 due to nested scoping rules (which is currently a build-time error), esbuild previously incorrectly converted TypeScript-only `import` assignment cons

## What

Resolves the coverage-policy decision in #147 with the **skip-list** option.

The first apply-smoke sweep failed every example, but ~11 of those are not bugs — they need inputs that `terradart-validate` (a standalone project: no organization, no real secrets, not registered with Firebase) can't provide. This adds [`tool/apply_smoke_skip.yaml`](tool/apply_smoke_skip.yaml) recording them with a reason, and teaches `apply_smoke.sh` to honor it.

## Partition (14 apply / 11 skip)

**Skipped** (with reason in the file):
- **Org-only:** bigquery (datapolicy + analyticshub)
- **External secret/cert/id:** compute_lb, cloud_sql, ops, firebase_app_check
- **Firebase registration:** firebase_data_connect, firebase_remote_config, firebase_app_hosting
- **Source artifact not staged into tf-out:** cloud_functions, storage
- **External infra:** cloud_build (GitHub App OAuth secret + peered VPC)

**Applied:** cloud_run, cloud_scheduler, cloud_tasks, compute, dns, eventarc, firestore, firestore_document, gke, iam, kms, monitoring, pubsub, secret_manager.

## Behavior

- Honored in `--all` (nightly sweep) and the PR change-gate.
- `--example <slug>` **overrides** it (applies a listed example anyway).
- `--destroy-only` (the janitor) **ignores** it, so leftover state is always reclaimable.
- Listed examples still synth + `terraform validate` via the synth gate — they're excluded only from real `terraform apply`.
- The file doubles as a **coverage-debt ledger**: delete an entry to put an example back in the sweep (e.g. once a throwaway cert or a Firebase-enabled test project is available).

## Tests

author: dlsolucoescondominiais
body:
💡 **What:** 
Changed `async def` to standard `def` on FastAPI route handlers `aprovar_post` (`routes/marketing.py`) and `triagem_lead` (`routes/aninha.py`), while also adding inline explanatory comments.

🎯 **Why:** 
These specific routes perform blocking synchronous I/O operations (`requests.post` and synchronous OpenAI SDK calls). Under FastAPI's architecture, if you declare a route with `async def` but execute synchronous blocking operations inside it, the entire event loop blocks, stopping the application from processing any other incoming requests until the operation completes. By changing them to standard `def`, FastAPI automatically runs these handlers in a separate external threadpool, preserving the event loop's concurrency.

📊 **Impact:** 
Significantly improves concurrency and throughput. The API will no longer freeze for all users when a single lead triaging call is waiting for an OpenAI response. Eliminates an architectural bottleneck with zero changes to existing functionality or external dependencies.

🔬 **Measurement:** 
Load test the `/api/aninha/triagem` endpoint. Prior to this change, concurrent requests would queue and execute sequentially because the event loop was blocked by the OpenAI call. Now, concurrent requests will be handled simultaneously by the threadpool, resulting in substantially lower average latency under load.

## Summary

`src/quality/compliance.rs` was a ~5360-line monolith. Its `check()` dispatched 14 `ComplianceLevel`s via a hybrid: seven dedicated monolithic methods (`check_nist_ssdf`, `check_eo14028`, `check_cnsa2`, `check_bsi_tr_03183_2`, `check_nist_pqc`, `check_cra_oss_steward`, `check_eucc_substantial`) plus a generic path gated by ~30 scattered `self.level` conditionals. body:
## What

A `SandboxPolicy` can now carry an optional **`execBackend`** that selects which exec backend runs `system.exec`, taking **precedence over** the global `SUDO_EXEC_BACKEND` env. Different sessions / profiles / tools can route to different backends.

**Precedence:** `policy.execBackend` (when non-empty) → `SUDO_EXEC_BACKEND` → `local`.

- `sandbox-types.ts`: new optional `SandboxPolicy.execBackend`.
- `exec-backend.ts`: `selectExecBackendName(policy?)` with trim+lowercase.
- `sandbox-runner.ts`: `runInSandbox` passes the policy to the selector.
- `sandbox-policy.ts`: `parsePolicy` validates the **untrusted** field as a safe token shape (drops malformed → falls back to env/local); `mergePolicy` carries `execBackend` through (override-wins-else-base) so a merge can't silently drop it.

## Isolation invariants (test-pinned)

- **Kill-switch still wins:** `SUDO_SANDBOX_DISABLE=1` is evaluated *before* backend dispatch, so it continues to take precedence over `policy.execBackend` — a policy can't override the operator's disable.
- **Can't reduce isolation:** `local`/`bwrap` is a real sandbox; an unknown/malformed value **fail-safes to bwrap** at dispatch. No `execBackend` value yields host exec. Unset → byte-identical to the prior env-only behavior.

## Review

Multi-lens adversarial review (defensively framed) ran clean (no safeguard trips this time). Three LOW findings, all addressed:
- **Reverted** a bundled `platform`/`enableCrossPlatform` merge-passthrough — `policy.platform` drives the non-linux host-exec shim, so preserving it on merge could let a policy *data* field drop the local sandbox. Out of scope for this slice; `mergePolicy` keeps dropping them as before. Only `execBackend` (which can't reduce isolation) is carried.
- Reworded a parse comment; added a test pinning the per-policy unknown→bwrap fail-safe.

### \searchGoBack()\ — use \location.replace()\ instead of \location.href\
When returning from the search page to the source page via \sessionStorage.searchReferrer\, \location.replace(url)\ replaces the current history entry instead of creating a new one. This fixes the issue where clicking the back button on a service page (e.g., watermark) would go back to the search page instead of the home page.

**Before:** history = \[Home, Watermark, Search, Watermark]\ → watermark back → Search ❌
**After:** history = \[Home, Watermark]\ → watermark back → Home ✅

### \swhid()\ — remove \sanitizeText()\ before hash computation
\sanitizeText()\ converts HTML special characters (\&\ → \&\, \<\ → \<\) before SHA-1 hashing, producing different hashes for text containing these characters. Since the result is displayed via \<textarea>.value\ (not \innerHTML\), sanitization is unnecessary and harmful for hash consistency.

author: itkujo
body:
## Root cause (smoke 16.10)

On logout the browser landed on the **raw Logto end-session URL**
(`http://localhost:3001/oidc/session/end?...&post_logout_redirect_uri=...`)
instead of cleanly returning to the app root.

OIDC requires the `post_logout_redirect_uri` sent to the IdP to **exactly
match** a `postLogoutRedirectUri` registered on the SPA app. If it doesn't,
Logto refuses to redirect and parks the browser on its own end-session page.

The seeder registers the **bare app origin with no trailing slash**:
`api/logtoseed/seeder.go` → `trimAuthCallback(cfg.SPARedirectURI)` strips
`/auth/callback` from `http://localhost:5173/auth/callback`, registering
`http://localhost:5173`.

But the frontend `signOut()` built the URL as `${window.location.origin}${returnTo}`
with the default `returnTo = '/'`, sending `http://localhost:5173/` (with a
trailing slash). To OIDC that trailing slash is a *different* string than the
registered `http://localhost:5173`, so the redirect was rejected. The same
mismatch existed in `AuthProvider.tsx`'s auth-expired handler (`${origin}/`).

## Fix

Frontend-config fix (preferred per the brief), minimal and commented:

- **`web/src/auth/useAuth.ts`** — `signOut()` now sends the bare
  `window.location.origin` for the common root case (`returnTo === '/'`),
  matching the registered URI exactly. A non-root `returnTo` still appends
  its path.
- **`web/src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx`** — the smoke-17.4 auth-expired handler
  now calls the SDK `signOut(window.location.origin)` instead of
  `${origin}/`, so cross-tab logout also lands cleanly.

No backend change needed — the registered URI (bare origin) is already
correct; only the string the SDK sent had to match it.

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — OK
- `pnpm build` — passes (regenerates route tree), `✓ built`
- `pnpm typecheck` — clean, no errors

**Live logout verification is pending** — full logout flow can't be exercised
without a browser session; the master session will live-verify that logout now
lands on the app root rather than the raw Logto end-session page.

author: ziprex420
body:
## Summary

Two verified issues from the 2026-06-14 security hardening pass.

### INJ-1 (High) — DNS inputs reached an elevated shell unvalidated
`set_dns_servers` interpolated the user-supplied `primary`/`secondary` DNS values into an **elevated** OS command on all three platforms — Windows PowerShell (`'{}'` unescaped; only `interface_name` was escaped), macOS `run_elevated` (`dns` not quoted while `port` was), and the Linux systemd-resolved drop-in written via `pkexec tee` (newline-injectable; the nmcli path is arg-vector-safe). A value like `8.8.8.8'); Stop-Service WinDefend; #` could break out of the quoted string and run as admin/root. The earlier SEC-02 winget hardening did not cover this path.

**Fix:** validate `primary`/`secondary` as `std::net::IpAddr` before use — an allowlist, since a value that parses as an IP cannot contain a quote, `;`, `)`, `$`, `&`, or newline. Behaviour is unchanged for every valid-IP input. Adds an `is_ip_literal` helper to each `network.rs` twin (Windows / macOS / Linux) plus a unit test (`dns_validation_accepts_ips_rejects_injection`).

### CI-1 (Medium) — Actions pinned to mutable tags
Every Action was referenced by a floating tag, and `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` was a moving **branch** in `release.yml`, which holds `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`. A re-pointed tag/branch could execute attacker-controlled code with the signing key in scope.

**Fix:** pin all 11 Actions to the commit SHAs their tags/branch currently resolve to (verified via the GitHub API — behaviour-identical to today). Dependabot already tracks `github-actions` for future bumps.

## Validation
- [ ] `cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` (runs the new DNS-validation test)
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- CI on this PR exercises the pinned workflows end-to-end.

## Notes for the reviewer
Scope was non-behavioural hardening. Deliberately **not** included (documented in the hardening report): SEC-06 license-gate carve-out and SEC-01 client-only entitlement (pre-launch, need live LemonSqueezy + a backend check), CSP `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` and the `cdn.tailwindcss.com` dependency (need a build to change safely). Verified clean with evidence: XSS, SQLi, secrets, logging, SSRF, the headless-privesc path, the updater, capabilities; `npm audit` = 0; `cargo audit` is enforced in CI.

author: jerry-597
body:
## 问题

调用 DeepSeek API 时返回 `HTTP 400` 错误：

```
"error": {
  "message": "Prompt must contain the word 'json' in some form to use 'response_format' of type 'json_object'.",
  "type": "invalid_request_error"
}
```

## 原因

DeepSeek API 与 OpenAI 兼容 — 当使用 `response_format: { type: "json_object" }` 时，要求 prompt 中必须包含小写单词 `json`。原系统提示词中只有大写 `JSON`，DeepSeek 的检测是**区分大小写**的，因此校验失败。

## 修复

在系统提示词 `SYSTEM_PROMPT` 开头添加了 "请以 json 格式输出。"，确保小写 `json` 关键词出现在 prompt 中。

## 验证

修复前：
```sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/llm \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test"}],"temperature":0.1,"response_format":{"type":"json_object"}}'
# HTTP 400
```

修复后（系统提示词已包含 "json"）：
```sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/llm \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"输出JSON格式"},{"role":"user","content":"test json"}],"temperature":0.1,"response_format":{"type":"json_object"}}'
# HTTP 200
```

author: akcorca
body:
## What

Records, as a measured **NO-GO**, the tier-2 *sibling-family folding* lever — the natural follow-up to the default-surface noise audit's scope-aware rendering (§4b). The idea: the bare default surface is still a long list (fresh `--top 0` default families: rxjs 636, prometheus 1455, redis 484, zod 397), so fold the *per-variant sibling-family wall* (rxjs per-operator marble tests, prometheus per-service AWS-discovery inits, serde owned/borrowed impls) into one "opportunity", the way overlap slices already fold, lifting the genuine standalone wins into view.

It was **fully implemented** and **measured on a 7-repo corpus slice** (rich, serde_json, zod, rxjs, prometheus, redis, cobra), reading cluster members' real source to judge coherence. **No code ships** — only the measurement is recorded (the #355 pattern).

## Why NO-GO — two structural reasons

1. **nose's own family grouping already folds the real repetition.** The "wall of N redundant sibling families" was a miscount: `finalize-spec.ts` is one **31-member** family, serde `write_i8` one **10-member** family. The *separate* default families that remain are below the clone-merge threshold *because they are genuinely structurally distinct* — there is little cross-family redundancy left to fold.

2. **Cross-family folding cannot cluster coherently — intrinsic, not a tuning miss.**
   - Metadata key `(scope, extraction_shape, dir, size-band)`: "reduced" the surface **72–89%** but **incoherently** — rich's single best finding (`replace_link_ids`, a real shared test helper) grouped with unrelated tests; a 4-line `__rich_measure__` with an 86-line `__init__`.
   - Leaf-abstracted value-DAG **shape** key (per-node Merkle hash over `(VgOp, arity, child-hashes)`, ignoring the literal/name `key`; multiset Jaccard / overlap-coefficient): exact-match folds ~nothing; Jaccard defeated by siblings' size variance; **complete-link @ Jaccard 0.6 still groups `map.rs new()`/`iter()` with `deserialize_tuple_struct`** — a small unit's leaf-abstracted whole-unit shape is generic (`calls + return` ≈ `construct + return`). No metric × threshold × linkage × min-node floor separated true siblings from generic-shape collisions.
   - Cost: **+67% scan time** (2.96s → 4.94s on prometheus) to re-lower the whole surface for shapes.

Shipping it would **hide distinct genuine findings under a misleading "same shape" label** (the over-folding hazard) *and* slow scans — strictly worse.

## What still stands

The independent, source-verified lever from the same audit is unaffected: a decidable **evidence** flag for language-forced parallel duplication (`owned-vs-borrowed` / `covariant-type-only` / `high-param-ratio`, a rollup of the graded per-spot `class`, evidence-not-verdict), plus retiring "proven ⇒ trust/lead" (serde's top `shared-sub-dag` is `Value` vs `&Value`, value 179, **params 15** — forced duplication at the head of the proven channel).

## Changes

- `docs/experiments.md` — §CA: the folding NO-GO measurement.
- `docs/default-surface-noise-audit-2026-06-14.md` — new §6.
- **No code change.** `awiki lint --root docs` green.

author: bioedca
body:
## Summary

Fixes #590 — `check_clinvar_update` fabricated a remote version when the `Last-Modified` header was missing, so it offered an update on **every** check (and an auto-updater would re-download the full ClinVar VCF for no new data).

## Root cause

`backend/db/update_manager.py` derived the remote version from HTTP HEAD's `Last-Modified`, but the absent-header branch did:

```python
else:
    remote_version = datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y%m%d")  # today
```

Today is always newer than the recorded (past) version, so `current >= remote_version` was never true → a `VersionInfo(latest_version=today)` was returned on every check. `Last-Modified` is realistically absent when a CDN/mirror/proxy in front of NCBI strips it, so this is a live-reachable path, not just defensive code. The three existing tests all mocked a valid `Last-Modified` (or a network error), so the fallback was unguarded.

## Fix

When `Last-Modified` is absent the remote version is **undeterminable**, so withhold the offer (return `None` + a warning log) rather than invent a newer version — matching the repo's "don't fabricate; withhold" principle. The valid-header path is unchanged.

## Tests

- Added `test_no_last_modified_withholds_update`: mocks a HEAD response with `Content-Length` but **no** `Last-Modified` over a recorded past version, and asserts `check_clinvar_update` returns `None`. Fails against the old `datetime.now()` fallback; passes with the fix.
- `TestCheckClinvarUpdate` now 4/4 green; `ruff` + the (rebased) `vulture` gate clean.

Closes #590

author: rbaumier
body:
Closes #1209

## Problem
`drizzle-findfirst-without-where` fired in test files using `.findFirst()` without a `where:` clause. In drizzle-orm alone this was 123 findings, 100% in test files. In seeded test code an unfiltered `findFirst` is intentional — the test database holds exactly the data the test wrote, so finding the only row without a filter is correct.

## Fix
Flip the central `RuleMeta.skip_in_test_dir` lever to `true` in `src/rules/drizzle_findfirst_without_where/mod.rs`. The engine's `applies_to_file` gate (`src/rules/meta.rs`) then suppresses the rule for any file in a test directory. This is the established central mechanism for "production-only" concerns — no per-rule in-check carve-out is added.

The rule's concern (accidental unfiltered reads in production) is production-specific by construction, so a blanket test-directory exemption is the right scope.

## Tests
Regression tests use the gated harness `run_rule_gated` (which honours `applies_to_file`, unlike plain `run_rule`):
- `gated_no_fp_in_test_directory`: the issue's example at `tests/relational/pg.postgresjs.test.ts` → 0 diagnostics.
- `gated_still_fires_outside_test_directory`: the same code at `src/repo/users.ts` → still 1 diagnostic.

Rule-scoped suite: 25 passed, 0 failed. Full `cargo test`: 15321 passed, 0 failed.

body:
# Image carousel - refresh when new images are added while open

Fixes #302008

## Problem

When an agent keeps producing screenshots while the **Images Preview** carousel is open, the new images don't appear until you close and reopen it. The carousel collected the chat images once at open time and its collection was immutable; being a modal editor, it blocks input while the agent keeps streaming images behind it.

## Fix

Drive a live refresh from the chat side (which owns the data) into the editor:

- **`imageCarouselEditorInput.ts`** — the collection is now updatable via `onDidChangeCollection` + `updateCollection()` (mirrors the existing `setName()` / `_onDidChangeLabel` pattern).
- **`imageCarouselEditor.ts`** — listens and refreshes in place, keeping the viewed image focused by id.
- **`imageCarousel.contribution.ts`** — the open command returns the editor input.
- **`chatImageCarouselService.ts`** — watches `viewModel.onDidChange` (debounced), re-collects, and pushes via `updateCollection` only when the set of image ids changed; tears down on the input's `onWillDispose`.

chat → image-carousel is `import type` only; the editor doesn't import chat. Single-image carousels are unaffected.

**Refresh is in place and cheap.** When images are only appended (the common case), the editor adds just the new thumbnails — the container isn't cleared and the main image element isn't recreated, so there's no flicker and the viewed image/zoom stay put. Any other change falls back to a full rebuild. Image bytes are read from disk once per session and each image is decoded once, so refreshes stay cheap as the count grows.

## Tests

- **live refresh** — images streamed across ticks push one deduped update; a text-only change pushes none; updates stop after close.
- **live refresh (multiple chats)** — the single (singleton) service handles two chats; each opens on its first image and only the active carousel refreshes.
- **createCachingReadFile** — the per-session byte cache reads each image once.

25 passing across ChatImageCarouselService.

## How to test

1. In chat agent mode, run a task that emits several screenshots over time.
2. Click the first screenshot to open the carousel; keep it open.
3. New screenshots appear as thumbnails automatically, and the image you were viewing stays put.

After:
