author: tyabu12
body:
## Summary
`VoteHandler` tallied any parsed vote unconditionally, so a self-vote under
`exclude_self` (or an eliminated / hallucinated target) was counted —
flipping vote tallies and elimination outcomes (#524, observed 3× in the
first scenario-factory cycle).

**Fix (runtime drop):** a vote outside the voter's candidate list is now
excluded from `tallies`. The raw value stays in the per-voter `votes` map so
the `voteResults` event remains observable (you can still see that an agent
misbehaved). Backend-independent (Mock / Ollama / llama.cpp), fully
unit-tested.

## Why not a grammar-enumeration prevention layer
The first cut added a second layer mirroring `ChooseHandler`: a per-voter
`OutputSchema` that enumerates the candidate list for the `vote` field at the
GBNF level, so a self-vote would be structurally unreachable on-device.

The merge-gate QA (factory pipeline, real Gemma + llama.cpp on macOS) **caught
a crash** in that layer:

```
Sampler crash caught: Unexpected empty grammar stack after accepting piece: 開き (169824)
```

Running `docs/gallery/iiwake_battle_v1.yaml` (persona `開き直りマコ`), llama.cpp's
grammar sampler broke on a CJK BPE token — the engine.md "empty grammar stack"
crash class. It is **token-dependent and unpredictable** (a sibling
`word_wolf.yaml` run with pure-katakana names completed fine), so grammar
enumeration over arbitrary persona names cannot be made safe by a static
guard. The grammar layer was therefore **removed** (commit ⏪); the runtime
drop alone fully fixes #524.

## Test plan
- `dropsInvalidVotesFromTally` — regression: self-vote + hallucinated name
  dropped from tallies, raw values preserved in `votes` (fails if the fix is
  reverted)
- Full unit suite (1864 tests) green; `swiftlint --strict` clean
- Factory real-LLM QA: `word_wolf.yaml` completed `ok`; `iiwake_battle_v1.yaml`
  re-run pending to confirm it now completes with the self-vote dropped from
  the tally (grammar-crash path removed)

## Follow-up
- #599 — `choose`'s `.enumeration(options)` carries the same CJK grammar-crash
  exposure (now documented there); separate from this fix.

Closes #524

body:
## Summary

- **Bug 1 (SECURITY):** WS (`workstations.update`, `workstations.create`) and HTTP (`PUT /v1/workstations/{id}`, `POST /v1/workstations`) error handlers called `err.Error()` and embedded it in the RPC error response body. When the bytea encode failure occurred, pgx included the full `map[string]interface{}` — including `privateKey` — in the error string. gcplane logs the error response it receives, so the key appeared in plaintext logs.
  - Fix: replace `err.Error()` with `"see server logs"` on all workstation create/update error paths in both WS and HTTP handlers.

- **Bug 2 (correctness):** `json.Unmarshal` into `map[string]any` leaves `metadata` as `map[string]any`. The store `Update()` switch handles only `[]byte` / `string`, so `map[string]any` fell through with `plainBytes = nil`, skipping encryption. The raw map reached `pgDialect.TransformValue()` (identity) and pgx failed to encode it into the `bytea` column — every `workstations.update` call with metadata failed.
  - Fix: after marshaling + validating metadata in `handleUpdate` (both WS and HTTP), replace `updates["metadata"]` with the `[]byte` value before passing to the store.

## Files changed
- `internal/gateway/methods/workstations.go` — WS handler fixes
- `internal/http/workstations.go` — HTTP handler fixes

## Description

Previously, `issue_redirector.py` loaded testcases using `helpers.get_testcase(testcase_id)`, which only verified testcase existence and did not enforce access controls. As a result, unauthorized users could enumerate testcase IDs and infer the existence of security-sensitive testcases through redirect responses.

This change replaces `helpers.get_testcase(testcase_id)` with `access.check_access_and_get_testcase(testcase_id)`, ensuring that the same access checks applied by other testcase handlers are enforced by the issue redirector as well.

## Changes

* Updated `src/appengine/handlers/issue_redirector.py` to use `access.check_access_and_get_testcase(testcase_id)`.
* Updated `issue_redirector_test.py` to mock the new access-control path.
* Added test coverage for:

  * Authenticated but unauthorized users (`403 Forbidden`).
  * Unauthenticated users (redirect to `/login`).
* Added local NDB context setup/teardown required for the updated tests.

## Verification

Executed the issue redirector unit tests:

```bash
python butler.py py_unittest -t appengine -p issue_redirector_test.py
```

All tests passed successfully, including the newly added access-control test cases.

author: jgyy
body:
## Problem

When a wild mob is pulled past its leash it switches to the `evade` state (`src/sim/sim.ts`): it **drops its hate table**, walks home at `EVADE_SPEED_MULT`, and only heals to full **on arrival**. `enterCombat` explicitly refuses to re-aggro a mob in `evade`, so it will not fight back during the retreat.

However, `dealDamage` only guarded `dead` and `gm` targets — there was **no guard for `evade`**:

```ts
private dealDamage(...) {
  if (target.dead) return;
  if (target.gm) return;
  // <-- nothing stopped damage to an evading mob
```

So a player could:
- keep landing hits on a retreating mob (re-seeding its threat table with damage it never reacts to), and
- **kill it outright** before it reached home — a completely risk-free kill, since the mob never retaliates.

This also breaks the classic reset contract, where an evading mob is immune until it fully resets.

## Fix

Add an early return in `dealDamage` for mobs in the `evade` state:

```ts
if (target.kind === 'mob' && target.aiState === 'evade') return;
```

This covers both leash-broken wild mobs and pets freed to the wild (`releasePetToWild` clears `ownerId` and sets `aiState = 'evade'`). Direct hits and lingering DoT ticks now no-op until the mob resets and can be pulled again.

## Tests

Adds `tests/evade_immunity.test.ts`:
- no damage and no threat gained from a hit while evading
- cannot be killed while evading
- normal damage + threat resume once the mob is fighting again

Verified the new test **fails without** the one-line fix (2/3 cases) and **passes with** it. Full suite: 392 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean. (The unrelated `homepage_foundation` file only fails when `DATABASE_URL` is unset in the environment — pre-existing, passes with it set.)

This is independent of #153 (leash anchoring / social-pull tuning), which does not address damage immunity during `evade`.

author: rbaumier
body:
Closes #1200

## Problem
`drizzle-multi-statement-tx` fired on sequential `db.insert`/`db.update`/`db.delete` calls in **test files** (697 findings in drizzle-orm, 100% in `.test.ts`/`.spec.ts`/`tests/`). Test code intentionally seeds data with sequential mutations and manages isolation via rollback fixtures / truncation — a transaction wrapper adds nothing there.

## Root cause / fix
The rule's concern is production transaction safety, which does not apply to test code. Flipped the central `RuleMeta.skip_in_test_dir` lever from `false` to `true` in `src/rules/drizzle_multi_statement_tx/mod.rs`. The engine's `applies_to_file` (`src/rules/meta.rs`) skips the rule for any file in a test directory. No per-rule in-check carve-out — this uses the established central mechanism.

## Tests
Added gated regression tests using `run_rule_gated` (which applies the production gate) with the issue's exact sequential-`db.insert` example:
- `skips_test_directory`: `tests/relational/pg.postgresjs.test.ts` -> 0 diagnostics.
- `still_fires_in_production_code`: same source at `src/repo/users.ts` -> still fires (rule intact for prod).

RED established pre-flip (positive test failed with `skip_in_test_dir: false`). Scoped suite and full `cargo test` pass (0 failed).

author: jainapurva
body:
## Problem
After #315 each chat tab is its own DB conversation, but **sending** was still globally single-flighted: a `useRef(false)` `askingRef` and a global `busy` flag meant while one tab's ask was in flight, no other tab could send.

## Fix
Per-tab in-flight + busy state, extracted into `lib/chatAskState.ts` (mirrors #315's `chatPersistence.ts`) so the shipped concurrency logic is unit-tested:
- `askingTabsRef: Set<string>` — authoritative per-tab double-send guard (a tab with an ask in flight can't start a second; other tabs are free → they run concurrently).
- `busyTabs: Set<string>` (React state, immutable updates) — drives composer busy. The composer reads `isComposerBusy(busyTabs, activeTabId)` so it reflects only the ACTIVE tab; switching to an idle tab shows an enabled composer while another tab still loads.
- `runTabAsk(...)` runs the ask, routes the reply/error to the captured `targetTabId`, and clears state in `finally` (safe if the tab was closed mid-flight). `submitAsk` calls it after resolving `targetTabId` and appending the user turn.

All #315 persistence, thread routing, error handling, tab open/close, and localStorage preserved.

## Tests (`ChatScreen.concurrent-asks.test.tsx`, 10 — exercise the real `runTabAsk`)
Two tabs with concurrent in-flight asks (B not blocked by A); per-tab double-send guard; replies route to their own tab (no cross-routing); active-tab busy derivation flips on switch; cleanup on resolve AND error; no-throw when a tab is closed mid-flight; Set-helper units.

Full web suite **1127 passed**; production build clean.

author: cacarlt
body:
## Why the proxy went down tonight

The single-file bind `(/opt/minecraft/secrets/velocity_forwarding_secret → /server/forwarding.secret)` was being **shadowed** by the broader `/data/minecraft/velocity:/server` parent bind at container start (Linux mount semantics: parent mounted after child wipes out the child's contents). Velocity ended up reading whatever happened to sit at `/data/minecraft/velocity/forwarding.secret` on the host — which itzg's startup helpfully fills with a random secret when it's absent.

That bug was latent until #152 (MOTD bump) made `refresh-env.sh` detect a `velocity.toml` diff and trigger `docker compose restart velocity`. The "legacy cleanup" block in `refresh-env.sh` had been deleting `/data/minecraft/velocity/forwarding.secret` on every run; on the first restart after that deletion, itzg generated a fresh random secret, the C2E2 backend rejected the modern-forwarding HMAC, and every player got:

```
[connected player] camcast: disconnected while connecting to c2e2: Unable to verify player details.
```

## What this PR changes

**`docker/azure/refresh-env.sh`**
- Writes the KV value directly to `/data/minecraft/velocity/forwarding.secret` (the path Velocity actually reads via the directory bind). Mode `0400`, UID `1000:1000` so itzg's `chown -R` is a same-owner no-op.
- `write_secret` is now path-agnostic (`mktemp -p $(dirname "$dest")`), so the same atomic-write helper handles both `/opt/minecraft/secrets/ts_authkey` and `/data/minecraft/velocity/forwarding.secret`.
- `forwarding.secret` and `velocity.toml` changes both flow into a single `VELOCITY_RESTART_REASONS` list — at most one `docker compose restart velocity` per run regardless of which (or both) changed.
- The "legacy" cleanup now removes the **stale `/opt/minecraft/secrets/velocity_forwarding_secret`** (no longer consumed) instead of `/data/minecraft/velocity/forwarding.secret` (the live file).
- Header + rotation-procedure comments updated.

**`docker/azure/docker-compose.yml`**
- Drops the shadowed single-file bind from the velocity service.
- Comments now spell out the mount-shadowing trap so we don't reintroduce it.

## Verification

- ✅ Hotfix already applied on prod by writing the KV value to the data-dir path and restarting velocity. All three locations (host `/opt/minecraft/secrets/…`, host `/data/minecraft/velocity/…`, container `/server/forwarding.secret`) report sha `a38106fc…`.
- ✅ Velocity is `running healthy`, listening on `25577`, external TCP test against `mc.negativezone.cc:25565` succeeds.
- ✅ `bash -n` + `docker compose config` both pass locally on the modified files.

## Post-merge behavior

When this merges and `deploy-azure.yml` runs:
1. `refresh-env.sh` will see `forwarding.secret` content unchanged → no restart from secret block.
2. `velocity.toml` unchanged → no restart from toml block.
3. `docker compose up -d` will detect the volume-list change → recreate velocity once, briefly (<10s) interrupting players. New container reads the same correct secret.
4. The stale `/opt/minecraft/secrets/velocity_forwarding_secret` gets cleaned up by the updated legacy block.

## Rotation procedure going forward

Same as before but step 4 simplifies — just run `refresh-env.sh` and it auto-detects the change and restarts velocity (no separate `up -d --force-recreate` needed).

author: jeangtpr
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes critical deployment failures on Railway caused by Node.js version incompatibility with Supabase SDK and missing TypeScript configuration. The changes ensure builds pass consistently between local development and production environments.

## Key Changes

### 1. **Node.js Version Requirement (22+)**
- Updated `nixpacks.toml` to use `nodejs_22` instead of `nodejs-18_x`
- Added `engines.node = ">=22"` to `package.json`
- **Reason:** Supabase SDK requires native `WebSocket` support, which Node 20 lacks. This causes `createClient()` to crash during boot before the server starts, leading to health check timeouts.

### 2. **Lazy Supabase Client Initialization**
- Added `getSupabase()` function in `src/config/supabase.ts` that creates the client on first call instead of at import time
- **Reason:** Prevents boot crashes if runtime dependencies are missing; allows graceful error handling before `app.listen()`

### 3. **TypeScript Configuration for Isomorphic SDKs**
- Added `"DOM"` to `compilerOptions.lib` in `tsconfig.json` (alongside `"ES2022"`)
- Kept `skipLibCheck: true` to prevent false positives from third-party type definitions
- **Reason:** Supabase SDK references DOM APIs (`BroadcastChannel`, `Storage`, `WebSocket`) that aren't recognized without DOM types, causing build failures on Railway despite passing locally

### 4. **Dependencies vs DevDependencies Clarification**
- Moved `typescript`, `tsx`, and `@types/*` packages from `devDependencies` to `dependencies`
- Kept dev-only tools (eslint, prettier) in `devDependencies`
- **Reason:** Railway sets `NODE_ENV=production` during build, which skips `devDependencies`. This caused `tsc` to fail with hundreds of "Cannot find module" errors.

### 5. **Documentation & Checklists**
- Added comprehensive troubleshooting section for build failures with specific Railway scenarios
- Updated pre-deploy checklist with Node version, DOM types, and config verification steps
- Added warning about verifying config files on GitHub after push (sandbox file mount issues)
- Added new "Restart Loop" cause: boot crashes from missing WebSocket support

## Notable Implementation Details

- The lazy Supabase init pattern prevents top-level errors from blocking server startup
- GitHub verification step added because sandbox editors sometimes truncate/corrupt files during push
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing code; only configuration and initialization patterns change
- Updated date stamps to reflect current maintenance cycle

author: ylohnitram
body:
## What

Three non-blocking v1 follow-ups flagged in the [#1016 QA note](https://github.com/Replikanti/agentis-colonies/pull/1016) (v1 of #1014). All in the dispatch shell + docs — **`coordinator.ag` (the decider) and the decision policy are unchanged**.

| # | Fix | Kind |
|---|-----|------|
| 1 | `run-coordinator.sh` dispatch dropped a hunt's class | **bug** |
| 2 | stub fixture's `\|`-split glob collides with a full-cell glob | doc |
| 3 | `README.md` `##/###` heading blank-line spacing (MD022) | doc |

### 1 — hunt args parse (the real bug)

The dispatch loop parsed the coordinator's `ACTION|<type>|<args>|<rationale>` line with a flat `cut -f3`/`-f4-`. A **hunt**'s `<args>` is two `|`-fields (`subsystem|class`) where every other action's is one (`cand-id`, or empty). So `cut -f3` kept only `subsystem`, the `class` leaked into the logged rationale, and the queued PENDING candidate id was built malformed as `cand-N|subsystem` instead of the documented `cand-N|subsystem|class`.

Fix: type-aware parse — for `hunt`, args = fields 3-4 and rationale = 5-; all other action types unchanged. Mirrors the field shape `demo-coordinator.sh`'s `expect` helper already documents.

### 2 — stub fixture glob

`stub_outcome()` splits each fixture rule on `|` into `type|glob|outcome`, so a glob containing a literal `|` (a full `subsystem|class` cell) is mis-split. Documented the rule in the `--fixture` header block + the `stub_outcome` comment: use a subsystem-prefix glob (`vault*`) whose trailing `*` spans the `|class` suffix.

### 3 — README spacing

Blank line inserted before four `##/###` headings.

## Verification

- **Isolated parse test** — a `hunt` line yields `args=[vault accounting|C1]` with a clean rationale and a well-formed `cand-1|vault accounting|C1` id; refute/stop unchanged.
- **End-to-end stub run** (`--executor stub --backend mock`) — decision trace shows `step=0 action=hunt args=reentrancy|C8` (full cell, no leaked class) and the next step refutes the resulting `cand-0`.
- `demo-coordinator.sh` (offline coordinator demo) still **PASSes** (it asserts the full `ACTION|hunt|vault accounting|C1|...` shape).
- `colony-lint.sh` → **364 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped**.
- `dark-factory/CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased] → Fixed` entry added.

## Scope

Part of #1014; this does **NOT** close the epic — the v2 event-driven substrate dispatch remains open.

body:
Addresses the **Phase 5** section of the "Equinox Bugs" playtest doc. Landing incrementally on one branch; commits are scoped per item.

## Shipped so far

### Scrap desync — TOP PRIORITY (`c255915`)
> "flew into scrap … a huge spike in corrections … there is a desync."

Root cause: the client spawned each scrap fragment as a **locked** predWorld body (infinite mass — `World.lockBody`'s own docstring: *"other bodies bounce off it as if it had infinite mass"*) while the server runs scrap **dynamic at mass 1** (`SwarmSpawner` → `staticBody: false`). The local player's prediction bounced off an immovable wall while the server let the ship shove the light debris aside → every snapshot reconciled the divergence as a correction spike (worse than drone-ram because the mass gap is 1-vs-∞).

Fix: make scrap **drone-like, not asteroid-like** — `EntityKindRegistry` scrap descriptor is now `interpolated`; `scrapClientLeaf` spawns an **unlocked** mass-1 body and no longer reposes in `onSync`; `updateMirror`'s kinematic follower and `swarmSpriteUpdater`'s pose path both include kind 3, so the body follows the single interpolated pose (render == collision) and the predicted deflection matches the server.

Test-first (invariant #13): `scrapClientLeaf.test.ts` drives the local ship into a scrap fragment in the real predWorld and asserts it is shoved (was `moved=0` on the locked code).

### Laser damage falloff is LINEAR, not reverse-square (`0d6633c`)
> "the laser beam falloff should be linear not reverse square."

`hitscanFalloffFrac` now interpolates `1 − (1 − minDamageFrac)·t` over the optimal→max band. Server-authoritative damage; no wire change. `hitscanFalloff.test.ts` + core CLAUDE.md updated.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

SQLite echoes a duplicate trigger's name **exactly as written in the source**, preserving its quoting form:

| CREATE TRIGGER form | sqlite3 3.51.0 error |
|---|---|
| `tr1` (unquoted) | `trigger tr1 already exists` |
| `"tr1"` (double-quote) | `trigger "tr1" already exists` |
| `[tr1]` (bracket) | `trigger [tr1] already exists` |
| `` `tr1` `` (backtick) | `trigger \`tr1\` already exists` |

(verified against sqlite3 3.51.0 directly). VibeSQL strips delimiters during tokenization, so the bare-name fix from #5526 emitted the unquoted name for every form, failing `trigger1-1.2.2` and `trigger1-1.2.3`.

## How the source-token form is preserved

The token stream collapses `"x"`, `[x]`, and `` `x` `` into a single de-quoted `DelimitedIdentifier(String)`, so the original delimiters are gone by parse time. Rather than refactor that widely-matched token variant, the verbatim spelling is recovered via byte spans:

- **Parser** now optionally retains the original SQL plus per-token byte spans (`Parser::new_with_source`, fed by the existing `Lexer::tokenize_with_spans`). `Parser::new(tokens)` is unchanged and degrades gracefully (no source -> normalized name).
- **`CreateTriggerStmt::name_source: Option<String>`** (new AST field) carries the trigger name token's exact source text — including its quotes/brackets/backticks — captured in the trigger parser. `trigger_name` still holds the normalized identifier used for catalog lookups.
- **Error site** (`TriggerExecutor::create_trigger_with_sql`) now raises `TriggerAlreadyExists(name_source)` for a bare duplicate `CREATE TRIGGER`, falling back to the normalized name when `name_source` is absent (programmatically-built ASTs). The existing-trigger check is resolved before target validation, matching SQLite's ordering.
- **TCL shim**: VibeSQL emits `Trigger '<echoed>' already exists` where `<echoed>` already carries the original delimiters; the shim simply lowercases the wrapper and passes the name through (comment updated; the "known gap" note removed).

## sqlite3 parity per quoting form

End-to-end parse->execute executor test asserts the raw VibeSQL message for each form:

- unquoted -> `Trigger 'tr1' already exists` -> shim -> `trigger tr1 already exists`
- double-quote -> `Trigger '"tr1"' already exists` -> shim -> `trigger "tr1" already exists`
- bracket -> `Trigger '[tr1]' already exists` -> shim -> `trigger [tr1] already exists`

Parser tests assert `name_source` captures `tr1` / `"tr1"` / `[tr1]` / `` `tr1` `` while `trigger_name` stays normalized.

## trigger1.test delta (clean runs, sqlite3 3.51.0 reference)

- Baseline (origin/main): **41** failures, including `trigger1-1.2.2` and `trigger1-1.2.3`.
- With this PR: **39** failures; **1.2.2 and 1.2.3 now pass**, no new failures.

## No #5526/#5469 regression

`trigger1-1.2.1` (`trigger tr1 already exists`) is absent from the failure set both before and after — the unquoted case is unaffected. Other already-exists errors (table/index/etc.) are untouched.

## Notes / follow-ons

- The remaining 39 trigger1 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (TEMP-trigger cross-connection state, datatype-mismatch, single-quoted-identifier parsing in `CREATE TRIGGER 'name'` for `trigger1-8.x`, SELECT-result mismatches).
- **Table/index already-exists wording**: the TCL shim lowercases + re-quotes those names rather than echoing source quoting (`scripts/tester_vibesql.tcl` table/index branches use `string tolower`). If SQLite is later found to preserve source quoting there too, the same `name_source` mechanism can be extended via byte spans — worth a follow-on issue if a conformance test surfaces it.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vibesql-parser` (incl. 4 new `name_source` tests) green
- [x] `cargo test -p vibesql-executor` (incl. new duplicate-echo test; 68 trigger tests) green
- [x] `cargo build --release` (AST field addition) green
- [x] `make test-tcl-file FILE=trigger1.test`: 1.2.2 + 1.2.3 pass, 1.2.1 still passes, 41 -> 39 failures

First, safe-and-verifiable slice of the full codebase audit. Every change here keeps `tsc --noEmit` at **0 errors** and the production build green; nothing alters runtime data flow. The deeper items (removing `service_role` from the browser bundle, RLS policies, Edge Functions, the Logs/Settings features) require the live Supabase backend and are documented as a roadmap in `SECURITY.md` rather than half-implemented here.

### What changed

  ```
  console.log/.debug → logger.debug
  console.info       → logger.info
  console.warn       → logger.warn
  console.error      → logger.error
  ```
  In the prod bundle `logger.debug(...)` compiles out entirely (`if(false) ...`). Remaining `console.*` strings in `dist` come from third-party deps (React/supabase-js), not app code.
- **Dead code.** Removed the `excelExportPro.ts` re-export shim and repointed its 3 importers straight at `excelExport` (e.g. `import { exportToExcel as exportToExcelPro } from '@/utils/excelExport'`).

author: h4x3rotab
body:
Two small leftovers from the #7 cleanup list.

The session store used to scan the whole id map on every write (`by_id.retain`, O(n) per request) to drop expired entries, in both the in-memory and JSONL stores. This factors a shared `SessionIndex` that keeps the id→session map alongside a `BTreeMap<expires_at, ids>`, so a write pops only the buckets that actually expired (O(k)). It also de-duplicates the get/list/evict logic that was copy-pasted across the two stores.

The one subtlety: sessions are content-addressed, so the same channel is re-put with a later `expires_at` on every request. The index drops the superseded expiry hint on refresh, otherwise eviction at the old deadline would remove a still-live session. A new test (`refreshed_session_survives_its_old_deadline`) guards that.

Also deletes the unused `ChannelBinding::origin()`.

227 tests pass, clippy + fmt clean.

author: devresponse
body:
## The problem

`pnpm test` (parallel) failed intermittently on **random** files — whole files red, passing in isolation. The old config's own comment conceded it and worked around it by forcing **CI single-worker**, leaving local runs flaky and untrustworthy as a signal.

## Root cause (diagnosed, not guessed)

Inside a **single** Vitest process, the SSR module runner instantiates our heavy graph (Better Auth + Kysely + pg + next-intl) per isolated file, and the **shared Vite transform server races under any in-process concurrency**. A module's named export reads back as `undefined`:

```
TypeError: (0 , __vite_ssr_import_6__.getServerEnv) is not a function
```

Confirmed it is **not** a code cycle (`@/lib/env` imports only `zod`), the corrupted transform is **cached** (so test `retry` can't recover it), and it reproduces at low concurrency. Measured:

| Config | Result over N runs |
| --- | --- |
| default (≈19 workers) | flaky (random file failures) |
| `maxWorkers: 4` | **3/4 runs failed** |
| `maxWorkers: 4 + retry: 2` | **6/8 runs failed** (retries fire but re-hit the cached-corrupt module) |
| **single-worker per process** | deterministic |

## The fix

Remove concurrency **inside** a process; restore it **across** processes (each gets its own transform server → nothing to race).

- **`vitest.config.ts`** — `maxWorkers/minWorkers = 1` unconditionally (dropped the `process.env.CI` special-case); raised `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout`.
- **`scripts/test-shards.mjs`** — runs N independent `vitest run --shard=i/N` processes in parallel, scaling shards to the box (one ≈ serial on tiny runners). Buffers output, prints a per-shard summary, dumps any failed shard's full log, exits non-zero on any failure.
- **`package.json`** — `test` → the shard runner; new `test:serial` → plain single-process vitest.

## Validation

- **`pnpm test`** (6 shards): **8/8 consecutive runs green**, ~25s (vs ~100s serial), all **694** tests, no files dropped.
- **`pnpm test:coverage`** (the actual CI gate, single-process): green, **694 tests**, coverage **41.2 / 40.3 / 38.8 / 41.3** — above the `38 / 36 / 34 / 38` thresholds.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` clean.

## Reviewer notes

- **CI is unchanged in behavior** — `ci.yml` already ran `pnpm test:coverage` (single process), which is now deterministic by config rather than by the `CI` env flag. No workflow edit needed.
- Determinism does **not** depend on shard count — only wall-clock does — so small CI boxes safely fall back to fewer shards (or one).
- The single-process sub-scripts (`test:unit`, `test:integration`, …) are now single-worker too: deterministic, slightly slower; the fast path is `pnpm test`.

author: nickbock
body:
Fixes #1309

## Problem

On a device that exposes multiple `/dev/input/event*` nodes, the injector could grab and start its read loop on the *wrong* node, so the mapped button never produced any output. Observed with a **SteelSeries Aerox 9 Wireless**: the mapped button emits on one event node, but the injector read from a different one and nothing was injected. A single-interface device (e.g. a plain keyboard) was unaffected.

## Root cause

Device selection in `Injector` keyed everything on `get_device_hash()`, which is `md5(str(capabilities) + name)`. Two issues:

1. **Hash collisions.** That hash is **not unique per devnode**. Some hardware (the Aerox 9 among them) exposes several event nodes with byte-identical capabilities *and* name, so they produce the **same** `origin_hash`. `_find_input_device` built `devices_by_hash = {hash: device}` and `_grab_devices` returned `{hash: device}` — both collapse colliding nodes to a single entry, so only one twin was grabbed/read. If the event is emitted on the other twin, it is silently missed.

2. **Over-strict capability gate.** `_find_input_device` additionally required the mapped `code` to be present in the node's advertised capabilities. Nodes that emit codes outside their static capabilities had their valid `origin_hash` discarded, and `_update_preset` then overwrote it via the device-type fallback — pointing the injector at a different node.

## Fix

- Replace `_find_input_device` with `_find_input_devices`, returning **every** devnode whose hash matches the `origin_hash` (and dropping the capability gate — a matching hash already guarantees identical capabilities to recording time, so the recorded node is authoritative).
- Key `_grab_devices` by **path** instead of hash, so colliding nodes are all grabbed.
- Start **one read loop per devnode** in `run()`. Forwarding devices stay keyed by hash (one per unique hash; colliding nodes are interchangeable for forwarding).

When `origin_hash` is absent or matches nothing (old presets / configs moved between machines), behavior is unchanged: the existing `_find_input_device_fallback` still runs.

## Tests

Adds two regression tests in `tests/unit/test_injector.py`:
- `test_grabs_all_nodes_sharing_an_origin_hash` — two hash-identical nodes are both grabbed (the Aerox 9 case).
- `test_reads_from_origin_hash_node_on_multi_interface_device` — a node that under-reports the mapped code in its capabilities is still honored, not overwritten by the fallback.

Both fail on `main` and pass with the fix. `test_injector.py`, `test_event_pipeline`, `test_groups`, `test_event_reader` and `test_context` pass (the two pre-existing subprocess-spawning failures in `test_injector` fail identically on `main` and are unrelated to this change).

Verified live on the affected SteelSeries Aerox 9 Wireless: the mapped button now works.

[Fandhe-AI/template-frontend-react_router#14](https://github.com/Fandhe-AI/template-frontend-react_router/pull/14) を参考に、本リポジトリの CI を調整しました。PR #14 の `ci.yml` は frontend テンプレート向け（pnpm / Playwright / Storybook ビルド系）で本リポジトリには適用対象がないため除外し、該当する `update-external.yml` を更新しています。

- **`update-external.yml` の両ジョブ（submodule / skills）を `runs-on: self-hosted` → `ubuntu-latest` へ変更**
- **`Fandhe-AI/actions` の参照を最新へ更新**: `submodule-update` / `skills-update` を `b506f30f`（#6）→ `c80ff94f`（#8・PR #14 と同一）

PR #14 はトークンを `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` から **GitHub App トークン**（`actions/create-github-app-token` + `vars.AUTOMATION_APP_ID` / `secrets.AUTOMATION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`）へ切り替えています。本リポジトリは現状 `secrets.SUBMODULE_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` で、PAT が設定されていれば CI 発火問題を回避できるため今回は変更していません。App トークン方式へ揃える場合は別途対応可能です。

author: wegamekinglc
body:
## Summary

Implements Phases 1-3, 5 of the PTIRDS single-currency curve extension plan (`docs/experimental/replicate-ptirds-single-currency-curve.md`), respecting the locked API design (`.claude/designs/`) and critic decisions R1-R5 / blocking findings B1-B3.

- New `DiscountLogDF_` curve (`dal/curve/yclogdf.{hpp,cpp}`): discount curve parameterized by `(nodeDates, logDF, DayBasis_, Handle_<Interp1_>)`.
- New `LogDfScheme_` enum (`LOG_LINEAR`, `LOG_CUBIC_NATURAL`, `MIXED`) selects the on-log-DF interpolator inside `BuildDiscountCurve`'s `LOG_DISCOUNT` branch.
- New `MixedSchemeSpec_` + `NewMixedLogDF` composite interpolator (`dal/math/interp/interpmixed.{hpp,cpp}`).
- Wire `LOG_DISCOUNT` end-to-end in `calibration.{hpp,cpp}`: `ParamsPerKnot` returns 1, anchor excluded from unknowns, validation relaxed (`>=` only for LOG_DISCOUNT), per-node seed (`initialGuessPerNode_`, flat-2% default), weights metric dimension-matched, post-solve DF validation on free knots only.
- Machinist-generated files committed (`MG_LogDfScheme_enum.*`, `MG_DiscountLogDF_v1_*`).
- Deliverable acceptance test `dal-cpp/tests/curve/test_ptirds_curve.cpp` (suite `PTIRDSCurveTest`) asserts all three schemes against the authoritative rateslib Table 6.2 three-column reference.

## Empirical resolutions of design open questions

- **S3 (1-business-day swap):** Works with `maturity = 2022-01-03` once leg conventions use `BizDayConvention_("Unadjusted")`. `Following` rolls Sat 2022-01-01 → Mon 2022-01-03 == maturity, zeroing the annuity. The original 2022-01-02-vs-2022-01-02 question is moot — the real issue was weekend rolling under `Holidays::None()`.
- **S2 (one or three §2.5 columns?):** THREE columns. The schemes do NOT agree at nodes within 1e-6. Log-linear matches §2.5 within 5.2e-7; log-cubic-natural drifts by up to 1.0e-4 at the 10Y node; mixed by up to 9.1e-5. The off-node interpolator changes the long-end swap Jacobian columns, so node DFs genuinely differ across schemes. The plan doc §2.5 has been corrected to carry the three-column rateslib reference (PR #100).
- **B3 (conditioning):** `||J⁻¹||_inf ≈ 1.1e-9` on the tolerance-scaled Jacobian — well-conditioned, no rank deficiency.

## Test plan

- [x] `dal_cpp_tests` full suite (681 tests) passes with zero regressions
- [x] `PTIRDSCurveTest.*` (3 deliverable tests): log-linear / log-cubic-natural / mixed solved node DFs each match the authoritative rateslib Table 6.2 three-column reference within 1e-6, with per-instrument repricing residuals ~2.6e-12
- [x] Mixed matches log-linear exactly through 2025-01-01 and diverges only at the 2027/2029/2032 nodes (the structural invariant from rateslib's `t` knot sequence)

## Deferred

- The standalone `examples/ptirds_single_currency_curve/` demo program from plan §6 — not created; the calibration + three-scheme solve + DF readback are fully covered by `test_ptirds_curve.cpp`, so the example is demonstration-only and can follow up if wanted.
- Phase 6 (AAD analytic Jacobian) and Phase 7 (public API + pybind11) — explicitly out of scope per task.
- BSpline1_ (design §3.2 Step 2 fallback) — not triggered; natural cubic is the documented scheme-2 choice.

author: ly-wang19
body:
# Description

`DashScopeParse._create_job` is `async`, but before the async `add_file` POST it opened the file, requested the upload lease (a **blocking** `httpx.Client` request inside `__upload_lease`), and uploaded the file — all synchronously on the event loop. So `await`ing it (via `aload_data` / `aget_json`) stalled the loop for the entire lease + upload.

This extracts the file open + lease + upload into a sync helper (`_upload_file_with_lease`) and runs it via `asyncio.to_thread`. The async `add_file` request then runs as before using the returned lease, and the file handle no longer stays open across the async POST. Behavior is unchanged.

Found by a static sweep for blocking IO reachable from `async` paths.

Fixes # (no tracking issue)

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

- [x] Yes — `llama-index-readers-dashscope` 0.5.0 → 0.5.1

`test_upload_file_with_lease_runs_blocking_upload` covers the extracted helper, and `test_create_job_offloads_blocking_upload` asserts `_create_job` routes the blocking work through `asyncio.to_thread`. Suite passes (3 passed); `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

author: bykoleksii-hardo
body:
Improves Google ranking potential for the site and the Knowledge Hub publications. Content quality was already strong; these changes close the technical-SEO gaps that gate rich results, crawl/index efficiency, and Core Web Vitals.

## Structured data (rich results)
- Enriched **Article** JSON-LD: `image`, `dateModified`, `mainEntityOfPage`/`url`, `publisher` w/ logo, `wordCount`, `inLanguage` (was headline/desc/date only).
- **BreadcrumbList** on articles and the hub.
- **Organization** + **WebSite** on the homepage.
- **FAQPage** on the homepage (sourced from shared `faq-data` so schema always matches the rendered FAQ).
- **CollectionPage**/**ItemList** on the Knowledge Hub.
- New `lib/seo.ts` (single source of truth + builders) and `<JsonLd>` (escapes `<` to prevent script breakout from DB content).

## Crawl & index hygiene
- Single `SITE_URL` source of truth (sitemap, robots, `metadataBase`).
- Sitemap `lastModified` now uses article `updated_at`; honest hub/home dates; dropped thin `/login` + `/signup`.
- `robots`: disallow gated `/vault` and `/auth`.
- Hub canonical consolidates `?category=` filtered views to `/knowledge`.
- Markdown body headings clamped to `<h2>`+ so the page `<h1>` stays unique.

## Internal linking & discoverability
- "Keep reading" related-articles block on each article (same-category first) — internal links + topical clustering.
- `/llms.txt` guide for AI crawlers (AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity).
- `/knowledge/feed.xml` RSS feed, linked from the hub.

## Performance / Core Web Vitals
- Knowledge pages were `force-dynamic` only because the shared header needed auth state; the article body is identical for everyone.
- Moved header personalization to a client island (`<HeaderAuth>` + `/api/viewer`); reads the anonymous variant server-side (correct for crawlers/logged-out visitors) and hydrates signed-in/paid/admin chrome client-side (no hydration mismatch).
- New cookieless `getSupabaseStatic()` for public, published-only reads, so cached routes stay statically renderable.
- `/knowledge/[slug]`: `force-dynamic` → `revalidate=3600` + `generateStaticParams` (ISR via Cloudflare KV).
- Bonus: `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt`, and the RSS feed are now statically cached (1h) instead of dynamic.

### Behavioral note
On cached article/hub pages a logged-in user briefly sees the anonymous header before it hydrates to their signed-in state. Logged-out visitors and crawlers (the SEO audience) get the correct static HTML immediately.

## Verification
`tsc --noEmit` ✓ · vitest 15/15 ✓ · eslint (no new errors) ✓ · `next build` ✓ — build confirms `/knowledge/[slug]` is now ISR and sitemap/llms/feed are statically cached.

Signal-definition picker in the **Layers** popover; per-farm observation fan-out → `buildSignalOverlay` FC on the map; reuse `SignalObservationPanel` for the popup (URL `?signal_obs=`).

author: vivekkhimani
body:
Hardens the two CI gaps that let `agentic-fs-worker` silently sit on a stale image for hours (the bug the background agent caught):

1. **Loud roll.** `image.yml`'s roll steps swallowed `get-function` failures with `>/dev/null 2>&1`, so an **AccessDenied** (the CD role lacked permission on the worker) looked identical to "function not created yet" → it skipped the roll while reporting success. Now anything other than `ResourceNotFoundException` **fails the job loudly**.
2. **ci-roles visibility** (your #32 observation — it didn't show in the plan comment). `terraform.yml` only plans/applies `examples/quickstart`. Added a **read-only PR plan job for `global/ci-roles`** that comments its diff with a **⚠️ MANUAL-APPLY** banner *only when that root changes* — so a ci-roles change can't merge invisibly and sit un-applied. The root stays manual-apply **by design** (`DenyCiIdentitySelfEdit` forbids CI from mutating its own identity roles).

Dedicated PR; the ingestor-rung work continues separately.

1. **Telegram 通知・操作の保証ルール + 強制フック（最重要）**
   - rule: `capability/rules/telegram/notify-and-operability.md` — ①通知を止めない ②操作チャネルを殺さない ③ユーザーに復旧作業をさせない、の 3 つの不可侵保証。
   - hook: `aiko/hooks/enforce-telegram-reply.sh`（Stop フック、実行権限付き）— 直近の Telegram 受信に reply ツール呼び出しが無いままターンを終えようとすると block して送信を強制。fail-open 安全装置（連続 block で解除）・劣化時の自己通報・per-agent インシデントログ付き。
   - `.claude/settings.json` の `hooks.Stop` に登録（既存の PreToolUse / PostToolUse / SessionStart / SessionEnd は無改変）。
2. **その他 Telegram 挙動ルール（汎用なものだけ）**
   - `raw-output.md` / `turn-start-announcement.md` / `slash-router.md` / `voice-switching.md` / `INDEX.md`。
   - ラボ運用ログ（TUNING-LOG.md / TASKS.md）は移植せず。INDEX は移植したファイルだけを指すよう整理。
3. **誠実さ・正直さルール**
   - `capability/rules/integrity/honesty-and-candor.md` — 取り繕わない / 弱点を先に開示 / 検証なしに「できた」と言わない 等 6 つの不可侵ルール。
4. **clock-source ルール**
   - `capability/rules/clock-source.md` — 時刻はその都度 `date` で取得（キャッシュ/推論しない）。

## 何を汎用化したか

- 「マサさん/マサくん」→「ユーザー」、一人称・固有名を除去。
- ラボ固有パス（Agent-Lab / Agent-team / persona/overrides / ~/.aiko/observations 等）・特定 persona（aiko-pr / maid / hisyo / aiko-dev）・fame-strategy・健康監視/スケジュール・`[[...]]` メモリ内部リンク・固有日付/インシデントを除去（規範の実質は薄めていません）。
- **フックのチャネル汎用化**：固有 chat_id / channel のハードコードは無し。
  - envelope 検出を寛容化：公式プラグインの `source="telegram"` と、ラボの `source="plugin:telegram:telegram"` の**両形式**にマッチ（`chat_id=` の存在も併用判定）。
  - chat は受信メッセージから自動解決（`TG_GUARD_CHAT` / `AIKO_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` で上書き可）。
  - token は `TG_GUARD_TOKEN_ENV` → `~/.claude/channels/*/.env` → `~/.aiko/telegram.env` → `AIKO_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` env の順で解決（Agent-Aiko の実起動方式 `~/.aiko/telegram.env` に対応）。
  - インシデントログ出力先をラボ固有パスから汎用の `~/.claude/aiko/hooks/.telegram-reply-guard.log` に変更。

## voice-switching の扱いと理由

**除外せず、汎用主旨だけに書き換え**ました。ラボ版は CHANNEL-MAP.md による多人格ルーティング（telegram-a→aiko-pr / telegram-b→maid …）に強く依存しており、そのままでは Agent-Aiko の単一人格（origin / override / 名前付き人格）モデルで壊れます。一方で「Telegram 返信は**現在アクティブな人格**の口調で、ターミナル地の文はミニマル（読まれない前提）」という主旨は配布版でも普遍的に有用なので、人格決定を CHANNEL-MAP ではなく Aiko の `mode`（origin/override/名前付き）に読み替えて残しました。多人格専用の口調表（aiko-pr/maid/hisyo の語尾表）・issue 番号・SessionStart hook 依存・ラボパスは全削除。

## レビュー観点

- フックが Agent-Aiko の実起動（`--channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official`、envelope `source="telegram"`、token `~/.aiko/telegram.env`）と矛盾しないか。
- `hooks.Stop` 追加が既存フック（voice 等）と両立するか。本テンプレートには既存 Stop フックは無いため衝突なし。
- 汎用化で規範が薄まっていないか（固有情報の除去のみで、やること/禁止事項は維持）。

## 検証（実施済み）

- `bash -n enforce-telegram-reply.sh` → OK。埋め込み Python も `py_compile` → OK。
- `jq` で settings.json 妥当性確認 → OK。hook キーは Stop 追加のみ、既存 4 つ保持。
- フック挙動スモークテスト：非 Telegram→allow / Telegram 受信×reply 無→block / Telegram 受信×reply 成功→allow / ラボ形式 envelope→block、いずれも期待通り。
- 移植ファイル全体を固有語スキャン → 残存なし。

**この PR はマージしません。**

author: itsoso
body:
把 `/ai-assistant` 对话渲染层从「dev 工具感」提升到消费级（ChatGPT/Claude 那种干净克制）。**纯 UI/渲染层改动，不碰 streaming / agentApi / 后端 / 消息数据结构**。编辑现有组件，无新页 → 无 page-freeze。

## 改了哪些视觉

**① 工具调用 chip（最高优先，原来最丑）**
模型有时把工具调用当 markdown 文本吐出来，正文里出现裸文本如 `[tool_call: health_query(type=lab_results, days=7)]`。现在在渲染前识别该 pattern（含 `[工具调用: ...]` / `[调用工具：...]` 中文变体），切段渲染：
- 文本段照常走 `MarkdownRenderer`
- 工具调用段渲染成内联灰底圆角 pill：小图标（检索类 `Search`，其余 `Wrench`）+ 中文动作词，**不显示原始 args/JSON**
- 多个连续 tool_call 合并成一行 chips；流式进行中图标轻微 `animate-pulse`
- 没有 tool_call 文本的消息走原路径（廉价预检 `hasToolCall`），零回归风险

**② 性能脚注瘦身（原 `5.5s LLM 4.9s · 3 轮 · commercial/Claude-Opus-4.7`）**
默认只显示一个干净的模型友好名（`commercial/Claude-Opus-4.7` → `Claude Opus`，去前缀 + 补丁版本号）。耗时/轮数收进该名字的 hover tooltip，不再在 UI 上占位。`SourcesChip`（AI 用了 N 项数据）保留，并入同一行元信息，视觉统一。

**③ 整体打磨**
消息间距 `space-y-7` → `space-y-6`；元信息行用 flex 统一节奏；暗色 `#212121` 系不变；无新增渐变/emoji。

## tool_call chip 映射表

| 工具原名 | 展示标签 |
|---|---|
| `health_query` / `health_query_data` | 查询健康数据 |
| `health_record` | 记录健康数据 |
| `health_analysis` | 分析健康数据 |
| `health_manage` | 管理健康计划 |
| `health_data_summary` | 汇总健康数据 |
| `knowledge_search` / `knowledge_query` | 检索知识库 |
| `web_search` | 联网搜索 |
| `search` | 搜索 |
| `health_*`（未列出） | 调用健康工具 |
| `knowledge_*` / `*_search` | 检索知识库 / 搜索 |
| 未知工具 / 空名 | 调用工具（兜底） |

## 前后对比要点
- 之前：工具调用 = 正文里一坨裸文本 + JSON args；脚注 = 一排 dev 指标 + 内部模型 id。
- 之后：工具调用 = 一排人话 chips；脚注 = 一个干净模型名（细节藏 tooltip）。

## 新增文件（均 < 500 行）
- `toolCallParse.ts` — 纯字符串解析（切段 + 标签映射）
- `modelName.ts` — 模型 id → 友好名

- `npm run test` → 17 files / **120 passed**
- `npm run lint` → 通过（仅既有 warning，无 error）
- `npm run build` → 通过

author: alondero
body:
Closes #318.

## What this adds

The user-facing Settings surface over R1's backend (#315): a **"Coordinator Read API"** section in `AppSettingsModal` that turns the backend-only token into something a user manages, and makes "off and safe" obvious on a fresh install.

- **Disabled-by-default toggle** — driven by `get_coordinator_status` → `set_coordinator_api_enabled`, optimistic with rollback on failure.
- **Mint + copy token** — "Generate token" calls `generate_coordinator_read_token`, reveals the value in a read-only mono field with a Copy button (→ "Copied!", resets after 2s). Token controls only appear once the API is enabled.
- **Mint-once-reveal** — when a token already exists from a prior session, a masked `••••••••` placeholder shows and the button reads "Regenerate token", honouring the backend's choice never to re-expose a token value.
- **Clear messaging** — "binds to loopback and your LAN only — reaching it from anywhere else is your own tunnel (Tailscale, Cloudflare, WireGuard)", plus a warning banner about who can read node statuses.

## Notes

- **Frontend-only.** R1 already shipped the three registered Tauri commands.
- The kill-switch guarantee lives backend-side: `validate_coordinator_read_token` returns `false` whenever the API is disabled, so flipping the toggle off immediately rejects requests regardless of any minted token. The UI just flips the flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Settings surface shows the coordinator API as disabled by default.
- [x] User can enable it and mint a read-scoped token.
- [x] Token can be copied to the clipboard.
- [x] Master toggle disables the API (kill-switch), immediately rejecting further requests.
- [x] Copy makes the loopback/LAN-bound, own-tunnel nature clear.

## Tests

`tests/unit/coordinator-settings.test.tsx` — written test-first (red → green), 5 cases mapping to each acceptance criterion. Full unit suite **417/417**, `tsc` clean, desktop + mobile build green.

## Summary
Operators on the published package have no `client/.env` — each harness authenticates through its OWN auth store outside the Jinn app, and the daemon only forwards an allowlisted set of env vars (`buildAgentEnv`) to the spawned harness binary. Without a doc for this, operators put provider keys in `client/.env` and hit silent, delayed 403s.

This adds `docs/operator/rotating-harness-keys.md`: the per-harness auth store, canonical rotate command/file, and forwarded env vars for the three shipping harnesses (claude-code, codex, hermes-agent); an explicit warning that the repo `client/.env` is dev-only and must not be used for runtime provider keys (distinguished from the legitimate docker-compose `.env`); and a "why a wrong key fails silently" troubleshooting section pointing at the operator app's §2.9 precheck/doctor panel. Cross-referenced from `docs/operator-testnet.md`, `client/README.md`, `client/OPERATOR-APP-SPEC.md` §2.9, and `CLAUDE.md`.

All per-harness facts were verified against the harness adapter source (not guessed). The issue's `hermes auth add` command could not be found in code, so the doc leads with the verified surfaces (`~/.hermes/.env` + `hermes login`) and flags the add/rotate subcommand as unconfirmed.

## Test plan
Docs-only change — no code touched, so no typecheck/test/build applies.
- All relative links (the new doc's outbound links + the four back-links + in-doc anchors) verified to resolve.
- Per-harness auth claims cross-checked against `client/src` / harness adapter source.
- `client/.env` dev-only claim verified against `client/src/main.ts` (loaded only under `JINN_LOAD_DEV_ENV=1` / `NODE_ENV=development`).
- No emoji; plain speech on keys/auth.

Closes #563

author: ogabasseyy
body:
## Summary
- **Bump react-doctor 0.5.1 → 0.5.5** (latest). 0.5.5 adds security analyzers (`supabase-rls-policy-risk`, `insecure-crypto-risk`, `dangerous-html-sink`, `repository-secret-file`, `build-pipeline-secret-boundary`, …).
- **`ignore.files`** for non-React-app code the broad `-y` scan mis-flags as `unused-file`: deployed Supabase edge functions, VPS cron workers, Cloudflare proxy, temp/CLI scripts, `public/` assets, generated Supabase types, the Expo config plugin.

## Why
react-doctor's `-y` scan covers the whole monorepo, so it reports deployed/tooling/generated files as "unused" (they have no in-repo importers but are entry points). This scopes the `unused-file` signal to actual app source: **111 → 48 unique** (the remaining 48 = 25 dynamic-`import()`-loaded storefront/template false positives + 23 real app-source candidates, handled in a follow-up).

Security findings (crypto, RLS) are in `src/` + migrations — **not** the ignored dirs — so real-issue coverage is unaffected.

author: xuyushun441-sys
body:
## Why

Follow-up to [#1842](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/framework/pull/1842), which made the skill catalog (README index + `guides/skills.mdx` tables/cards) **generated** from each `SKILL.md` frontmatter via `build-skill-docs.ts`. Without a CI gate, the generated files can still be hand-edited or left stale when a `SKILL.md` changes — the exact drift that caused the original fabricated-docs problem.

## What

Adds a **`Check Skill Docs`** job to `ci.yml`:
- Gated by `paths-filter` — runs only when `skills/**`, `content/docs/guides/skills.mdx`, or `packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts` change.
- Runs `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:skill-docs` (`build-skill-docs.ts --check`), which **fails (exit 1)** if the README/guide listings differ from what the frontmatter would generate, with a hint to run `gen:skill-docs`.
- Lightweight: install + run, no build (the script only reads files via `tsx`).

## Verification

- `ci.yml` validated as YAML.
- Ran the exact CI command against current `main` → **passes** (`Skill docs in sync`).
- Negative test: introduced drift in the guide → check **exits 1** with the fix hint; reverted → passes again.
- This PR edits `ci.yml`, so the new job runs on the PR itself (self-test).

Ajoute des **profils** (presets) pour l'agent d'implémentation : un profil regroupe un modèle, un effort et un implémenteur, choisissable en un clic.

## Summary

Fixes OCR reprocess classification for Transkribus retries when triggered from the staff UI.

Production finding: document 69 had a reusable Transkribus upload run (`remote_doc_id`, `pages_query`, matching collection/model), but the web ECS task did not have Transkribus routing/reprocess config. author: lamasu
body:
Small additive endpoint that returns the four-slot view for one operator. Built so an operator's onboarding agent can verify all slots are wired before going live.

## API

```
GET /api/operators/:slug/status
```

Response: `{ kernels, capabilities (with sla + availability), channels, totals, agentCardUrls, status: 'ready' | 'partial' | 'unconfigured', missing: string[] }`.

## Slot mapping

| Slot | Check |
|---|---|
| 1. Capability | capabilities exist for the operator's kernels |
| 2. SLA | capabilities[].sla set (human lane only) |
| 3. Channel | at least one enabled channel attached |
| 4. Availability | capabilities[].availability set with non-empty mode |

If anything's missing, the `missing[]` field tells the agent (or the human) exactly which slot + how to fix it (with the relevant A2A skill / route).

## Tests

7 vitest cases — unconfigured / ready / partial-on-each-slot / agent-card-urls / cache header.

## Dependencies

Builds on PR #112 (operator-channels, on master). **Does NOT depend on PR #118** (registry-talks-back) — orthogonal.

## 1. macOS Retina 立绘模糊
`PortraitController._apply_pixmap_to_label` 原按逻辑尺寸缩放(dpr=1.0),在 2x
retina 屏上被拉伸成半分辨率(糊)。改为按物理像素(逻辑尺寸 × devicePixelRatio)
缩放并标记 dpr,逻辑尺寸(deviceIndependentSize)不变 → 不影响舞台布局,只提升清晰度。

## 2. 舞台与碰撞体积过大
- **宽度动态包络**:窗口宽此前固定保底 860,远大于实际内容(气泡 640、立绘更窄),
  两侧留大片空白。改为 `window_w = max(立绘, 控制组) + 边距`,随内容收窄(如 736),
  去掉 860 保底。
- **舞台碰撞贴合(默认开)**:`setMask` 把窗口命中/绘制区裁到「立绘+气泡+输入栏」矩形
  并集 ∪ 可见子控件,立绘四周透明空白点击穿透到下层、不再误拖桌宠;异常清除遮罩降级。
  窗口尺寸变更(`_apply_pet_layout`)与子控件重排(`_layout_stage`)两条路径都刷新
  遮罩(抑帧内单帧呈现),避免气泡自适应变高时被裁。设置页保留关闭开关。
- 附:舞台调试框开发者选项(env `SAKURA_STAGE_DEBUG` / 设置页),叠加窗口/布局/立绘
  三框 + DPR 数值,用于排查布局与 HiDPI。

## 3. 接话(backchannel)TTS 稳定性
- **文本清洗**:`_normalize_tts_request_text` 去前导标点、迭代脱「」/括号/引号、无可
  发音字符返回空串 → 调用点跳过合成,根治 "……"/纯标点文本触发 GPT-SoVITS 400。
- **队列门控**:接话音频预生成限额 16→2,且仅在 TTS 队列空闲
  (`_tts_provider_has_queued_work`)时预生成,避免抢占正文合成/播放。
- 变体级 portrait 校验(manifest 加载时按角色表情词表校验)。

## 测试
全量单测 612 passed(含新增 TTS 清洗、manifest 变体 portrait、pet_window 用例)。

## 部署
立绘 dpr 与宽度包络无新依赖;碰撞遮罩默认开、设置页可关。

author: thusspokedata
body:
## Qué

Agrega `suppressHydrationWarning` al elemento `<time>` de la sección **Auditoría / Última edición** en `EditorialContentForm`.

## Por qué

El texto humano se formatea con `toLocaleString("es-AR", { dateStyle: "long", timeStyle: "short" })`, cuyo resultado depende del ICU del runtime:

- **Server (Node):** `14 de junio de 2026, 12:32 a. m.`
- **Cliente (browser):** `14 de junio de 2026 a las 12:32 a. m.`

La diferencia en el conector dispara un hydration mismatch de React (`Recoverable Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client`).

El atributo `dateTime` ya expone el ISO estable y machine-readable, así que el único texto que difiere es el visible. Suprimir el warning en este `<time>` es el patrón recomendado de Next para fechas inherentemente locale/ICU-dependientes.

## Scope / auditoría

Código admin pre-existente de **v0.3-geo-a/b** (PRs #11 / #12), **no parte de v0.4-a**. Branch chica de 1 commit.

Se auditaron los otros usos de formateo de fecha/número en admin; ninguno reproduce el mismo bug:

| Componente | Patrón | Veredicto |
|---|---|---|
| `StatusSection` | `toLocaleDateString` solo fecha (client, SSR) | sin hora → sin conector; mes corto consistente entre ICUs → OK |
| `ListingsTable` | date-only + `Date.now()` | **server component**, no hidrata → OK |
| `SavedIndicator` (`ListingForm`) | `toLocaleTimeString` solo hora | estado client-only (`savedAt` null en SSR) → no se renderiza en SSR → OK |
| `EditorialContentForm` :365 | `value.toLocaleString` (número) | grouping es-AR determinista → OK |

## Quality gates

- `npm run lint` → ✅ No issues found
- `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) → ✅
- `npm run build` (`next build`) → ✅

body:
## Summary

Phase 6 of MOBILE-PLAN.md — **Build & distribution**. Produces an installable, sideloadable release APK from source, signed with a **dedicated app-signing keystore** that is separate from the `expo-secure-store` Android Keystore holding user API keys. Follows #1→#3: zero upstream-file edits, so `git merge upstream/main` stays clean.

Also marks **Phase 5** done in the plan (it was already emulator-verified in `abcfb07` but the doc still said TODO).

## What's here

- **`plugins/withReleaseSigning.js`** — Expo config plugin that injects a release `signingConfig` into `android/app/build.gradle` *at prebuild time*. `android/` is gitignored (regenerated by `expo prebuild`), so expressing signing as a plugin keeps a *signed* build reproducible from source **and** keeps the tracking repo merge-clean. Reads gitignored `credentials/keystore.properties`; falls back to the debug key when absent, so credential-less prebuilds/CI still build.
- **`scripts/build-apk.sh`** + `npm run build:apk` — one-command flow. Pins **JDK 17** (RN 0.79 / Gradle 8.13 reject JDK 21+), ensures `local.properties`, prebuilds, `assembleRelease`, and verifies the signer cert.
- **`docs/BUILD.md`** — prerequisites, signing model, keystore generation/**backup warning**, verification, deferred Play `.aab` path.
- **`.gitignore`** — never commit `/credentials/` (the keystore is the app's identity).

## Distribution

v1 ships as a **sideloaded universal APK** (`adb install -r …/app-release.apk`). Play `.aab` deferred (YAGNI for v1).

## Verification

- Clean `expo prebuild --clean` reproducibly injects the release `signingConfig`.
- Release JS bundle builds — **986 modules** (Metro bundles the aliased upstream router/providers in production mode).
- `gradlew assembleRelease` → **75 MB `app-release.apk`**, signer SHA-256 `03a05328…518926` **matches the generated release keystore** (`CN=freellmapiphone`, not the debug key).

## Summary

First foundation sub-project (F1) of the FishHaven × Micya roadmap. Replaces the always-on demo login with a real **account → multi-profile** identity system and clears the production-audit blockers.

- **Accounts & profiles:** one Auth.js login owns an `accounts` row that owns N `people` (profiles, `kind = adult | child`). Netflix-style profile picker (auto-skipped for a single no-PIN profile); optional per-profile PINs.
- **Admin/guardian zone** (`/app/admin`): PIN-locked; required once a child profile exists. Admin re-locks on every profile switch and child profiles are hard-blocked from admin (defense in depth).
- **Persisted data:** activity re-keyed `email → person_id` with the previously-missing `log_activity`/`my_activity` RPCs; strikes now persisted (`add_strike`/`clear_strikes`/`active_strikes`), seeded into the UI and recorded on trigger.
- **Auth hardening:** removed the demo Credentials provider and `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking`; Auth.js split into edge-safe `auth.config.ts` + Node `auth.ts`; security headers (CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options); in-memory rate limiting + PIN throttle.
- **Security:** privileged `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs have EXECUTE **revoked from `anon`/`public`** and granted only to `service_role` (the public anon key would otherwise allow PIN brute-force / account spam). The server calls them with the service-role key.
- **Rebrand:** Haven Kids → **FishHaven** (all-ages framing).

author: jarbozhang
body:
## Summary

BitSender can now craft HTTP/1.1 cleartext request frames from semantic Layer 7 fields instead of requiring users to hand-write HTTP bytes as hex. The new HTTP mode still behaves like BitSender: it emits raw Ethernet + IPv4 + TCP + payload bytes, with checksums handled by the existing typed Rust builders.

## What changed

| Area | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Protocol builder | Added `PacketSpec::Http` and `HttpSpec`, serializing method/host/path/headers/body into CRLF HTTP/1.1 request payloads over TCP. |
| Validation | Rejects empty method/host, malformed header lines, and duplicate `Host:` in free-form headers so the dedicated host field stays authoritative. |
| Editor UX | Adds an HTTP tab with Application-layer fields and APP-colored bytes in the hex scope. |
| Templates/docs | Adds a default HTTP GET template and documents that this is raw HTTP payload crafting, not a stateful HTTP client or HTTPS/TLS stack. |

## Design notes

- HTTP intentionally delegates frame construction to the existing TCP builder, preserving IPv4/TCP checksum behavior and the Rust -> TypeScript specta contract.
- This does not implement TCP handshakes, seq/ack tracking, response capture, or TLS. Those remain follow-up work for a future stateful transaction engine.
- The e2e mock now returns an HTTP-shaped frame for `kind: "http"`, so the UI verifies Layer 7 rendering without requiring a Tauri runtime.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm test:e2e`
- `ce-code-review mode:agent plan:docs/plans/2026-06-14-001-feat-http-packet-builder-plan.md` -> Ready to merge; one duplicate-Host finding fixed.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No additional production monitoring required. This is a desktop packet-construction feature with no backend service, database, or hosted runtime to observe after merge.

Validation after release should focus on local app behavior:

- Open Packet Editor -> HTTP tab; confirm the scope shows APP-colored HTTP bytes.
- Build a default HTTP GET frame and confirm payload bytes decode to `GET / HTTP/1.1` with the expected `Host` and `Connection` headers.
- Watch for GitHub issue/search terms: `HTTP`, `Host header`, `checksum`, `PacketSpec::Http`, `headers`.
- Rollback trigger: revert this PR if HTTP preview fails to build or existing TCP/UDP/ICMP previews regress in released binaries.

## Overview                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
Adds TOTP (RFC 6238) two-factor authentication as a second confirmation                                                                                                                                             
layer for high-risk write operations executed by the Telegram AI agent.                                                                                                                                             
Any operation classified as high-risk (e.g. DELETE, bulk UPDATE) must be                                                                                                                                            
confirmed with a 6-digit code from the user's authenticator app before                                                                                                                                              
it is executed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
## Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
A single inline-button confirmation is insufficient for high-risk ops:                                                                                                                                              
- Anyone with access to the Telegram session can tap Confirm.                                                                                                                                                       
- TOTP requires physical possession of the user's phone, providing a                                                                                                                                                
  strong second factor with no external service dependency (fully offline,                                                                                                                                          
  stateless, RFC 6238 compliant).

author: anarchistsid
body:
## What

Closes the **+1 day offset** in auto-scheduling surfaced when investigating why movies wasn't publishing on the same day as gaming. Same root pattern silently affects movies/sports/ai_creators/anime — every approval gets scheduled 1 day later than it should.

## Root cause chain (proven by tracing 2 movies blueprints)

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| 1 | `push_to_backlog` pre-sets `scheduled_for` at blueprint creation — today's 06:30 UTC if not yet past, else tomorrow's |
| 2 | Afternoon-pipeline niches (movies/sports/ai/anime run at 08:00 UTC+) get **tomorrow** as their pre-set slot |
| 3 | Operator approves later that day via the dashboard, which calls `_next_available_slot` to recompute (always-recompute logic so multi-same-day approvals don't stack) |
| 4 | `_next_available_slot` queries existing VISUAL_READY+PUBLISHED records, treats their `scheduled_for` as occupied — **but does NOT exclude the record being scheduled** |
| 5 | The blueprint's own pre-set `scheduled_for` blocks its own preferred slot → scheduler picks day-after |

**Why gaming is immune:** its pipeline runs at 04:00 UTC (BEFORE the 06:30 UTC publish window), so its pre-set slot is always today's 06:30 UTC. By approval time, that's already past → skipped by the `candidate <= earliest` guard rather than the `occupied_slots` check. So gaming has no self-collision; afternoon-pipeline niches do.

### Evidence

Two movies blueprints approved 2026-06-13 16:07 IST and 16:35 IST got scheduled to **Jun 15 + Jun 16** instead of **Jun 14 + 15**:

```
24d7c0b3 "Does Woody finally get his ending in Toy Story 5?"  approved 16:07 IST → scheduled Jun 15 12:00
e6cd1958 "What happens when aliens contact Earth on live TV?" approved 16:35 IST → scheduled Jun 16 12:00
```

Same pattern explains why sports/anime/ai_creators have been silently slow-shifting all their publishes too.

## Fix

`dashboard/server/core/publishing_queue.py`:
- `_next_available_slot()` accepts new `exclude_record_id` parameter
- Collision-loop skips records whose id matches `exclude_record_id`
- Record id can live at `r["id"]` or `r["fields"]["id"]` depending on backing store — check both defensively
- **Backward compatible**: default empty string preserves old behavior exactly

Updated 6 call sites to pass `record_id`:
- `publishing_queue.PublishingQueue.approve`
- `review_server _execute_review_action`
- `review_server` batch-approve handler
- `blueprints.py` batch-review
- `blueprints.py` `approve_and_schedule`
- `blueprints.py` `batch_approve_schedule`

## Tests (3 new + 5 regression)

```
test_excludes_self_record_from_collision_check       PASSED  ← pins the headline fix
test_does_not_exclude_other_records_with_same_niche  PASSED  ← 1-per-niche rule intact
test_default_empty_exclude_id_preserves_old_behavior PASSED  ← backward compat

(existing test_optimal_time_learner_wiring suite — 5 tests, all pass)
```

## Operational impact after merge + deploy

Future approvals on afternoon-pipeline niches (movies / sports / ai_creators / anime) will publish **1 day earlier** than they currently do.

The 2 movies blueprints already scheduled to Jun 15 + 16 will publish on those days as currently scheduled — this fix applies to NEW approvals only. If you want to manually move them forward 1 day, run:

```sql
UPDATE blueprints
SET scheduled_for = scheduled_for - interval '1 day'
WHERE id IN ('24d7c0b3-...', 'e6cd1958-...');
```

(Not automated — preserving the existing schedule is also fine; movies will be back on a daily cadence within 2-3 days regardless.)

## Open PRs from this session (now 7 + 6 deep-dive)

| PR | Lines | Headline |
|---|---|---|
| #185 | 247 | One-shot PR-#183 migration deploy script |
| #186 | 453 | Generic `deploy.sh` + DEPLOYMENT.md + 3-layer drift findings |
| #187 | 58 | `daily_intel.sh` UV resolution + self-heal symlink |
| #188 | 421 | `install.sh` fresh-box setup |

author: nicholaskissel
body:
Collapses the onboarding wizard from five steps into a compact **two-screen** flow, rebased on current `main` (keeps the extracted `agent-prompts.ts`, the rivet-run-url fix, and other recent onboarding changes).

## Flow
- **Screen 1 — Run locally**: have your coding agent scaffold + run your first Actor (copy-prompt) or follow the quickstart. The separate "install RivetKit" and "create Actor" steps are gone — the prompt/quickstart cover them.
- **Screen 2 — Deploy to {platform}**: defaults straight to **Rivet Compute** (no upfront platform-picker step). Shows `npx @rivetkit/cli deploy --token …` + a live "waiting for deployment" check (`DeploymentCheck`), with **Done** gated until the deploy is detected. Other platforms reuse the existing connect setup.
- **Switch platform** dropdown is pinned **top-right** on the deploy screen (opens downward) and re-tunes the screen via the `provider` form field.

## Implementation notes
- `stepper-form.tsx`: added a `titleFor` / function-`description` slot + `StepHeading` so the deploy step can render the dynamic "Deploy to {platform}" title.
- `getting-started.tsx`: 2-step `defineStepper` (`local`, `deploy`); default provider `rivet`; managed pool provisioned on the local→deploy transition; finish saves non-Rivet config then routes to the dashboard. Removed the now-dead provider grid, install step, and verify-step components.

## Caveat
The deploy command shows `npx @rivetkit/cli deploy`, which is the **upcoming** CLI (not in the repo yet); the "waiting" state uses the existing Cloud-API managed-pool polling, so it works against today's backend. Swap the command's wording if the CLI ships under a different name.

## Patch .claude/rules — escalation routing + rule scope

Encodes two process rules so future autonomous runs escalate correctly and the gate
stops false-failing CI/test code.

1. **review.md — Loop Cap → Escalation Routing:**
   - Recurring same bug-class (≥2×) → autonomously **restructure with tests** (extract +
     unit-test), don't keep guessing one fix per Gate-3 cycle, don't escalate.
   - A purely **technical** loop-cap → label **`needs-architect`** + a structured decision
     request in the PR body (Jo forwards, does not decide the technical call).
   - **`needs-jo`** reserved for tier-3 risk, cost/quota, or product/strategy only.
2. **architecture.md — Scope:** the stack rules (pnpm/no-npm) and "no raw SQL outside
   `lib/db/migrations/`" govern application code (`app/`, `lib/`, `src/`, `server/`). CI
   workflows + `scripts/` + test fixtures follow their own conventions and are out of scope
   — e.g. a SQL classifier necessarily has SQL test fixtures, and CI may install a CLI tool.
   This resolves the reviewer contradiction "demand classifier tests but ban their SQL fixtures."
3. New `needs-architect` label + a regression test pinning the policy.

author: mattgyverlee
body:
## Produced-glyph set — foundation for the §8 inventory diff

Spec §8 mandates "Inventory — character discovery, **diffed against the base output set**." This lands the canonical "what glyphs does this keyboard produce" extractor that the diff (and the §18.6 coverage check) need.

### Landed
- **`buildProducedSet(ir, options?)`** in `@keyboard-studio/contracts` (`src/ir/producedSet.ts`) — the distinct NFC graphemes a keyboard emits from its `KeyboardIR`: rule char-outputs (**run-merged** before NFC), `index`/`outs` store expansion, deadkey *composition* outputs; excludes deadkey markers, `beep`, `raw`, control chars, and (by default) space.
- **`producedGlyphs(ir)`** (engine) is now a thin sorted-array wrapper over it.
- **`buildEmittableSet`** (keyboard-lint §18.6 coverage) now delegates to the same shared core.

### Why it matters (review-driven)
km-keyman + km-synthesis caught that the first cut NFC-normalized each char element *independently*, so a keyboard emitting base+combining as two `char` elements (`e` + `◌́`) yielded `["e","◌́"]` not `["é"]` — which would (a) falsely list `é` as a "letter to add" in the §8 diff and (b) emit a false `KM_LINT_INVENTORY_UNCOVERED` in §18.6. The **run-merge** fix + consolidating both consumers onto one core removes the bug *and* the §8/§18.6 divergence.

### Verification
`pnpm -r typecheck` clean (6 packages); **contracts 239, engine 695, keyboard-lint 60** passing.

The studio inventory-diff wiring (capture alphabet → `alphabet − producedGlyphs` → gallery) folds into the upcoming working-copy refactor.

author: johannesjo
body:
Durability follow-ups to #7901 / #7892 (Android total data loss when the
WebView IndexedDB is evicted while the durable on-device backup survives).

- Mobile auto-restore: on a blank/evicted launch (no state cache, but a
  usable on-device backup exists) restore the newest usable backup
  automatically instead of behind a confirm dialog users routinely dismiss.
  Only triggers for a genuinely empty live store (a deliberate in-app delete
  leaves a valid empty state cache and is not auto-restored); falls back to
  the informed prompt for corrupt/data-less blobs. Reports counts via snack.

- KeyValStore.onUpgrade no longer DROPs the table. It holds the durable
  on-device backup (keys backup / backup_prev); a destructive upgrade would
  wipe it the moment DATABASE_VERSION was bumped. Upgrades are now additive
  (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS), preserving rows.

- Record the last successful local-backup time (after the meaningful-data
  guard) and surface a "Last backup: <date>" line in the mobile Automatic
  Backups settings, so no-sync users can see they're protected; the
  timestamp also rides along in exported logs for eviction diagnosis.

Docs: correct 3.06-User-Data (Android backup is native app-private SQLite,
not WebView IndexedDB) and document the auto-restore + timestamp behavior.

Tests: auto-restore (usable / import-failure / corrupt-fallback / no-backup)
and getLastBackupTime in local-backup.service.spec; config-page spy updated.

Two toggleable map overlays on the live dashboard, like iridium-toolkit's `live-map`: the broadcasting **Iridium satellites** and the **targeted ring/beam ground footprints**. The data's already decoded from ring-alert frames — this surfaces it.

## Backend (`http.rs`)
Bucket ring-alert positions by altitude:
- geocentric **~800 km → satellite** (keyed by sat id, labelled with the satmap NORAD name when matched, with a ground-track trail)
- **<100 km → ground beam footprint** (keyed by sat+beam)

Served in `/api/state` as `iridium_sats` / `iridium_rings`, each with its own expiry (sats 10 min, rings 5 min).

A Leaflet layer control (top-right) toggles each overlay; visibility persists to `localStorage`. Satellites render as a 🛰 marker with a faint dashed ground track; rings as a teal footprint circle. Both stay **out of the aircraft/vessel auto-fit** so global satellite positions never yank the local view. Status line gains a sat count.

- Backend bucketing unit test (sat vs ring by altitude → `/api/state`)
- Browser render (gstack /browse) with injected data: the **IRIDIUM 106 satellite marker + ground track** and the **ring footprint circle** render with **no console errors**; both layer toggles present

author: michaelverdegaal
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a UNIQUE constraint on the `slug` column in the `pages` table to prevent multiple URLs from using the same slug, which would cause collisions in the on-disk `saved/<slug>/` folder structure.

## Key Changes
- **Database schema**: Added `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pages_slug ON pages(slug)` to enforce slug uniqueness. Using a unique index (rather than a column constraint) allows the constraint to be backfilled onto existing databases on their next open.
- **Test fixtures**: Updated `_page()` helper functions in both `test_database.py` and `test_cli.py` to use `slug_for_url(url)` instead of a hardcoded slug value. This ensures test pages have deterministic, unique slugs matching production behavior and satisfies the new constraint when multiple pages are seeded in a single test.
- **New test coverage**: Added `TestSlugConstraint` class with two tests:
  - `test_duplicate_slug_is_rejected`: Verifies that attempting to upsert a page with a duplicate slug raises `sqlite3.IntegrityError`
  - `test_index_is_added_to_a_db_created_before_the_constraint`: Confirms that the migration works correctly on legacy databases without the index
- **Documentation**: Updated `AGENTS.md` to document that `slug` is UNIQUE and names the on-disk `saved/<slug>/` folder.
- **Code cleanup**: Moved `import sqlite3` to the top of `test_database.py` with other imports instead of inline.

## Implementation Details
The unique index approach provides several benefits:
- Prevents slug collisions that would break slug-keyed lookups and cause file system conflicts
- Uses `IF NOT EXISTS` to safely apply the constraint to both new and existing databases
- Improves slug lookup performance as a side effect
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing databases

author: paulbellamy
body:
## Summary
This change makes the `mcp auth` command idempotent by detecting when a server is already authenticated and reachable, short-circuiting the OAuth flow and returning immediately with a "complete" status.

## Key Changes
- **Added `serverConnected()` function** in `auth.go`: Checks if an authenticated MCP session can be established with a server using stored credentials. It retrieves the auth token, attempts to connect, and validates the connection by completing the initialize handshake.

- **Updated `cmdAuth()` logic**: Added an idempotency check that runs before the OAuth discovery step. If the server is already connected, it logs a message and returns `{"status":"complete"}` without initiating an OAuth flow.

- **Updated documentation** in `SKILL.md`: Clarified that `mcp auth` is idempotent and safe to run without checking first. Added guidance on using `mcp ping` to test connection status separately.

- **Updated help text** in `main.go`: Added "(idempotent; no-op if already connected)" to the `auth` command description.

## Implementation Details
- The `serverConnected()` check happens after server configuration is loaded but before any OAuth discovery, ensuring we don't waste time or confuse users with auth URLs when authentication is unnecessary.
- The function properly handles token refresh (via `getAuthToken()`) and validates the connection by actually opening and closing a transport session.
- Returns `false` for any error condition (missing token, connection failure, invalid credentials), allowing the normal auth flow to proceed.
- No pending auth state is written when the server is already connected, preventing stale authentication artifacts.
