author: pauldotterer
body:
Implements `manchtools/power-manage-sdk#88` — adds the missing argv validators so package-manager invocations validate against intent, and a `--` end-of-options helper so a flag-shaped value can never be reparsed as an option.

## What

- `pkg.ValidateRpmPackageName` — an RPM `%{NAME}` read off a (possibly crafted) `.rpm` must start alphanumeric and use `[a-zA-Z0-9._+-]`. Kills option/macro injection into `rpm -q`/`rpm -e` (e.g. a `.rpm` whose name is `--eval=%{lua:...}`).
- `pkg.ValidateRepoBaseURL` — dnf `baseurl` / zypper `url` / pacman `server` must be **https** with a host (package-manager template vars `$releasever`/`$arch` survive). apt is intentionally excluded — its security model is the gpg-signed Release file, so http+gpg is legitimate.
- `pkg.ValidateGpgKeyRef` — a dnf/zypper `Gpgkey` passed to `rpm --import` is restricted to an https URL, a `file:///abs` path, or an absolute path; no `..`, no leading `-`, no `http://`, no rpm `ext::` external transport.
- `pkg.ValidateRemoteName` — a flatpak remote alias is a leading-alphanumeric operand.
- `exec.SeparatePositionals(flags, positionals...)` + `exec.EndOfOptions` — returns a fresh slice with `--` always inserted before operands, without mutating the caller's `flags`.

## Tests

- `go/pkg/validate_test.go`: accept/reject tables for each validator, with the **invalid cases sourced from intent** (leading `-`/`=`, metacharacters, control chars, `http://`, `ext::`, traversal), plus the `ABSENT` (empty) case.
- `go/sys/exec/argv_test.go`: `--` is always inserted and precedes every operand; the caller's `flags` slice is never mutated.

All green; `go vet`, `gofmt`, and the `archtest` fitness functions pass. The agent PR consumes these next (advances the same issue).

## Summary
Email gateway SMTP connections now use the correct TLS mode for port 465 and a thread-safe IPv4 fallback for broken IPv6 routes.

Cherry-picks #46061 from @liuhao1024, then fixes the fallback path so it uses supported `smtplib` extension points instead of unsupported `sock=` kwargs. Also adds security-focused regressions: certificate/TLS verification errors are not retried through fallback, and the IPv4 path does not monkeypatch process-global socket resolution.

## Changes
- `gateway/platforms/email.py`: add `_connect_smtp()` with `SMTP_SSL` for port 465 and `SMTP` + `STARTTLS` elsewhere.
- `gateway/platforms/email.py`: add IPv4-only SMTP subclasses that override `_get_socket()` instead of passing unsupported `sock=` kwargs.
- `gateway/platforms/email.py`: close partially-open SMTP sessions if `STARTTLS` fails.
- `tests/gateway/test_email.py`: cover 465/587 protocol selection, IPv4 fallback, no TLS-error retry, and no global resolver mutation.

## Security notes
- TLS verification still uses `ssl.create_default_context()`.
- Certificate / TLS verification failures are treated as security failures and are not retried via IPv4.
- The IPv4 fallback is per-connection and thread-safe; it does not patch `socket.getaddrinfo` globally.

author: maknonet
body:
## Was & Warum

Neue Schwester-Komponente **`CodeViewer`** für eine **universelle, read-only Quelltext-Ansicht** vieler Formate (Java, C#, Python, JSON, YAML, HTML, CSS, JS, XML, SQL …) mit **Syntax-Highlighting**, **sprachgenauem Code-Falten** (Java-Methoden/Klassen/`if`, Python-Einrückung, JSON/HTML-Blöcke), **hell/dunkel-Theme**, Zeilennummern und umschaltbarem Umbruch.

Dieser Funktionsumfang entspricht einem read-only Code-Editor. Statt Syntax/Falten/Theming pro Sprache selbst zu bauen, wird — wie besprochen — **CodeMirror 6 eingebettet**. Die bestehende `SearchNavigator`-UI bleibt erhalten und wird über `MatchNavigable` an CM6s Suche angebunden — die Such-UI ist damit über **alle drei Viewer** (XmlViewer/TextViewer/CodeViewer) konsistent.

## Architektur

- **`code/CodeViewer`** (`extends Div`, `implements MatchNavigable`): dünner Wrapper. `extends Div` (nicht `Composite`), damit `@ClientCallable` zuverlässig auf dem eigenen Element liegt (`this.$server.onMatchChange`).
- **Such-Anbindung:** `search/next/previous` → `executeJs` an CM6; CM6 zählt Treffer (`SearchCursor`) + markiert sie (Decorations) und meldet `count/index` **asynchron** via `@ClientCallable` zurück → `MatchChangeEvent` treibt den `SearchNavigator`. `setText` feuert **synchron** ein Reset-Event. Funktioniert, weil der `SearchNavigator` rein event-getrieben ist.
- **Editor lebt clientseitig** (Glue `code-viewer.js`); Java hält nur **serialisierbaren** Zustand und baut den Editor in `onAttach` neu auf (Re-Attach/Clustering-fest).
- **Sprachschicht (reines Java, testbar):** `CodeLanguage` (Sprachen → CM6-Id + Endungen) + `CodeLanguageDetector` (Auto-Erkennung über Endung/Inhalt; CM6 erkennt selbst nicht).
- **CM6 als `@NpmPackage`-Frontend-Deps** (vom demo-app-Vaadin-Build aufgelöst); **`web-common` bleibt npm-frei** und kompiliert/testet ohne Node.

## Demo

Neue Route `@Route("code")` (`CodeDemoView` + `SampleCodeFactory`) mit Sprach-Auswahl, eigener `SearchNavigator`-Instanz und Toggles (Theme, Umbruch, Zeilennummern, Falten); `MainView`/`TextDemoView` verlinken darauf.

## Tests / Verifikation

- `spotlessApply` + `:web-common:spotlessCheck` + `:web-common:test` → **grün, ohne npm**.
- `:demo-app:compileJava` → **kompiliert** (CodeDemoView/SampleCodeFactory/Select).
- Neu: `CodeLanguageDetectorTest` (13), `CodeViewerTest` (8 – Zustand, `onMatchChange`-Callback, Reset-Event, **Serialisierungs-Roundtrip**, echtes `SearchNavigator`-Zusammenspiel). Bestehende Viewer-Tests unverändert grün.

## Noch zu prüfen (Browser/Zielmaschine)

Die **CM6-Laufzeit ist hier nicht prüfbar** (kein Node/Netz; `vaadinPrepareFrontend` blieb gecacht). Auf der Zielmaschine:
1. `./gradlew clean vaadinPrepareFrontend :demo-app:bootRun` (zieht CM6 per npm, regeneriert `demo-app/package.json` mit den `@codemirror/*`-Deps + Hash → gehört dann in den Branch),
2. `/code` prüfen: Syntax je Sprache, Falten, Theme-Toggle, Umbruch, Zeilennummern, Suche über den `SearchNavigator`.
3. **Exakte CM6-Paketversionen** (in `CodeViewer` gepinnt) ggf. an die Registry anpassen, falls npm eine nicht findet.

Hinweis: C#/`legacy-modes` faltet schwächer als die Lezer-Sprachen. PR **nicht** selbst mergen.

## What this does

Sharpens the **deal pipeline** and **demand forecast** for the HMD demo (the sales-tracking + forecasting focus area).

### Pipeline → forecast (the core loop)
- **Industry-standard stages** for both channels: `Lead → Qualification → Proposal → Evaluation → Negotiation → Closed Won/Lost` (migration `0004` renames the enum in place, no data loss). Replaces the RFI/RFP vocabulary to match how the customer described their process.
- **Advancing a deal now moves the forecast.** `changeStage` re-baselines win probability to the stage default, so the weighted pipeline + time-phased forecast track the pipeline. Manual override still applies.
- Reps can drive deals: **drag-and-drop** (`@dnd-kit`), an **Advance / Move-to-stage** menu, and an **inline probability slider**. Mutations invalidate deals + dashboards + accounts so the rep and Finance forecasts update live.

### Forecast transparency
- Hover a quarter bar to see its breakdown (revenue: device / fixed-term / recurring → weighted total; devices: per-model → units to build), plus a "how it's computed" caption stating the formula. Client-side, no backend change.

### Quality / UX
- Added a **toast** system; deal writes surface errors and self-heal (re-sync the board) instead of failing silently on a 404/403.
- **Open account** from a deal card (menu + account-name link) — notes/timeline live on the Account 360.

## Notes for reviewers

## Why

`RuntimeConfigPlugin` is the open mechanism that serves the SPA's per-request `features` map. But it enumerated a **closed** feature set and used **billing vocabulary** (`resolvePlanFeatures` / `RuntimeConfigPlanFeatures`), so a distribution couldn't add a commercial feature (custom domain, SSO, …) without editing the open framework — commercial/pricing policy bleeding into open-core.

## What

- The `features` map is now **open-ended**: the policy hook's returned flags are merged verbatim, so a host injects **arbitrary keys** (e.g. the cloud control plane returns `customDomain`/`sso` from its plan entitlements) with **no framework change**.
- Seam renamed **plan-agnostic**: `resolveFeatures` / `RuntimeFeatureOverrides`. `resolvePlanFeatures` / `RuntimeConfigPlanFeatures` stay as **deprecated, still-honoured** aliases (no breakage).
- `aiStudio` / `autoPublishAiBuilds` remain the framework's own non-commercial mechanism defaults (ADR-0005: AI authoring is all-plan, cost-gated — not a paid tier).

## Tests

New `runtime-config-plugin.test.ts`: base flags, **arbitrary-key passthrough**, deprecated-alias compatibility, static default. cloud-connection 48/48.

author: junhyeong9812
body:
## Overview

`InMemoryReactiveSessionRegistry` can lose a session when `saveSessionInformation` and `removeSessionInformation` run concurrently for the same principal.

## Problem

The per-principal session set was updated non-atomically:

- `saveSessionInformation` added the session id **outside** the `computeIfAbsent` mapping function.
- `removeSessionInformation` pruned the principal key with a non-atomic `get` → `isEmpty()` → `remove(principal)`.

Interleaving (principal `P` owns one session `S1`):

1. Thread A removes `S1`; the set becomes empty and A is about to remove key `P`.
2. Thread B saves `S2`: `computeIfAbsent(P)` still sees key `P`, returns the same set, and adds `S2`.
3. Thread A removes key `P` → the set `{S2}` is orphaned; `getAllSessions(P)` is empty and `S2` is lost.

The blocking `SessionRegistryImpl` already avoids this by performing both updates atomically with `compute`/`computeIfPresent` (on the same `ConcurrentMap` field shape and constructor); the reactive registry did not.

## Fix

Mirror the blocking `SessionRegistryImpl`: perform the add inside `compute`, and the remove-and-prune inside `computeIfPresent` (returning `null` to drop the key only while the set is empty). This makes the per-principal updates atomic.

A 1000-iteration, latch-synchronized concurrent save/remove stress test is added; it fails on the previous code and passes with the fix.

Closes gh-19338

author: alan-thegentleman
body:
Closes #862

## Type

Bug fix (`type:bug`)

## Summary

- `resolveNextRecommended` now routes to the next missing planning phase (`propose`/`spec`/`design`/`tasks`) instead of collapsing every incomplete-planning state into `resolve-blockers`.
- `resolve-blockers` is reserved for genuine anomalies (all planning done but apply still blocked).
- The status contract, all orchestrator/command prompts, and golden files are updated in sync so the orchestrator launches the planning phase instead of deadlocking.

## Why

The native status engine returned `resolve-blockers` whenever any planning artifact was missing — even during normal early planning. The orchestrator contract treats `resolve-blockers` as a hard stop, so the orchestrator refused to launch the very phases that produce the missing artifacts: a false deadlock during the planning half of the SDD lifecycle.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `internal/sddstatus/status.go` | Add `propose`/`spec`/`design`/`tasks` phase tokens; route planning in dependency order; reserve `resolve-blockers` for anomalies; add planning instructions |

author: cain-ish
body:
Review-driven follow-up from a four-axis deep audit (data-quality, automation-completeness, cost-router standalone+integration, code-size). This PR lands the **low-risk, well-specified, fully-tested** findings; the automation/command-collapse axis (D2) and the larger graph-GC + cost-router learning-loop items are tracked for a follow-up PR.

## Data correctness — a real YAML parser where it mattered
- `knowledge_validate` detects malformed frontmatter via `yaml.load()` instead of two hard-coded regex shapes. This catches the **live** failure classes the regex missed: duplicated mapping keys (the tolerant reader returned the STALE first `updated:` value, corrupting the recency boost) and unquoted colon-bearing values. The runtime detector now uses the SAME standard as the test-oracle, so it can never again diverge from real YAML validity. `js-yaml` promoted to a runtime dependency.
- Autofix gained duplicate-key collapse (keep the freshest value).
- MOC `description:` is quoted (and drops the inner colon) — every generated `projects/*.md` was previously invalid YAML on every reindex.
- dream-runner writes canonical `related: [a, b]`, not invalid bracketless `related: [[a]], [[b]]`.
- **New oracle tests**: the detector flags EXACTLY the pages a real parser rejects (no more, no less); the dup-key autofix repairs the page AND keeps the freshest value.

## cost-router
- SessionStart banner drops `compact` — post-compaction hook output is silently dropped (upstream anthropics/claude-code#15174; matches the root hooks' documented stance).
- Premium-spend line shows only when spend was actually recorded today, so a standalone install (which never writes the ledger) stops advertising a permanent, misleading `$0.00`.
- README states one pricing baseline instead of two contradictory framings.

## Build hygiene
- Tracked `mcp/dist/` is now ONLY the 16 self-contained `*.bundle.js` that actually run (`mcp.json` launches `server.bundle.js`). The **176** per-file `tsc` artifacts that nothing imports at runtime are untracked + gitignored. `build` typechecks (`tsc --noEmit`) without emitting them; `tsconfig.build.json` removed.
- `verify.sh` / `test-verify.sh` probe `server.bundle.js` (the file that launches).
- `test-episodic-index` builds its one needed search module on the fly via esbuild (the only test that imported per-file dist), so the suite is independent of untracked artifacts.
- Removed dead `stop-hook-predicate.sh` (+ orphan test).

**Audit correction:** the code-size audit flagged `migrate-to-2.8.0.sh` as dead, but it implements the `.maintainer-needed`→`.wiki-writes` migration and has a passing test — kept (verified, not assumed).

## Verification
- vitest: **367 passed** (41 files, +2 oracle tests) under the offline CI envs
- bash suite: **120 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip**
- bundle-current gate, plugin validator, server smoke (`server.bundle.js` responds to `initialize`): all green

## Summary

The agent can now draw diagrams that appear in the carousel. When a diagram clarifies an explanation, the agent `Write`s a `.d2` file to a scratch dir; a second `PostToolUse` hook renders it browser-free (`d2 → svg → resvg → png`) into the same per-pane manifest the viewer already reads, and the carousel auto-opens **once per session**. A host-gated `SessionStart` hook nudges the agent on when/where to draw.

Design: `docs/2026-06-11-d2-diagrams-design.md` · Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-11-d2-diagrams.md`

### What's included
- `diagrams.sh` — `PostToolUse` render hook: `.d2` → png → manifest, with content-hash dedup, symmetric d2/resvg failure logging (`render-errors.log`), silent no-op when renderers absent, and once-per-session auto-open.
- `diagram-guidance.sh` — host-gated (`$TMUX`/`$KITTY_LISTEN_ON`) `SessionStart` hook injecting the diagram nudge with the resolved scratch dir embedded.
- `tmux-claude-images.sh` — new `--ensure-open` mode (open-if-closed; never kills an open viewer).
- `skills/diagrams/SKILL.md` — on-demand d2 cheatsheet (keeps the always-on footprint small).
- `hooks.json` — registers the 2nd `PostToolUse` + `SessionStart`.
- `flake.nix` / `README.md` — `d2` + `resvg` devShell deps + runtime-requirement note.

### Design decisions
- **Why `.d2` file + `PostToolUse`** (not a `Stop`-hook transcript scan): reuses the proven `images.sh` payload/keying machinery, no unverified transcript parsing, keeps chat prose clean.
- **Storage** in durable `images/diagrams/` (not the evictable transcode cache) so manifest paths never dangle.
- **Renderers resolved from ambient PATH**; absent → silent no-op (consistent with `images.sh`'s `jq` dependency).

author: hanzei
body:
Server-sourced reads (background fetch, single-note fetch, SSE note_updated)
and the post-import sync could overwrite a note's local row with stale server
state before its queued offline edit drained, transiently reverting the edit
(perceived data loss / UI flicker). The scope-prune step and remote/404 delete
paths could go further and hide or tombstone such a note entirely.

Defer all server-sourced writes to pending local state, keyed off the sync
queue:

- Add getPendingNoteIds(db): the set of note IDs with a pending queue op,
  parsed from the enqueued endpoint shapes (/notes create via local_id,
  /notes/reorder via note_ids, and /notes/{id}/... sub-resources).
- saveNote/saveNotes take an optional skipNoteIds set; queue-aware writers
  saveServerNote/saveServerNotes/saveServerNotesScope read the pending set
  once and skip those rows. Queue-drain writes stay ungated so they remain
  authoritative for the very op being replayed.
- removeLocalNotesNotIn also protects pending notes from the scope-prune
  DELETE, so an optimistic un-archive/restore isn't deleted before it drains.
- Gate the remote-delete paths (SSE note_deleted, the 404/410 tombstone in
  useOfflineNote) on the pending set; the drain reconciles afterward.
- Route useOfflineNotes, useSSE, useLabels post-mutation sync, and the Keep
  post-import sync through the queue-aware writers.

Notes with no pending ops sync from the server exactly as before, and
offline-created (local_*) notes remain protected from pruning. No API or
storage changes; mobile-internal sync behavior only.

Tests cover endpoint parsing, the skip/prune gating, and the fetch/SSE-vs
-pending-queue race for note edits, restores, and deletes.

author: agent-farnsworth[bot]
body:
Part of #1382

## Changes

First decomposition increment of #1382 — **Finding 2**, the safe and concrete perf slice. Resolves the per-tool conversation id **at most once** per `CreateAsync` call instead of once per conversation-aware tool.

- `InProcessIsolationStrategy.CreateAsync` previously called the private `ResolveConversationIdAsync` helper **four times** (for the `conversation`, `ask_user`, `spawn_subagent`, and `canvas` tools), each with identical arguments. The helper is a read-only function of `(conversationStore, sessionStore, agentId, sessionId)` — all fixed for the duration of the call — so its result is safe to memoise.
- Added a memoised local resolver (`GetConversationIdAsync`) that runs the lookup on first use and returns the cached value (which may legitimately be `null`) on subsequent calls. All four sites now route through it.
- Net effect: up to **three redundant DB round-trips** (each is a `sessionStore.GetAsync` + `conversationStore.ListAsync`) eliminated on the hot agent-handle-creation path, with no behaviour change.

### Tests (TDD)

`InProcessIsolationStrategyTests` (3 new):
- `CreateAsync_WithConversationStore_ResolvesConversationIdOnce` — registers a `CountingConversationStore` decorator; an all-tools descriptor fires both `ConversationTool` and `CanvasTool`, yet `ListAsync` is invoked **exactly once** (was 2 before the fix).
- `CreateAsync_WithConversationStore_BindsResolvedConversationIdToCanvasTool` — proves memoisation does not change the resolved value: the `CanvasTool` still binds to the correct conversation id, and the resolution still happens once.
- `CreateAsync_WithoutConversationStore_DoesNotResolve` — no `IConversationStore` registered → zero lookups (resolution path stays inert).

All 22 `InProcessIsolationStrategyTests` pass (19 existing + 3 new). Full solution build clean (0 warnings). `test-impacted.ps1` green: Architecture 180, Gateway.Tests 3002, Gateway.Conversations 200, Cli 298, Mcp 186, Scenarios 29.

## Scope / what this deliberately does NOT touch

This is **only** Finding 2. It does **not** touch the held `IToolProvider` service-locator rewrite of `CreateAsync` (the larger, higher-risk structural change in #1382 that wires every tool into every agent handle). That remains under its `hold-1382` marker for an attended session. The remaining decomposition steps — (b) `StreamCoreAsync` `MapAgentEvent` extraction and (c) the `IToolProvider` collection — are still open.

## Merge Notes

Touches only `InProcessIsolationStrategy.cs` (`src/gateway/BotNexus.Gateway/Isolation/`) and its test file. No file overlap with any of the other open PRs — safe to merge in any order. The change is internal and behaviour-preserving (pure read-dedup), so it carries no migration or config impact.

body:
### Motivation
- Introduce explicit PKI environment concept so scans, validations and reports can be scoped to environments instead of a global latest-scan model. 
- Replace the older "Evidence Replay" presentation with a safer, interactive "Guided Exposure Walkthrough" that uses collected evidence only and allows harmless demo inputs.

### Description
- Add a new `PkiEnvironment` model and DB migration support in `app/db/migrate.py` via `_ensure_environment_schema` to create the `pki_environments` table, add environment-related columns to `scans` and `validation_runs`, and backfill an initial environment for existing scans.
- Wire environment resolution into ingestion in `app/services/ingest.py` by creating/resolving environments, setting `scan.environment_id`, maintaining `scan_sequence`, `previous_scan_id`, `is_current_for_environment`, and updating `environment.last_scan_*` metadata.
- Extend validation logic in `app/services/validation_engine.py` to build a walkthrough script (`build_walkthrough_script`), include `walkthrough_script` in `ValidationRun.evidence_json`, add sanitization (`sanitize_walkthrough_input`) and storage (`store_walkthrough_input`), and mark validation runs with `environment_id`.
- Update application routes and UI in `app/main.py`, templates and static assets to support environment selection (`environment-selector`), per-environment latest/selected scan behavior, export metadata, and replace evidence-replay pages with the guided walkthrough console; add a JS-driven interactive console in `app/static/js/validation.js` and styles in `app/static/css/style.css`.
- Add new/updated API and schema fields: `CollectorPayload` gains environment hints, and a new POST endpoint `/api/v1/validations/{validation_id}/walkthrough-input` to accept sanitized demo inputs.
- Add comprehensive tests covering environment isolation and scoping (`tests/test_environment_isolation.py`), validation engine behavior and input sanitization (`tests/test_validation_engine.py`), route behavior (`tests/test_validation_routes.py`), and safety/static checks (`tests/test_validation_safety.py`).

### Testing
- Ran the test suite including `tests/test_environment_isolation.py`, `tests/test_validation_engine.py`, `tests/test_validation_routes.py`, and `tests/test_validation_safety.py`, and all tests passed. 
- Exercised ingestion flow (`/api/v1/collector/ingest`) and UI flows for selecting environments, starting a walkthrough, and saving walkthrough inputs via the new API, verifying environment-scoped scans and validation `environment_id` propagation.

Users encounter "Drive files error: Request had insufficient authentication scopes" when calling the file listing endpoint, but receive a generic 500 response without guidance on resolution.

## Changes

**Error Handling in backend/src/drive.js**

Before: `500 { "error": "Failed to list Drive files" }`

After (development): `403 { "error": "Authentication failed: insufficient scopes...", "details": "..." }`

After (production): `403 { "error": "Authentication failed: insufficient scopes..." }`

This maintains backward compatibility for non-scope errors while providing scope-specific guidance that directs users to configure credentials correctly.

author: alexandrosk0
body:
## What

Closes the JQL-injection cluster from the 2026-06-13 security audit (HIGH **H3** + re-confirmed **E1**). Server-controlled strings were interpolated into JQL double-quoted literals **without escaping**, so a `"` in the value broke out of the literal and let a malicious / compromised tracker rewrite the autocomplete and key-fetch queries (cross-project disclosure / query manipulation).

## Changes

- **Shared helper** — promoted the file-local `EscapeJqlString` (anon namespace in `JiraActivityFeed.cpp`) into `tracker_jql::QuoteLiteral` at `Source/Core/include/Tracker/JqlEscape.h` + `JqlEscape.cpp`. One canonical copy; escapes `\` first then `"`; returns the escaped **inner** content (callers add the surrounding quotes). It lives behind the per-backend Tracker include tree — never on `ITrackerBackend` or a role interface (no backend-leak).
- **H3** (`JqlSuggestEngine.cpp` `BuildJqlUserInsert`) — both the display-name **and** AccountId paths now route through the helper. Previously a display name containing `"` was *abandoned* (fell through to an **unescaped** AccountId). Now the name is escaped and used; the AccountId fallback is escaped too.
- **E1** (`JiraIssueSearch.cpp` `BuildKeyInJql`) — every issue key is escaped in both the single-key `=` and multi-key `in (...)` paths.
- **`JiraActivityFeed.cpp`** — re-pointed to the shared helper (the 4 callers already escaped; behaviour unchanged).
- **Tests** — `tests/Core/JqlEscape.test.cpp` (doctest): proves an AccountId/key/display-name containing `"` and `\` produces a correctly-escaped literal that does **not** break out, including the audit's `FOO" OR project=SECRET OR key="BAR` payload and the backslash-first ordering; plus a wrapped-literal balance invariant.

## Verification

- Strict-zone delta-lint clean (`test-lint-rules.sh --diff origin/develop`).
- The four affected Tracker objects compile cleanly on **both** standalone (GLFW/GL) and DX12 targets.
- Doctest: 4 cases / 15 assertions — all pass (built + run standalone; the in-tree `SmatchetTests` link is blocked by a pre-existing, unrelated `OfflineQueueBackendSwap.test.cpp` exceptions-config break, last touched by #1120 — flagged as residual risk, not introduced here).

`docs/self-improvement/categories/security.md` H3 + E1 marked applied.

author: tsuka1128
body:
## 問題
手動AI分析を実行しても、通知ベルに何も表示されない（super_admin ユーザーの場合）。

## 原因
- AI分析完了通知は admin / executive / manager 宛に**作成されている**（本番DBで確認済み）
- `notifications` の RLS が `target_role = 自分のrole` の**厳密一致**（`migration 076`）
- ログインユーザーの role が `super_admin` のため、admin/executive/manager 宛のどの通知にも一致せず、ベルが常に空になっていた
- AI分析に限らず、**super_admin はロール指定の全通知を受け取れない**構造的な穴

## 修正
`notifications` の SELECT / UPDATE ポリシーに「**自分が super_admin かつ target_role='admin' なら可視**」を追加。super_admin は実質 admin 相当のため admin 宛通知を見せる。これで AI分析完了通知やその他のadmin宛通知がベルに出るようになる。

## 実装（CLAUDE.md準拠）
- SQL Editor直編集は禁止のため `supabase/migrations/20260614000000_notifications_superadmin_visibility.sql` を作成
- DROP POLICY IF EXISTS + CREATE の冪等な再作成
- **マージ後に `supabase db push` で本番反映が必要**

## 注意
- 通知の作成側（admin/executive/manager宛）は変更していない。super_admin 専用の通知行を増やすのではなく、RLSで admin 宛を見せる方式（行数を増やさずsystemicに解決）

author: fermatmind
body:
## What changed

This PR improves CMS-backed internal link rendering so article and rich-content surfaces no longer expose raw internal paths such as `/zh/tests/...` or `/zh/articles/...` as visible link text.

The change adds a shared internal-link label resolver and wires it into the existing CMS HTML, simple Markdown, and inline Markdown renderers. Article detail pages additionally resolve linked article routes to the target article's CMS title, so cross-article references show descriptive titles instead of slugs.

Covered rendering surfaces include article bodies, content pages, support/trust pages, career guides, career job rich text, personality content sections, public content assets, and topic rich-text sections.

## Why

Some SEO article sections were displaying internal links as raw paths. That made related reading, trust links, and next-step links harder to scan and weaker as editorial navigation. The desired behavior is descriptive anchor text, similar to common SEO article patterns, while still preserving backend/CMS content authority.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm vitest run tests/contracts/article-internal-link-anchor-text.contract.test.tsx`
- `git diff --check`
- Local browser verification on `/zh/articles/career-confusion-test-map` and `/zh/articles/enneagram-personality-test-explained`: no raw-path anchor text in main content links.
- Local sitemap subset scan across article/content/help/topic/personality/career guide/test SEO routes: no raw-path anchor text findings.
- Career job and career guide representative pages checked for raw-path anchor text.

## Repository Rule Impact

No content authority change. The frontend still only renders CMS/API-authored content; it does not add or replace public editorial copy. The new mapping is presentation-layer label resolution for known internal routes and CMS article titles.

## Intentionally deferred

- Existing visible canonical URL diagnostics on topic pages remain unchanged; those are metadata/debug display values, not article-body link anchors.
- Existing unrelated untracked files under `docs/research/personality/*` and `docs/seo/*` were not staged or included.

## Problème

Le \`cost_tracking\` affichait **0 sur tous les appels chat** : les clés de la table de prix (\`mistral-medium-3\`) ne matchaient jamais l'ID réel renvoyé par l'API (\`mistral-medium-latest\`) → \`unknownModel=true\` → \`costCents=0\`. Les **valeurs** de prix étaient aussi fausses (medium à 0.40/2.00 au lieu du tarif réel 1.5/7.5). Décisions budget aveugles.

## Correctif

**A — Table de prix réelle** (sourcé [mistral.ai/pricing](https://mistral.ai/pricing), juin 2026) : clés en préfixes (matchent les IDs versionnés via \`startsWith\`), 7 modèles aux tarifs réels. Test anti-collision \`magistral-medium\`/\`mistral-medium\`.

**B — Coût exact via cached tokens** : propagation de \`usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens\` (champ confirmé par appel réel à l'API) du client Mistral jusqu'au calcul ; cached facturé à 10%. Garde \`usage-missing\` ajouté pour ne plus retomber à 0 en silence si l'usage manque dans le stream.

## Preuve end-to-end (vraie route \`POST /api/chat/stream\`)

Appel réel → ligne \`cost_tracking\` : \`mistral-medium-latest\`, 9049 tokens dont **6408 cached (71%)**, \`cost_cents\` calculé avec déduction cached. L'usage est bien renvoyé par le stream → quota et coût reçoivent la vraie consommation.

## Validation

\`typecheck\` / \`lint\` / \`test\` : tout vert (38 fichiers, 0 fail). 8 tests cost-tracking (tarifs réels, collision de préfixe, split cached, clamp valeur aberrante).

## Hors scope (chantiers ultérieurs, pilotés par la mesure)

Optimisation \`prompt_cache_key\` · durcissement \`MISTRAL_MAX_TOKENS\` · extension du tracking aux autres opérations Mistral (titre, classif, résumé, OCR).

author: davidobando
body:
## Summary

Fixes the emitter to produce verifier-clean IL for nil-related operations on open type-parameter operands (`T?`, bare `T` after smart-cast narrowing). Pre-fix the JIT tolerated the IL at runtime but `ilverify` rejected it — eight `Gsharp.Extensions.Optional` helpers (the SDK migration introduced by #806) tripped the gate.

## Root cause

The existing slot-allocation/emit paths for nullable-related ops (`liftedBinarySlots`, `NullableValueTypeUnwrapCollector`, `NullableValueTypeCoalesceCollector`) gated on the operand's static `ClrType`. Open type parameters have no `ClrType`, so every shape over an open T fell through to the bottom of `EmitBinary`/`EmitUnary` and produced:

- `ldarg.0; ldnull; ceq` for `self == nil` — `[StackUnexpected]: found Nullobjref ... expected value 'T'`
- `dup; brtrue` for `self ?: rhs` — `Unexpected type on the stack` for `dup` over an opaque `!!T`
- `dup; brtrue` for `self!!` — same root cause

## Fix (emit-only, no new BoundNodeKind)

`src/Core/CodeAnalysis/Emit/MethodBodyEmitter.Operators.cs`:

- For `T? == nil` / `!= nil` over any open-T constraint: emit `box <T?>; ldnull; ceq` (with `ldc.i4.0; ceq` for the `!=` lobe). Per ECMA-335 III.4.1, `box Nullable<T>` yields a managed-null reference when `HasValue` is `false`, so the same shape works uniformly for class-, struct-, and unconstrained-T. The JIT elides the box for reference-typed T.
- For `T? ?: rhs` over class/unconstrained T: spill the LHS to a `T`-typed slot, probe via `box !!T; brfalse fallback`, reload the slot on the non-null path.
- For `!!` over class/unconstrained T (both bare `T` and `T?` shapes): spill to a `T`-typed slot, probe via `box !!T; brtrue nonNull`, throw NRE on null, reload slot on non-null.

`src/Core/CodeAnalysis/Emit/SlotPlanner.cs`:

- Extend `NullableValueTypeUnwrapCollector` and `NullableValueTypeCoalesceCollector` to pre-allocate `!!T`-typed slots for the new open-T paths.

## Tests

New file `test/Compiler.Tests/Emit/Issue831OpenTNilCompareEmitTests.cs` (7 cases) — each compiles a sample with `gsc`, gates the PE through `IlVerifier.Verify`, and runs it under `dotnet exec` asserting stdout:

| Test | Shape covered |
| --- | --- |
| `OpenTNilCompare_ClassConstrained_RoundTrip_Verifiable` | Original `Optional.Map` repro |
| `OpenTNilCompare_ClassConstrained_NotEquals_Verifiable` | `!= nil` negation lobe |
| `OpenTNullCoalesce_ClassConstrained_Verifiable` | `self ?: defaultValue` (`OrElse`) |
| `OpenTNullAssertion_ClassConstrained_NonNull_Verifiable` | smart-cast `self!!` after guard |
| `OpenTNullAssertion_ClassConstrained_NullThrows_Verifiable` | NRE preserved on null inputs |
| `OpenTNilCompare_StructConstrained_PassesIlverify` | `[T struct]` open-T `Nullable<T> == nil` |
| `OpenTNilCompare_BothOverloads_DispatchedCorrectly` | dual-overload dispatch end-to-end |

## Verification

- `dotnet test GSharp.sln` — **all 5,286 tests pass** (Core 3262, Compiler 1326, Interpreter 296, LanguageServer 266, Extensions 104, Sdk 32; 1 `RegenerateBaseline` skipped).
- `ilverify` on `Gsharp.Extensions.dll` — 8 Optional-helper errors → 0. Only the pre-existing unrelated `Sequences.Empty()` error remains (out of scope for this PR).
- `cd website && npm ci && npm run build` — clean build, no broken links.

## Links

Closes #831
Related: #806 (SDK migration that surfaced the gap), ADR-0084, parent #706

author: alan-thegentleman
body:
Closes #498

## Type

Bug fix (`type:bug`)

## Summary

- `resolveEngramCommand()` no longer bakes a versioned Homebrew/Linuxbrew Cellar path (e.g. `.../Cellar/engram/1.16.1/bin/engram`) into MCP client configs.
- When the resolved executable points into a versioned Cellar directory, it maps to the stable `<brew-prefix>/bin/engram` symlink (which brew keeps current), falling back to bare `engram` when that symlink is missing.
- Non-Cellar absolute paths are preserved unchanged.

## Why

After `brew upgrade engram` the old Cellar version directory is removed, so OpenCode/Codex fail to spawn the engram MCP server with `ENOENT: posix_spawn`. On Linux `os.Executable()` reads `/proc/self/exe`, which is already fully resolved to the Cellar path, so dropping `EvalSymlinks` alone does not help — the Cellar path must be explicitly detected and mapped back to the stable symlink.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `internal/setup/setup.go` | Add `stableHomebrewEngramCommand`; map versioned Cellar paths to the stable brew bin symlink; corrected doc comment |
| `internal/setup/setup_test.go` | Add `TestResolveEngramCommandHomebrewCellar` (linuxbrew, macOS arm/intel, missing-symlink fallback, non-Cellar preserved) |

## Test Plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go test ./internal/setup/` — all pass, including existing `TestResolveEngramCommand`
- [x] New table test covers each Cellar prefix and the fallback paths

## Context

Originally reported against gentle-ai (Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai#863), but gentle-ai already migrates Cellar paths in `opencode.json` and never writes `opencode.jsonc`. The real source of the versioned path is engram setup, fixed here.

## Checklist

- [x] Linked an approved issue
- [x] Exactly one `type:*` label
- [x] Conventional commit format
- [x] No `Co-Authored-By` trailers

author: cyberlife-coder
body:
## What & why

`VelesQL` `WITH (ef_search = N)` was **lossily coarsened** into one of four named `SearchQuality` buckets by **three byte-identical bracket `match` blocks** (`search_with_ef`, `search_with_opts`, `resolve_quality`). So `ef_search = 200` silently became `Accurate` (ef ≈ 512), and any value `> 512` became `Perfect` (brute-force) — breaking the documented contract (`CONFIGURATION.md`) that `N` is the requested search budget, and only honored exactly via the string form `mode = 'custom:N'`.

## Change (DRY / KISS / surgical)

- Add **one** value-preserving helper `ef_to_quality(N) -> SearchQuality::Custom(N)` in `vector_filter.rs`.
- Reroute the **3 duplicated bracket sites** to it, eliminating the duplication.
- `Custom(_)` already shares `Accurate`'s high-recall rerank gate, so the change is **recall-safe by construction**.
- **Unchanged**: default-`Balanced` (no ef, no mode) and the `explicit mode > ef_search > default` precedence. The config-level SSOT `VelesConfig::effective_ef_search()` is untouched (already correct).

## Tests & docs

- Re-scoped the stale parity test that pinned the now-removed `ef(128) == Balanced` equivalence; it no longer asserts an invariant the change deliberately drops.
- Added targeted unit test `test_ef_to_quality_preserves_exact_value` (200 → `Custom(200)`, 64 → `Custom(64)`).
- Updated + dated the `ef_search` docs; corrected the stale Balanced default (`128` → `160`).

## Validation (local)

- `cargo clippy -p velesdb-core --features persistence --all-targets -- -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic` — clean
- **Recall Gate-1**: `recall_contract` (+ multimetric) all pass, incl. `balanced_mode_gte_95`
- `search_with` suite (56 tests) + new unit test — all pass

## Out of scope (flagged)

`VelesConfig::effective_ef_search()` is orphaned at query time (Collection/Database never read the global `[search]` config) — same pattern as the dropped item C; wiring it changes the recall-critical default path and reconciles two enum systems (architectural), so it is intentionally **not** in this PR.

author: blute
body:
## Lucee-compat / performance gap

Lucee's JDBC datasource pool does **not** run a liveness query on checkout by default (`validate` defaults off), so a `cfquery` is **one** round-trip to the server.

RustCFML's Postgres pool (`r2d2` `PostgresConnectionManager`) leaves r2d2's `test_on_check_out` at its default (**true**), and `is_valid` is implemented as:

```rust
// crates/cfml-stdlib/src/builtins.rs  (~6526)
fn is_valid(&self, conn) -> ... {
    conn.simple_query("SELECT 1").map(|_| ())...
}
```

Because a connection is checked out **per query** (`execute_postgres` → `pool.get()` per `cfquery`, ~7424), **every** `cfquery` fires an extra `SELECT 1` before the real statement → **two round-trips per query**. Against a remote DB (e.g. Neon) this roughly **doubles** request latency versus Lucee on the *same* database. (Found while comparing two Moopa apps on one Neon instance — the Lucee app was ~2× faster purely from this.)

## Test

Adds `tests/tags/test_pg_pool_checkout_validation.cfm`, gated on `RUSTCFML_TEST_PG_URL` **and** the presence of `pg_stat_statements` (the only CFML-observable signal for an internal pool ping). After a stats reset it runs one structurally-distinct marker query, then asserts **zero** bare `SELECT 1` (normalized `SELECT $1`) calls were recorded.

Run locally:
```bash
docker run --rm -d -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres postgres:16 \
  -c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements
RUSTCFML_TEST_PG_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres \
  cargo run -- tests/runner.cfm
```

**RED on stock v0.149.0** — records **2** validation calls after a single `cfquery`:
```
FAIL | PostgreSQL pool checkout validation
   FAIL: PG pool must not ping SELECT 1 on checkout (Lucee parity);
         recorded 2 validation query call(s) after one cfquery
```

## Suggested engine fix (yours to make)

One line in `get_postgres_pool`'s builder (`crates/cfml-stdlib/src/builtins.rs` ~6719):

```rust
r2d2::Pool::builder()
    .max_size(10)
    .min_idle(Some(1))
    .connection_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
    .test_on_check_out(false)   // <-- don't ping on every checkout
    .build(mgr)
```

`has_broken()` already returns `false`; with validation off, a connection killed server-side surfaces on the next real statement instead of costing a round-trip on every checkout. (If you'd rather detect dead connections without the per-checkout cost, `has_broken` / an `idle`-recycle is the usual r2d2 route.)

Test-only PR — no engine changes here.

author: alii13
body:
## Why

Server-side fetch can't see content behind a login, so X and Reddit saves fall back to URL-only (and the existing limitation note even says so). But when you save on a Mac, the page is already rendered in your authenticated browser tab - so capture it there instead. This recovers real tweet/thread and Reddit-post content for the sources recall is weakest on.

## What

**Server (`@recall/api` + `@recall/shared`):**
- `/save` accepts an optional `text` field.
- `processCard` uses provided text directly and **skips extraction** when present - the only place the login wall can be bypassed.
- New pure `providedContent()` helper in `@recall/shared` (builds extracted content from the text, derives a title), with 5 unit tests (TDD).

**Mac client (`scripts/recall-capture.sh`):**
- Reads the clipboard URL; when a browser's **active tab matches that URL**, grabs the tab's rendered text via AppleScript and posts `{url, text}`. Non-matching saves (a link copied from Slack/Notion) send URL-only, unchanged.
- X: captures the author's **full self-thread** by author-handle match, excluding other people's replies. Tweet/Reddit text is pulled from the post container, not whole-page chrome.
- `--check` reports the per-browser "Allow JavaScript from Apple Events" setting. When a matching tab is found but the setting is off, a notification fires so the URL-only downgrade is never silent.
- `RECALL_HOST` (env or `.env`) for the client host.

**Docs:** new "Recall - mac with tab text" section + updated limitations.

## Verification

- `@recall/shared` typecheck + 25 unit tests pass; `@recall/api` typecheck passes; biome format clean on touched files; `bash -n` clean.
- End-to-end against a live tweet (8-tweet self-thread captured, no stranger replies) and a live Reddit post (main post, not the 26 recommended ones), plus the URL-only fallback, wrong-tab safety rail, and non-URL refusal.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `note` is stored but never fed to the summarizer (the README implied it was) - separate fix if wanted.
- One manual step the GUI requires: point the `Recall - mac` Shortcut at the script (README has the steps).

**What type of PR is this?**

**What this PR does / why we need it:**
This PR comprehensively remediates all six bugs documented in the GAN + Self-Taught Learning Unseen Task Processing benchmark report, restoring the scientific validity of its metrics and allowing the example to run on environments other than the original developer's machine.

Changes implemented:
- **BUG-5 (Scientific Integrity):** Added the missing `imgs = encoder(imgs)` call to the validation loop in `deeplabv3/train.py`, ensuring the validation distribution matches the training distribution.
- **BUG-4 (Domain Transfer Disclosure):** Added an explicit "Scientific Validity Notes" section to the `README.md` documenting that the STL encoder is trained on synthetic images but evaluated on real images, and added a corresponding inline comment in `selftaughtlearning/train.py`.
- **BUG-6 (Hardcoded Pretrained Backbone):** Replaced 7 hardcoded absolute paths to local ResNet checkpoints (`/home/nailtu/...` and `/root/...`) in `deeplabv3/model/resnet.py` with a configurable `_maybe_load_weights` helper that supports environment variables and falls back safely to random initialization.

author: roelvangils
body:
## Problem

When streaming a remote macOS app, a tiny generic window briefly
appears as its own floating "mini-window" over the real app window.

On macOS 26's Calculator it's a **66×20 window titled `"Window"`** that
the app maps during launch. It isn't a one-frame flash — it *persists*
in the `SCShareableContent` list for the whole session, so it stays
streamed (and rendered as a separate sub-window by the client) the
entire time.

## Cause

`apply_content` already filters to `windowLayer == 0` and a 16×16 floor,
but that 66×20 placeholder clears both bars, so it's tracked like a real
window.

## Fix

Also drop windows that are **both** small (`<120w` or `<60h`) **and**
lack a meaningful title (empty, or the generic AppKit `"Window"`):

```objc
bool generic_title = title.length == 0 || [title isEqualToString:@"Window"];
if (generic_title &&
    (scw.frame.size.width < 120 || scw.frame.size.height < 60)) continue;
```

Real dialogs and palettes carry a title (or are larger), and any
properly-titled / large window streams unchanged — the heuristic only
catches the small-and-nameless transients.

## Testing

Instrumented `apply_content` to log each candidate window, then ran
Calculator via `sketerm app localhost …`:

```
KEEP    win=2679 230x408 title="Calculator"
FILTER  win=2682 66x20   title="Window"
```

(repeated every poll cycle — confirming the placeholder persists and is
suppressed each time). Main window streams normally; the mini-window is
gone. Verified visually in the client. Apple Silicon, macOS 26.5,
Zig 0.16.0.

author: pablof7z
body:
## TLDR

Download deletion is now transactional with Rust's downloaded projection: failed filesystem deletes keep the episode marked as downloaded, and the failure is surfaced in episode Diagnostics.

## Overview

### Root cause

`handle_delete_download` cleared the store's local download path before attempting `std::fs::remove_file`, then ignored delete errors. The auto-delete-after-played paths used the same mutation-before-delete pattern through `clear_local_path_if_auto_delete`.

That meant a file deletion failure could make Rust project an episode as not downloaded even though the local file was still present, including after restart when the store projection was restored from Rust state.

### What changed

- Added a shared download delete helper that removes the file first and only clears `local_paths` / size metadata on successful deletion or `NotFound` stale-path cleanup.
- Updated explicit delete-download, audio `ItemEnd`, and `inbox/mark_listened` auto-delete paths to use the same transactional helper.
- Added `download.delete_failed` audit events and Swift rendering metadata so failed deletes are visible in Diagnostics.
- Replaced the store auto-delete helper with a read-only delete candidate resolver, preserving the setting gate while avoiding pre-delete state mutation.
- Added focused Rust coverage for explicit delete success, stale missing paths, delete failure retention, and auto-delete failure retention.
- Updated `docs/BACKLOG.md` for `download-state-projection` and added a whats-new entry.

## Validation

```bash
git diff --check
jq empty App/Resources/whats-new.json
cargo check -p nmp-app-podcast --lib
```

Not run: Swift/iOS xcodebuild, because the Swift change only adds display metadata for a new audit-event kind and the resource change is validated with `jq empty`.

The focused unit-test commands currently cannot run because the repo's `nmp-app-podcast` lib test target has pre-existing compile failures against the pinned NMP API:

```bash
cargo test -p nmp-app-podcast download_delete --lib
cargo test -p nmp-app-podcast item_end_auto_delete_failure_keeps_download_state --lib
```

Both fail before executing these tests with the existing `ActorCommand::DispatchHostOp`, `ActionModule::execute` arity, `TypedProjectionData` field, and `SnapshotUpdateSignal::new` API drift errors. This is separate from the broader CI path-dependency blocker tracked in #479.

## Decisions / Tradeoffs

- Treat `remove_file` `NotFound` as successful stale cleanup so old local-path mappings can be cleared when the file is already gone.
- Keep other filesystem errors as failures: the local path remains projected as downloaded, and Diagnostics gets the file path plus error string.
- `tuist generate` was not run because no project shape, target membership, package, entitlement, or generated Xcode state changed.

author: sidhasadhak
body:
Closes the **last of the five product directions** (#4). The 5 backends were already wired (Ollama, LM Studio, Groq, Together, Anthropic) but config was **env-only and process-global** — you had to edit `.env` and restart to switch. Now a user can choose & change the provider, models, base URLs and API keys **at runtime**.

## Backend — a config layer with clean precedence (runtime → env → default)

`aughor/llm/provider.py` gains a runtime config so headless/CI runs stay unchanged:
- `data/llm_config.json` (gitignored, `chmod 600`) holds backend / models / base_urls + API **keys, secretvault-encrypted**. `current_config()` returns a **secret-free** view — keys reported as set/not-set, never the value.
- `get_provider(role)` is unchanged for its **34 call sites**; it now rebuilds its cache on a config **version bump**, so model *and* backend changes take effect live (previously only a backend change flushed the cache).
- when a backend is explicitly chosen, env model-overrides (tuned for the env backend) **no longer leak across** — an unset model uses that backend's own default (this fixed a 404 when probing a different backend).

## API
- `GET /llm/config` · `POST /llm/config` (merge: `""` clears, masked = unchanged) · `POST /llm/config/test` (a tiny **real** completion to validate a backend with its saved/env key).

## UI
An **Inference** panel in Settings — provider dropdown, conditional API-key (write-only, "configured" indicator) / base-URL fields, per-role models with default placeholders, **Save** + **Test connection**.

## Proof (real path)
The UI switches to **Groq**, the key field appears, and **Test connection** runs a live completion → **"✓ Groq responded (llama-3.3-70b-versatile)"** (screenshot in the session). **7 unit tests** (precedence, key encrypt/mask, cache invalidation, clear-to-default); full unit suite green (**770 passed**). No secrets are logged or returned.

author: lathrys-at
body:
## Summary

Two caller-input-driven sinks raised a plain exception that hit `_safe_tool`'s catch-all (`logger.exception("Unhandled error in …")` → ERROR + traceback, and a leaked parse detail) instead of the house rule for expected bad input (`ToolInputError` → WARNING, no traceback):

1. **Malformed `modified_since`** — `datetime.fromisoformat(...)` raised a bare `ValueError` (with the leaky "Invalid isoformat string" message) at `actions.py` (the `list_notes` action) and at its duplicate in `collection.py`.
2. **Invalid regex/backref in `find_replace_notes`** — `re.sub` in `apply_replacement` (`collection.py`) raised `re.error`, reached via the action. The dry-run preview loop compiles the pattern on **every** call, including a real apply, so this bit applies too, not only `dry_run`.

## Changes

- `src/shrike/actions.py`
  - `list_notes`: wrap the `modified_since` parse in `try/except ValueError` → `ToolInputError` with a clean, non-leaky message.
  - `find_replace_notes`: wrap the `wrapper.find_replace(...)` call in `try/except re.error` → `ToolInputError`. (`re` now imported.)
- `src/shrike/collection.py`
  - `CollectionWrapper.list_notes`: the lower layer (no `ToolInputError` import by design) re-raises a clean, non-leaky `ValueError` the tool layer translates, replacing `fromisoformat`'s leaky message.

The catch is narrow at each sink (the specific `ValueError`/`re.error`), not a blanket `except` — genuine bugs still fall through to the catch-all with a traceback. This mirrors the sibling `collection_query` action, which already maps a malformed search expression to `ToolInputError`.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/test_tools_list_notes.py` (new) — `test_malformed_modified_since_is_clean_input_error` (asserts no "Unhandled error" log record) + `test_valid_modified_since_is_accepted`.
- `tests/unit/test_tools_find_replace.py` — `test_invalid_regex_is_clean_input_error` added to `TestValidation`.

Both bad-input tests are adapted from the audit repros `s3_modified_since.py` / `s3_bad_regex.py`: they fail before the fix (catch-all logs "Unhandled error" + traceback) and pass after.

Fixes #599.

body:
## Summary

A no-change re-scan of an already-imported corpus was doing a lot of pointless work — re-reading every transcript, importing each subagent file twice, and deleting + reinserting unchanged rows (churning the FTS index). This skips that work: parents are recognized as already-imported from their filename before the file is read, subagent files carry an mtime guard so unchanged ones are skipped, batch flows drop subagent files whose parent is in the same batch, and title extraction is folded into the single parse pass so each transcript is read at most once.

## Linked issue

Closes #87

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Build / CI / tooling
- [ ] Tests only

## Affected area

- [x] Ingestion (JSONL parsing, transcript import, watcher)
- [ ] Dashboard UI (session list, timeline, context chart, agent tree)
- [ ] CLI (`start`, `import`, `status` commands)
- [ ] Analysis (compaction detection, token tracking, agent efficiency)
- [x] Database (SQLite schema, migrations, queries)
- [ ] Build & CI

## Test plan

- `npm run build` — tsup + vite both succeed
- `npm test` — 568 pass (8 new in `test/ingestion/transcript-importer.test.ts`)
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- New tests cover the matrix from the issue: event-`id` stability across a no-force re-import (proves no delete+reinsert), filename≠sessionId fallback, standalone unchanged-subagent skip, changed-subagent re-import, `filterCoveredSubagents` drop + no-dupe batch, and fresh-vs-`--force` result equality.

## How to validate

1. `git checkout claude/dev-flow-87-hmys1w && npm install && npm run build`
2. `npm test` — expect green; the new cases live under `transcript-importer.test.ts` (`skip/dedupe matrix`).
3. `node dist/index.js import` against an already-imported `~/.claude/projects/` — expect every line to print `⊘ … (already imported)` and finish in well under a second with `0 imported`.
4. `node dist/index.js import --force <same path>` — confirms forced re-import still rewrites everything (events present, counts unchanged).
5. Regression check: open the dashboard (`node dist/index.js start`) and confirm an existing session's Timeline + Agents tabs render unchanged.

## Risk / rollout notes

- Adds **migration 015** (`agent_relationships.child_imported_mtime REAL`) — idempotent, guarded `run()` (mirrors migration 014); applies once on first DB open.
- Touches the hot import path (`src/ingestion/transcript-importer.ts`, `jsonl-parser.ts`) and `POST /api/reimport`, which now routes through the shared `importTranscripts` batch (subagent dedupe applies there too). No API contract change — `/api/reimport` still returns `{ imported, errors }`.
- The parent skip-before-parse trusts `basename === sessionId` (the Claude Code transcript layout) for the fast path, with the existing post-parse `sessionExists` check as the correctness fallback for renamed files.
- No new dependencies. No CLI flag changes.

- [x] `npm test` passes
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] Tests added or updated for changed behavior
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under `[Unreleased]`

## Quiet Dawn — teacher home, marketing photos, filtered quote bank

Three connected pieces, all mock-driven, tokens-only, and verified across the six themes + phone.

### Teacher home — `/home` ("Quiet Dawn")
- **Crossfade photo-montage hero** (`HeroPhotos`): four warm teaching moments graded + feathered into a **theme-hued poster frame** so text holds contrast on every theme; 4 shots × 7s = a contiguous 28s cycle (no blank gap). Reduced-motion → single still; phone drops opacity + uses a surface-heavy scrim. Gated by the existing "Soft background photo" toggle.
- **Rolling attributed insight**: random per visit, categories alternate (classroom culture → learning → teaching → leading). `aria-live` stays `off` during ambient rotation and only goes `polite` on manual prev/next, so AT users aren't interrupted every interval.
- **Quote rotation settings** (topic + interval) in both the on-page Customize popover and Settings → Appearance.
- Daily-dashboard rows below the hero. Extracted the hero's themed gradient into a reusable **`<ThemeWash />`** primitive (`components/ui`).

### Marketing — `/welcome`
- New **"In real classrooms"** photo collage (feature crop + 2×2 teaching moments, rounded, hover-zoom, subtle `--grad-hero` glaze, real alt text).
- Testimonial swapped from "RM" initials to a **real teacher portrait**.

### Quote bank — `scripts/quote-mining/`
- Library-mined attributed insight bank with a strict **off-topic / controversial filter** — keep only teaching / learning / education-&-team leading / classroom management. **1,203 removed** (a 13-agent semantic review + supplemental source blocks for AI/futurism/policy sources), leaving a clean, balanced **320-quote hero pool** the app bundles (`insights.hero.json`).
- Reproducible + reversible pipeline; topic-scope limits and a removal report live in the MD ledgers (`QUOTE-SOURCES.md`, `QUOTE-REMOVALS.md`).

### Photos
15 user-supplied classroom photos optimized to `public/classroom/c00–c14.webp` (sharp, q76).

---

### Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean · `next lint` clean · **production `next build` green** (`/home` 526 B and `/welcome` 1.25 kB both prerender ○ static).
- No browser-console errors; six themes (paper/cloud/night/mint/sky/blossom) + phone width checked on both pages.
- **Code-review gate (CLAUDE.md §4a):** the Codex gate hit its ChatGPT usage limit, so per the documented fallback an **independent code-reviewer agent** (which did not author the diff) ran the adversarial review in gate format. Its findings (a quote-filter bootstrapping bug, a reset-sequence doc gap, an `aria-live` interruption, and a multi-tab storage-sync gap) were all fixed; the lone "crossfade gap" finding was a false positive (4×7=28 s is contiguous). Local verification stack ran on top.

### Notes for the reviewer
- **SideNav:** this adds a "Home" item as the first entry in the Plan group. A SideNav rewrite is in flight on another branch — if that lands first, this one line is the only expected conflict.
- **Default landing:** wiring `/home` as the post-login default (`app/(planner)/layout.tsx`) is intentionally **not** in this PR — it's a separate change.
- **Repo weight:** the raw mining inputs (`scripts/quote-mining/output/`, ~131 MB) and the full unfiltered `insights.data.json` (~5 MB) are gitignored; only the reproducible scripts, ledgers, removal lists, and the bundled 320-quote hero pool are tracked.

author: souliane
body:
Closes #2387

## Problem

The raw-merge PreToolUse gate (BLUEPRINT §17.1 invariant 8) matched the
`gh pr merge` / `glab mr merge` subcommand as a **substring anywhere in the
Bash command text**. A command that only *documented* the merge command — a
`cat >> note.md <<EOF … gh pr merge … EOF` here-doc, an `echo`/`printf` of the
phrase, or a `# gh pr merge` comment — was therefore wrongly denied on a
teatree-managed repo (same content-not-action over-block class as #1415).

## Fix

The subcommand match now flows through a new `teatree.hooks.raw_merge_detect`
leaf:

1. strip here-doc bodies (so a body line that *begins* with the phrase cannot
   land at a command position),
2. lex via the shared `teatree.hooks._shell_lexer` (comments and quoted strings
   already fall away there),
3. split into command segments and fire only when a segment's leading words are
   `gh pr merge` / `glab mr merge` — an actual invocation at a command position.

A here-doc body, a quoted argument, an `echo`/`printf` string, and a `#` comment
that merely mention the phrase no longer trip the gate. The REST-API
merge-write arm (`_is_raw_merge_api_write`) and the managed-repo carve-out
(#126) are unchanged, so **every genuine raw-merge block still fires** — the
fail-safe-on-uncertainty posture is preserved (import failure fails *closed*,
treating the command as a possible merge).

`hook_router.py` nets a small shrink (6377 → 6376 LOC, the shrink-only ratchet
stays green): the per-call `sys.path` bootstrap is extracted into one
`_teatree_src_on_path` context manager reused by the merge, safe-kill, cadence,
and slug helpers, and the duplicated effective-HTTP-method classifier is unified
into `_effective_method_is_write`.

## Tests (anti-vacuity, observed RED on pre-fix)

Driven against the real hook in a subprocess (the `--event PreToolUse` harness),
plus a fast pure-logic unit suite on the leaf:

- `test_heredoc_documenting_merge_is_allowed` — a here-doc that documents the
  merge command is allowed (**RED on pre-fix**: it was denied).
- `test_merge_phrase_in_comment_is_allowed` — the phrase inside a `#` comment is
  allowed (**RED on pre-fix**: it was denied).
- `test_echo_of_merge_phrase_is_allowed` — an `echo` of the phrase is allowed
  (also RED on pre-fix).
- `test_real_raw_merge_is_still_blocked` — an actual `gh pr merge` on a managed
  repo is **still denied** (regression guard: green before and after).

The leaf unit test covers the adversarial here-doc-body-begins-with-phrase case,
double-space/tab variants, and the REST-API form (handled by the separate arm).

## Architecture pre-check — #2387

### 1. BLUEPRINT § alignment
§17.1 invariant 8 (out-of-band merge blocked on teatree-managed repos). The
invariant's *intent* is unchanged — only the matcher is made action-aware so it
stops over-blocking documentation of the command.

### 2. FSM phase boundaries
n/a — no `Ticket.State` / `Worktree.State` transition.

### 3. Extension-point contracts
n/a — no `OverlayBase` / scanner / hook-router-registration surface changed; the
handler registration (`handle_block_out_of_band_merge`) is untouched.

### 4. Component boundaries
Detection logic lives in a `src/teatree/hooks/` leaf (cohesive with the shared
`_shell_lexer` it consumes); `hooks/scripts/hook_router.py` keeps only the thin
gate glue. Matches the existing `safe_kill_detect` sibling pattern.

### 5. Dependency direction
`raw_merge_detect` imports only `teatree.hooks._shell_lexer` (same package,
lower-level). hook_router imports the leaf lazily. `uv run tach check` passes.

### 6. Test surface
`tests/teatree_hooks/test_raw_merge_detect.py` (pure logic, 100% leaf coverage)
+ `tests/test_out_of_band_merge_action_aware_subprocess.py` (real hook,
cross-cutting). Each behaviour has a named assertion; the over-block fixes were
observed RED on the pre-fix matcher.

### 7. Resilience invariants
Pure detection, no external write. The gate fails **closed** on any import error
(treats the command as a possible merge → the cwd-managed check then blocks on
uncertainty), preserving the never-weaken posture.

### 8. Identity and key normalization
n/a — no bare-vs-qualified identity. Matching is positional (command-segment
leading words), not a strip-to-compare.

### 9. Behavior preservation / capability deletion
The matcher is **narrowed** (substring → action-aware), but the safety coverage
is *not* weakened: every real raw-merge invocation still blocks, the REST-API
arm and the #126 carve-out are byte-for-byte unchanged, and the existing
must-block regression tests stay green (none inverted). The narrowing only
removes false positives on documentation of the command.

author: hanzei
body:
Background read-syncs (notes, labels, users) treated local SQLite as the
source of truth and refreshed from the server in a one-shot useEffect that
swallowed transient failures, leaving stale data on screen until the next
mount/reconnect/foreground trigger.

Add a small retry/backoff helper (src/utils/retryWithBackoff.ts) and wire it
into the background fetches so a transient failure re-attempts a few times
before giving up, while keeping the local cache as the fallback. Following
mobile/CLAUDE.md "Sync Loop Safety": exponential backoff (1s base, 60s cap),
a capped number of attempts, retries that stop when offline and resume on
reconnect, and cooperative cancellation on teardown.

- retrySync: exponential backoff over a cancellable SyncCanceller sleep;
  retries only transient errors (network/timeout/429/5xx). A 401 is treated
  as permanent (the response interceptor clears the session and redirects to
  login, so retrying would only fire doomed authenticated requests).
- useOfflineNotes / useOfflineNote / useLabels' useBackgroundSyncQuery /
  UsersContext.loadUsers now fetch via retrySync, gated on connectivity and

body:
- root cause (issue #46): 99% of the positive reward was earnable while standing still, so the policy learned to lift feet one-at-a-time IN PLACE and never translated -- it looked like a crawl but went nowhere
- gate crawl_gait on forward velocity (clamp(fwd_vel/0.15, 0, 1)) so the one-at-a-time pattern only pays while the body is actually moving
- promote forward_progress from scale 4 to 15 as the primary objective (linear in real velocity, no standstill payout)
- reduce lin_vel 4 to 2 and feet_air_time 0.5 to 1 (both were farmable in place)
- net effect: walking forward now earns ~6x standing still, vs the inverted ratio before
- actuator unchanged (stays explicit IdealPD on main); this is purely the reward rebalance
- closes #46

author: veera-bharath
body:
## Summary
- Adds a `toggle:pause` output kind, selectable as "Toggle pause" in the action dropdown for any mouse gesture or keyboard combo.
- When fired, flips a global `IsPaused` flag on the daemon.
- While paused, `MouseCallback` passes all mouse input through untouched (clean for gaming/recording/screen-sharing). `KbdCallback` also passes everything through untouched, except keyboard bindings mapped to `toggle:pause` are still checked so the user can resume.
- Resume is keyboard-only by design — detecting a paused mouse gesture would require running the full timer-based gesture state machine, which would swallow/delay mouse clicks during pause.
- Visible indicator: a "⏸ Paused" badge appears next to the hook status in the main window when the daemon is running and paused (polled via `pause.state` file written by the daemon).

Closes #32

## Tasks from the issue
- [x] `toggle:pause` in `ActionKind`/`ActionLabels`/`ActionOrder` (`StandardActions`) + `DetectAction` disambiguation
- [x] PS-side parsing in `ShortcutHook.ps1`'s binding-build loop
- [x] `IsPaused` static flag + branch in `ExecuteBinding`/`ExecuteStep`
- [x] `KbdCallback`/`MouseCallback` short-circuit to pass-through when paused, with `toggle:pause` keyboard bindings still evaluated
- [x] Visible paused-state indicator in main window

## Test plan
- [ ] Build `ShortcutHookUI` and confirm "Toggle pause" appears in the action dropdown for both mouse gestures and keyboard combos
- [ ] Bind a keyboard combo (e.g. `Ctrl+Alt+P`) to "Toggle pause", start the daemon, fire it — confirm other bindings stop firing and the "⏸ Paused" badge appears
- [ ] Fire the same combo again — confirm bindings resume and the badge disappears
- [ ] While paused, confirm mouse clicks/gestures pass through to the OS/apps untouched

author: chrisworkgit
body:
Beschreibung
Dieser Pull Request führt eine automatisierte Build-Pipeline mittels GitHub Actions ein. Ziel ist es, den manuellen Aufwand für die Erstellung von Release-APK-Dateien zu eliminieren und eine einfache, tag-basierte Verteilung von Versionen zu ermöglichen.

Wichtige Änderungen
Workflow: Neue Datei .github/workflows/android-release.yml für automatisierte APK-Builds.

Trigger: Die Pipeline wird bei jedem Push eines Tags mit dem Muster v* (z. B. v1.0.0) ausgelöst.

Prozess:

Setup: Ubuntu-Environment mit Java 17.

Build: Gradle-Task assembleRelease.

Deployment: Dynamische Umbenennung der APK mit Git-Commit-Hash und automatisches Hochladen als GitHub Release.

Cleanup: Integration des Commit-Hash-Tagging direkt in der CI-Pipeline (löst Probleme mit dem Gradle-Configuration-Cache).

Vorteile
Effizienz: Kein manuelles Bauen oder Hochladen der APKs erforderlich.

Nachvollziehbarkeit: Jedes Release ist durch den Tag und die Git-Historie exakt einem Code-Stand zugeordnet.

Stabilität: Git-Befehle werden nun sicher in der CI-Umgebung statt während der Gradle-Konfiguration ausgeführt.

Test-Anweisungen
Diesen Branch mergen oder direkt testen.

Einen Test-Tag setzen und pushen:

Bash
git tag v0.1.0-test
git push origin v0.1.0-test
Im GitHub-Reiter "Actions" prüfen, ob der Workflow erfolgreich durchläuft.

Nach Abschluss unter "Releases" die generierte APK prüfen.

author: necoweb3
body:
## Summary

This makes TUI-created session artifacts use the active session profile's Hermes home instead of the gateway process' launch Hermes home. Profile-bound sessions now store uploaded images, clipboard images, rendered PDF pages, and collapsed paste files under that profile.

## Why

The TUI gateway can host sessions bound to different Hermes profiles, and the normal session state already tracks `profile_home`. However, artifact-producing shortcuts still wrote to the process-global `_hermes_home`:

- `clipboard.paste` wrote clipboard screenshots to the launch profile's `images/`.
- `image.attach_bytes` and PDF page rendering used `_queue_attached_image()`, which also wrote to the launch profile's `images/`.
- `paste.collapse` wrote large paste files to the launch profile's `pastes/`.
- The TUI frontend did not send `session_id` with `paste.collapse`, so the backend could not scope collapsed paste files even if it wanted to.

In a multi-profile TUI/Desktop/dashboard session, that places user-provided artifacts in the wrong profile, breaks profile isolation, and can leave later prompts referencing files outside the active profile's artifact area.

## Changes

- Add a small `_session_home()` helper that prefers `session["profile_home"]` and falls back to `_hermes_home`.
- Use the session home for TUI clipboard image artifacts.
- Use the session home for byte-uploaded images and rendered PDF page images.
- Use the session home for collapsed paste files when a `session_id` is provided.
- Send the active `session_id` from the TUI frontend when calling `paste.collapse`.
- Add regression tests for profile-scoped image upload, clipboard paste, and paste collapse storage.

## Tests

```text
python -m pytest tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "artifact_home or paste_collapse or attach_bytes" -q --timeout-method=thread
8 passed, 266 deselected
```

Not run:

```text
npm run typecheck
```

`npm run typecheck` failed in this checkout because `tsc` is not installed/available in `ui-tui`.

author: jravas
body:
## Problem

`GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot trigger downstream workflow runs (GitHub's recursion prevention). Since `release-please.yml` switched from the GitHub App token to `GITHUB_TOKEN` in b8fef79, every release created by release-please silently skipped the `publish.yml` workflow — v0.3.0, v0.4.0, and v0.5.0 all failed to auto-publish. v0.5.0 was only shipped manually.

## Fix

Move the publish steps into `release-please.yml` as a second job (`publish`) gated on the action's `release_created` output. Because it runs within the same workflow invocation, the `GITHUB_TOKEN` restriction does not apply.

`publish.yml` is kept but stripped down to `workflow_dispatch` only — a manual escape hatch.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge this PR
- [ ] Confirm next release-please PR merge runs both `release-please` and `publish` jobs
- [ ] Confirm `publish` job is skipped on pushes that don't cut a release

author: avifenesh
body:
## Summary

Makes `websearch` **self-contained / zero-config** and substantially improves how it serves results to a model. Previously the tool hard-failed without a session-configured SearXNG URL; now it works out of the box with **no API key and no self-hosted service**, via a bundled keyless fallback chain. Implemented in **both** TypeScript (`@agent-sh/harness-websearch` → 0.4.x) and Rust (`harness-websearch`), kept at parity throughout.

Backend choices were made from **first-hand live probes** (not assumptions): Mojeek, Marginalia, and Wikipedia work keyless today; DuckDuckGo is 202+captcha from datacenter IPs and is deliberately excluded.

## What changed

**Zero-config keyless default**
- Bundled engines behind the existing `WebSearchEngine` interface: Mojeek (HTML SERP), Marginalia (public JSON API), Wikipedia (MediaWiki JSON), plus keyed Brave/Tavily and the existing SearXNG.
- `resolveEngine(session)` builds the chain: explicit override → Brave/Tavily (key) → SearXNG (url) → keyless tail (Mojeek→Marginalia→Wikipedia). An explicit backend is **exclusive by default** (a SearXNG hiccup shouldn't leak queries to public scrapers); `fallbackToKeyless` opts in.
- **Breaking**: the "no search backend configured" `INVALID_PARAM` is gone — zero config now just works.

**Token-efficient, model-friendly output** (researched the LLM-facing search APIs; Tavily/Brave/Anthropic/Exa converge on compact ranked text)
- Replaced the multi-line `<search>` XML block with one `WEB "query" · engine (class) · N results` header + 3-line entries (~410→~335 tokens at count=5). Snippet cap 300→240, session-tunable.
- **Quality signal**: engine coverage class in the header (`general web` / `indie/small-web index` / `encyclopedic`) so the model can tell broad-web from a niche/encyclopedic fallback.
- **Honest recency**: per-result `age` only when the backend provides it (Brave/Tavily/Wikipedia), never fabricated; and when an engine ignores `time_range`, the header says `time:week NOT applied` instead of mislabeling all-time results as filtered.

**Robust fallback + ranking**
- Gather-and-merge with a **sufficiency threshold** (don't stop at a 1-hit leader when 5 were asked for) and **cross-engine dedupe** by normalized URL.
- **Engine-class-aware empty/degraded**: a general engine's empty is authoritative; a niche/vertical-only empty while a general engine *errored* is treated as degraded (error), not a misleading "no results".
- Rate-limit/bot-block (401/403/429) → `SERVER_NOT_AVAILABLE` (skip + continue), never `INVALID_PARAM`.
- Per-engine timeout slices so one slow backend can't starve the chain.
- **RRF + engine weights** for merge ranking (`fused = Σ weight(e)/(K+rank_e)`, K=10) — A/B-validated (`scripts/ab-rank*.mjs`). Gives a consensus boost when engines agree and keeps a backstop from outranking broad web. Honest scope (WS-D19): in the keyless default the fast path usually skips merging and the backends rarely overlap, so day-to-day impact is small; the real value is robust weighting + consensus for keyed/multi-engine setups. Semantic/LLM rerank left as a deferred opt-in hook.

## Validation

- **Unit/integration**: TS **130** tests, Rust **63** tests, clippy clean, umbrella `@agent-sh/harness-tools` + `@agent-sh/harness-e2e` typecheck. Engines tested against saved real-response fixtures.
- **Live**: verified zero-config search, fallback, gibberish→empty, and the merge/dedupe path end to end.
- **Real-model e2e**: full `websearch.e2e.hard.test.ts` suite — **10/10 on the TS engine and 10/10 on the Rust engine** against Claude Opus (Bedrock). New hermetic-fixture tests cover zero-config (WS7), keyless-empty (WS8), honest-recency (WS9), and cross-engine merge (WS10); the 6 original SearXNG-path tests are kept.

## Notes / follow-ups

- Decision log in `agent-knowledge/design/websearch.md` (WS-D7..D19) records every call and the honest caveats.
- The text rendering is explicitly **not** part of the stability contract — consumers should parse `meta`/`results`, not the `output` string.
- Not run here (needs the local Ollama box): the qwen/gemma multi-model baseline matrix. The suite is ready for it.

author: sirus20x6
body:
## Problem

Star/system names, spectral types, the program name (`argv[0]`), and catalogue designations flow into output **unescaped**. A value containing `'` `"` `<` `>` `&` or a newline corrupts or injects into the generated files. This matters now that names / `desig` / `spec_type` load **verbatim from `data/*.tsv`** (PR #37) — and real-star catalogues commonly contain apostrophes (*Barnard's Star*). The JSON path is already safe (nlohmann escapes).

## Fix

Four escape helpers in `utils`, each a **no-op on strings without special characters** (so default + shipped-catalogue output is byte-identical):

| Helper | Context | Transform |
|---|---|---|
| `escapeXmlText` | HTML element text, SVG/XML text | `& < >` → entities |
| `escapeXmlAttr` | HTML/XML attribute values | `& < > " '` → entities |
| `escapeCsvField` | inside single-quoted CSV fields | `'` → `''`, CR/LF → space |
| `escapeCelestiaId` | Celestia double-quoted identifiers (no backslash escape in its parser) | `"` → `'`, CR/LF → space |

Routed through every user-controlled emission site:
- **CSV** — star-header name/spec-type fields + the reflective row emitter (`PlanetRow.h emit_csv_row`, covering `Planet #` and `Atmosphere`). JSON emitter untouched.
- **HTML** — `<title>`, `<meta generator>`, spec-type `<td>`, thumbnail name/links, `url_path`/`system_url`/`svg_url` attributes, **and the `-L` list-as-HTML `<option>` emitter in `stargen.cpp`**. Fixed strings (`type_string`, gas `getHtmlSymbol` markup, the `°`-bearing `info` titles) deliberately left raw.
- **SVG** — `<title>`/`<desc>`.
- **CELESTIA** — designation quoted identifier + comment line.

Scope discovered via a per-format fan-out; correctness gated by an adversarial review (4 lenses). The review caught the `stargen.cpp` `-L` emitter the first pass missed (now fixed); over-escaping, byte-identity, and escaper-implementation lenses were clean.

## Verification

vs. clean master (both `-O3`):
- **Byte-identical** default output: random-gen JSON/CSV/HTML/SVG × 3 seeds (**81 files**) + Andromeda-catalogue CSV + CELESTIA (path-normalized) + `-L` (6018 lines).
- **Escaping confirmed** with name `A'B"C<D>E&F` → HTML/SVG `< > &`→entities, `'"` raw (correct for text); CSV `'`→`''`; CELESTIA `"`→`'`.
- `scripts/verify.sh`: **9/9 ctest pass**.

The dead (commented-out) moongen path is left for card-3058109c.

## What

On the GitHub workflow-generator page, when **build type = Static**, hide the **Environment variables** and **Env groups** inputs, and omit them from the generated workflow YAML.

## Why

Static deployments serve a release from the edge and have no pod, so env vars and env groups don't apply — the apiserver zeroes `Env`/`EnvGroups` for static deployments. Showing the inputs (and emitting them into the workflow) is misleading and would be ignored/rejected downstream. This matches how the detail page already hides env/envGroups for static.

## How

- Wrapped the env / env-group / pull-secret grid in a single `{#if gen.buildType === 'dockerfile'}` guard, folding in the pull-secret block's existing identical conditional (so all three container-only fields share one guard).
- Gated the `env` / `envGroups` lines in `withBlock()` on `buildType === 'dockerfile'` so they never leak into the generated YAML even if values were typed before switching to Static. `workingDirectory` stays (it applies to static builds too).

Most of the diff is re-indentation from un-nesting the pull-secret block; the behavioral change is the two guards.

`bun lint` and `bun check` pass clean.
