author: tsenoner
body:
Fixes the green-dot / missing-final-data bug, the missing-seed gaps, and the empty historical-Elo lens — all by re-sourcing data from Jeff Sackmann's CSVs through the existing exact name-join, plus a status-heuristic fix so the app boots into the latest tournament.

Closes #19. Closes #20.

## What was wrong

- **Green dot + missing data** (US 2021, AO 2021, US 2020 + WTA RG 2021, WTA AO 2019): five finals shipped as `status:"scheduled"` with no winner/score. `slamStatus` fell through to `"live"`, so the app booted into **US Open 2021** showing a *projected* champion (Djokovic).
- **Seeds**: 14 slams (2015/2022/2024 clusters + two single gaps) had absent or partial seeds — SofaScore's draw payload omitted them. The user's example, 2022 US, had **zero** seeds.
- **Historical Elo** (#20): every 2009–2025 snapshot had `elo:null`; `elo.ts` only scrapes *current* Tennis Abstract ratings.

## What this does

| Area | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Finals** | New `ingest/finals.ts` parses a Sackmann F-row score (winner-perspective, oriented onto the snapshot's fixed p1/p2 slots) and fills winner/score/minutes for the 5 finals. |
| **Seeds** | New `ingest/seeds.ts` two-pass name-join (fullKey → guarded sigKey) fills `players[*].seed`. Merge-only, preserves legit <32 draws, rejects Sackmann's `33+` "notable unseeded" markers, never fabricates. |
| **Historical Elo** (#20) | New `ingest/historical-elo.ts` computes surface-aware Elo (538-style `K=250/(n+5)^0.4`, 400-scale logistic) over full Sackmann history, frozen at each slam's own start date (strict `<`, zero in-tournament drift), joined into `players[*].elo` (overall + hard/clay/grass). Keeps the Tennis Abstract scrape for the lag-prone current slam. |
| **Status / default boot** | `slamStatus(snap, now)` anchors classification to the event's calendar window (new `config.eventWindow`): a past slam with an unscraped final degrades to `complete`, never `live`. `reindex` classifies against the wall clock so the *latest* slam can't get stuck live either; `pickDefaultSlam` (unchanged) now opens the latest tournament. |

Shared name-join primitives were extracted from `durations.ts` into `ingest/names.ts` (behaviour byte-identical) so all three backfills reuse one implementation.

## Verification

- **Finals**: all 5 winners/scores/durations checked against Sackmann (Medvedev d. Djokovic 6-4 6-4 6-4, Thiem d. Zverev in 5, etc.). In-browser: US 2021 now shows Medvedev as champion with the real score; no green dot.
- **Seeds**: 2022 US → Medvedev 1 / Nadal 2 / Alcaraz 3 (WTA: Swiatek 1); all seeds in 1..32, no duplicates, no existing seed overwritten. Caught & fixed a "seed 33" bug where Sackmann encodes notable unseeded players above 32.
- **Elo** (#20 acceptance): RG 2016 ATP → **Djokovic #1 overall (2440.6) and #1 clay (2318.3), Nadal #2 clay (2303.2)**; the match-detail ELO line renders on historical matches.
- **Boot**: app now opens **RG 2026** (latest), not US Open 2021. `index.json` live count 5 → **0**.
- 313 unit tests pass; `tsc` + `vite build` clean; reindex deterministic.
- An adversarial review pass surfaced 4 latent edge-case defects (none affecting shipped data) — all hardened in the final commit (re-running the backfills leaves the data byte-identical).

## Notes

- The 113 changed `public/data` snapshots are the re-sourced data (finals + seeds + elo are disjoint fields; backfills are idempotent and never touch `generatedAt`).
- Wiring the computed Elo into the *live* ingest path (so future scrapes also get it) is a deliberate follow-up; the live path keeps the Tennis Abstract scrape for the current slam, which is correct.

body:
## What & why

The only module that touches the three tables — the layer the generation orchestrator and routes will call.

- **`createWorld`/`getWorld`, `getPage`/`insertPage`, `recordLinks`/`getIncomingLinks`** (`src/db/repo.ts`). `db` is injected as a parameter so the same code runs on postgres.js in prod and on an in-memory engine in tests.
- **`insertPage`** is the **L1** immutable-cache write — `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so the first writer wins under a generation race and pages never change.
- **`getIncomingLinks`** is the **L2** join — every existing page that links *into* a slug, with its title + body, ready for the prompt builder. Blue links to ungenerated pages contribute nothing (inner join).
- **pglite** (Postgres-in-WASM) test harness: the L1 immutability and the L2 join are tested against a real Postgres-compatible engine in CI — no DB infra needed.

## Verification

`npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (30 passing, incl. 5 DB tests), `npm run build` all pass.

## Next

The generation orchestrator: cache check → fetch world + incoming links → build prompt → stream from the model → parse [[links]] → record links + insert page atomically.

body:
This PR implements a series of backend performance optimizations focused on improving the efficiency of dashboard and financial statistics. 

The primary optimization involves refactoring non-SARGable (Search ARGumentable) queries that used SQLite functions like `strftime` and `fn('date')` in `WHERE` clauses. These functions were forcing full table scans on `exams`, `lessons`, and `payments` tables. By replacing them with `Op.between` range queries on indexed columns, the database can now leverage the B-tree indexes for logarithmic-time lookups.

Additionally, new composite indexes were added to ensure that queries filtering by multiple columns (e.g., `instructor_id` and `start_time`) can be satisfied entirely by index searches.

Key improvements:
- **`get-financial-stats`**: ~60% latency reduction.
- **`get-dashboard-stats (Instructor)`**: ~54% latency reduction.
- **`get-student-progress`**: ~38% latency reduction.

All changes have been verified with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` and benchmarked using the existing performance script. All functional and integration tests pass.

- **Unified Texture Handling:** All images in the `imageMap` are now `CroppedTexture` instances, providing a consistent API for rendering sub-regions of textures.
- **Shader Support:** Updated both rectangular and hexagonal shaders to support a `crop` uniform, which is used to transform texture coordinates based on the `CroppedTexture` metadata.
- **Nested Cropping:** Added a `subBox` method to `CropBox` to allow for easy creation of sub-regions from already cropped textures, which was specifically used to fix artwork rendering in `StackIcon`.
- **API Consistency:** Updated `TextureRenderer` with new overloads to handle `CroppedTexture` seamlessly across different rendering methods.

I have verified the changes by ensuring the project compiles and by running relevant unit tests.

author: nasyrov
body:
Adds a `plumix({ basePath })` option so a plumix site can be served under a subdirectory (e.g. `example.com/custom-directory/*`) behind a reverse proxy. The design follows the model the major frameworks converged on (Next.js `basePath`, Nuxt `app.baseURL`, Astro `base`): normalize once at config load, strip the prefix once on the inbound request, and re-add it on every outbound URL. A root deployment (`basePath: ""`, the default) is a no-op throughout — existing behavior is byte-for-byte identical.

```ts
plumix({ basePath: "/custom-directory" }) // "" | "/seg"; path-only, never touches auth.passkey.origin
```

**Strip once at the edge.** The dispatcher rewrites the inbound request to its root-relative form before any routing, so every downstream surface — RPC, MCP, REST, auth flows, plugin routes, the public router, the admin shell — matches root-relative paths with no base awareness of its own. A request that isn't under the base 404s as `outside-base-path`. Leading-slash collapse keeps `//base/...` from dodging the gate.

**Outbound re-prefixing via `withBasePath`.** Canonical tags, sitemap (index + sub), RSS/Atom feeds, permalinks, and the session + locale cookie `Path` all carry the prefix. The OAuth `redirect_uri` / magic-link email + post-auth redirects are base-scoped too, so those flows complete under a subdirectory instead of bouncing to a base-less 404. Passkey was already correct (JSON + base-aware admin client).

**Admin: relocatable precompiled bundle.** The admin ships precompiled, so it can't bake a per-deploy base. Instead it's built with a relative Vite base and the worker injects `<base href="${basePath}/_plumix/admin/">` into the shell; the client derives its mount from that tag (`adminBasePath()`) for the TanStack Router basepath and the oRPC URL. Admin asset requests that reach the worker under the base are served from the assets binding at the stripped path.

**Validation.** Server-side (config → strip → outbound), the admin build, and all unit/integration layers are green: core 2167 + admin 562 + cloudflare 149 tests, typecheck/lint/knip/format clean, and the admin builds cleanly with the relative base (relative asset URLs, no absolute `/_plumix/admin/` refs). The one remaining manual gate is an **e2e run of the admin SPA behind a real subdirectory proxy** — asset loading + deep-link reloads under a base can only be fully proven in a browser, not by unit/integration tests.

author: b4nan
body:
T-SQL procedures can return result sets implicitly via a bare `SELECT`, but `callRoutine` discarded them whenever the routine declared no OUT/INOUT params — it always short-circuited to `undefined` even though the rows were sitting right there in the `execute()` result.

This surfaces those rows when present, while keeping pure-DML procedures resolving to `undefined`, matching how the MySQL driver already handles implicit result sets (`resultSets.length > 0 ? resultSets : undefined`).

Scoped to MSSQL only: MySQL already handles this, while PostgreSQL/Oracle don't surface implicit result sets (data comes back via refcursors/OUT params, already handled) and SQLite/libSQL don't support procedures.

The OUT/INOUT path is intentionally left untouched — those values come back through `ScalarReference` and the call still resolves to `undefined`, consistent with the other drivers.

Closes #7872

body:
Resolves neomjs/neo#13229

Authored by GPT-5 (Codex Desktop). Session 019ec50d-5a01-7b11-9490-50f3241e8cfc.

The Client now treats Bridge app-side `{type:'agent_disconnected', agentId, sessionId}` frames as lifecycle notifications before JSON-RPC dispatch and releases only the matching `(agentId, sessionId)` held locks via `WriteGuard.releaseAgent`. The handler fails closed on half-stamped frames so a missing `sessionId` cannot release every session for one agent, and an unknown disconnected writer remains a no-op.

Evidence: L2 (focused Playwright unit coverage around the Client lifecycle frame + real WriteGuard lock table) -> L2 required (Client-side release behavior is unit-verifiable; Bridge app-frame emission is already covered in current `dev`). No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket
Current `dev` already includes the Bridge app broadcast from `#13226`: agent close emits an app-side `agent_disconnected` frame with `sessionId`, and `Bridge.spec.mjs` covers that contract. This PR therefore implements the remaining Client consumer half and documents the fail-closed half-stamp boundary at the Client.

ZIEL: Im SAFunded-Checkout soll neben der bestehenden Stripe-Zahlung eine
Option "Mit Krypto zahlen (Validopay)" erscheinen. Wählt der Kunde sie, wird
eine Krypto-Bestellung angelegt und der Kunde zur...

✅ **Result:** Customers completing the SAFunded checkout can now pay for an Instant Funded account with cryptocurrency through Validopay, in addition to the existing Stripe card payment and Confirmo crypto option.

A new secondary button, "Pay with crypto (BTC)" ("Mit Krypto bezahlen (BTC)"), was added to the checkout page next to the existing payment buttons, styled with the same design system. Like the other payment options, it only becomes active once the customer has accepted all mandatory legal consents.

When a customer chooses this option, the checkout reads the signed-in user's identity from the Supabase session and creates a crypto order with Validopay, then redirects the customer to the Validopay payment page where the QR code, wallet address, and amount are shown. The order carries the same discounted USD amount that the customer sees in the checkout summary (the launch price after the LAUNCH35 discount), the selected plan ("25k" | "50k" | "100k"), and the plan's display name — so the crypto flow charges exactly what the Stripe flow would.

If something goes wrong — the customer is not signed in, or a network or order-creation problem occurs — a clear message is shown and the customer stays on the checkout page rather than being redirected.

The existing Stripe and Confirmo flows were left unchanged, and no pricing or crypto logic was duplicated: the checkout simply passes the already-computed discounted USD amount through. No secrets are used on the client; Validopay accepts the order without authentication and account activation after payment remains a server-side concern that was already in place.

The helper that talks to Validopay was added under the project's `lib/` directory, and the checkout copy was extended in both German and English.

author: ebongard
body:
## Why
Live-tested Media Follow Me: music stopped when leaving a room but never resumed in the next one. Two stacked bugs, both found by walking the house and reading the logs + the durable presence-event log.

## Bug 1 — resume bailed on enter-before-leave ordering
`on_user_enter_room` only resumed a session already in `SUSPENDED` state, assuming events arrive leave-then-enter. But `presence_stale_timeout=120s` means the old room's satellite keeps seeing the device long after the move, so the `enter(new room)` routinely fires while the session is still `PLAYING` → the handler bailed; then the lagging `leave` suspended it with nothing left to re-trigger a resume.

**Fix:** on enter, if the session is `PLAYING` in a *different* room, treat it as a move (stop old → resume here) instead of requiring it to already be suspended. Same-room enter stays a no-op.

## Bug 2 — the suspend cleared its own session
`on_user_leave_room` suspends by calling `_stop_playback` → `InternalToolService._media_control(action="stop")`, which has a "clear the follow session on stop" step (meant for a *user's* stop). It couldn't tell the follow's internal suspend-stop from a user stop, so **the suspend deleted the very session it was suspending**. By the time `enter` fired, there was no session to resume.

**Fix:** `_stop_playback` tags its stop with `_media_follow_internal=True`; `_media_control` skips the session-clear when that marker is present. A genuine user "stop" (no marker) still clears.

## Validated live
With both fixes (deployed as v2.17.14), the full chain fires and the music followed across rooms and back:
`suspending` → session survives → `entered <room> — resuming` → `Resumed playback`.

## Tests
37/37 media-follow tests pass, incl. the enter-different-room-while-playing follow, the same-room no-op, the no-session no-op, and the suspend-must-not-clear-session regression.

> Note: live testing also surfaced a separate **presence** flip-flop bug (broken room-change hysteresis) that makes presence itself unreliable for adjacent rooms — fixed in a follow-up PR. This PR fixes the media-follow *mechanism*; presence accuracy is tracked separately.

Closes #271. Adds a per-issue in-progress signal, derived live (nothing cached) from **either** a hot \`feat/<n>-\`/\`fix/<n>-\` branch **or** a \`work-plan:in-progress\` GitHub label (union; closed/merged never in-progress).

## What's in it
**Read path (live-derived, persists nothing):**
- \`lib/git_state.hot_issue_numbers\` — maps hot \`feat/<n>-\`/\`fix/<n>-\` branches to issue numbers (anchored regex, no \`2710\`-vs-\`271\` collision).
- \`lib/in_progress.issue_in_progress\` — union merge, closed/merged always wins.
- Lean GraphQL field set now fetches \`labels\` (was label-blind → the viewer's label signal would have been silently always-false).
- Surfaced in \`brief\`, \`orient\`, and the VS Code export + detail-webview **badge**.

**Write path (the toolkit's 2nd dedicated GitHub mutation):**
- \`in-progress <n> [--clear]\` — repo-resolved from the tracked set with **ambiguity rejection**; \`--repo\` to disambiguate; \`--repo\`-qualified \`gh\` calls; label auto-created; behind the reused public-repo confirm-token gate.
- VS Code detail-webview **toggle**, reusing the existing \`executeWrite\` confirm flow.

**Compatibility/docs:** \`MIN_CLI_VERSION\` → \`2026.06.14\`, extension → \`0.8.0\`; README command tables + GitHub-mutation inventory updated.

## ⚠️ Bundled production bugfix (#305, #285)
While wiring the VS Code toggle, found that \`isWebviewMessage\` (the inbound type-guard) was **missing cases for \`closeIssue\` and \`openPlan\`** — so the shipped "Close on GitHub" (#305) and "Open Plan" (#285) buttons were **silently dead** (their messages dropped before reaching handlers). Fixed root-cause: extracted the guard into a pure, unit-testable \`src/webview/messages.ts\` with a 43-case regression suite. Its own \`fix(vscode)\` commit (\`c5d58ec\`).

## Design + review trail
- Brainstormed → spec (\`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-…\`, Codex-reviewed: DO NOT SHIP → all 7 findings folded in) → plan → subagent-driven execution with per-task review.
- Final holistic review (Opus): **SHIP** — no-cache principle and the GitHub-mutation security boundary both verified clean.

## Tests (all \`gh\`/\`git\` mocked, offline)
Python **995 OK** · VS Code **582 pass** · typecheck clean. Covers branch→issue mapping, the union truth table, cross-repo non-bleed, ambiguity rejection, public-without-token = no mutation, and the dropped-message regression.

> Targets \`dev\`, not \`main\` (deploy is separate). Recommend \`/ultrareview\` before merge — this crosses the GitHub-mutation boundary.

author: kkd16
body:
Follow-up to the merged v3.0 release, adding four more well-scoped, fully-tested features to **QueryForge**. All changes stay inside `projects/queryforge-db-7q4x/`.

## What's new

1. **Bitmap OR scans** — `WHERE col IN (…)` over an indexed column now unions per-value index lookups into one bitmap (the OR counterpart to the v3.0 BitmapAnd) instead of falling back to a sequential scan. Folded into the same `chooseIndexAccess` that ranks single / composite / bitmap-AND / bitmap-OR paths by predicates consumed.
2. **`GROUPING_ID(a, b, …)`** — the combined grouping bitmap as a single integer, alongside the existing `GROUPING()`.
3. **`VALUES` constructor** — both a top-level `VALUES (…), (…)` statement and `FROM (VALUES …) AS t(cols)`, desugared in the parser to a `UNION ALL` of constant SELECTs so the existing derived-table + set-op type-unification machinery handles it.
4. **Derived-table column aliases** — `FROM (SELECT …) t (c1, c2)` renames a subquery's output columns.

## Verification

- Self-test suite grown **113 → 120**, all green (head-less + Tests panel).
- `node scripts/verify-project.mjs queryforge-db-7q4x` passes: scope + conformance + `pnpm lint` + `pnpm build`.

author: aureliolo
body:
## Summary

Foundational project-wide convention & hardcoding rollout (the audit sweep that seven sibling audit issues land on top of). No dual codepaths, no half-applied conventions; every change self-enforcing.

**Pydantic / models**
- `allow_inf_nan=False` on all 56 frozen models that lacked it; the frozen-model gate (`check_frozen_model_extra_forbid.py`) now enforces it across `src/synthorg/` (with `# lint-allow: frozen-allow-inf-nan` per-line opt-out, no `@computed_field` carve-out).
- Identifier/FK string fields retyped to `NotBlankStr` (`WebhookReceipt.event_type`/`.status`, `RefreshRotation.token`/`.session_id`, `ModelCallResult.finish_reason`).
- Deepcopy `model_validator` guards on every frozen model with a mutable dict/list field (`ReviewStageResult`, `CompletionResponse`, `SystemPrompt`, `AgentLifecycleEvent`, `TaskSpec`, `ActivityEvent`, `CareerEvent`, `Report`, `AdaptationProposal`); `_ProjectRecord` exposes a read-only `MappingProxyType` view over a private dict.
- Validators raise `ValueError` (not `TypeError`) so Pydantic wraps them into `ValidationError` (`cost_recording`, `workflow/definition`, `dto_workflow`).

**Hardcoding**
- Magic numbers moved to operator-tunable `settings/definitions/` (research triage/dedup/prefilter/per-query knobs; engine `max_turns`, `task_engine_max_queue_size`) or module-level annotated `Final` constants (argon2 params, CSRF code, drain timeout, RPM windows, max-token limits). `check_no_magic_numbers.py` stays green with no new allowlist entries.
- Backend selection via `persistence/backend_dispatch.build_for_backend` + the new `supports_conversational_approvals` protocol predicate, replacing open-coded `if backend == "sqlite"` chains and the conversational guard's literal compare.
- Sandbox/sidecar/desktop image pins derive from `__version__`; `backup.on_shutdown` defaults off (model + registry).

**Renames / hygiene**
- Removed dual-codepath/alias/dead artefacts: `STRATEGY_NAME_CHEAPEST`, `PassthroughMemoryFilter`, `_reject_legacy_max_requests`, `DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT` re-export; `_X_from_row` → `_row_to_<noun>`.
- Documented newly-found conventions in `conventions.md` (`get_by_<key>`) and `persistence-boundary.md` (`_row_to_<noun>` / `_to_row` / `_safe_rollback`).
- Web DTO drift fixed: `PaginatedResponse.degraded_sources` required on success; `WorkflowDefinitionVersionSummary` wraps the generated `WorkflowDefinition`.

**Schema**
- `webhook_receipts.event_type` tightened to `CHECK (LENGTH(TRIM(event_type)) > 0)` via yoyo revisions on both backends (backfill + constraint), matching the new `NotBlankStr` model field.

## Test plan
- New behavioural suites: NotBlankStr rejection, deepcopy guards, ValidationError-not-TypeError, settings round-trip/bounds, backend dispatch + protocol predicate, gate self-tests for `allow_inf_nan`.
- Full pre-push battery green (ruff, mypy, unit suite, frozen-model + magic-number + settings-startup-trace + schema-drift + dto-sync + ESLint + vale + sqlfluff + import-linter + architecture-drift).
- Web typecheck + lint clean.

## Review coverage
Pre-reviewed by 6 agents (issue-resolution-verifier, conventions-enforcer, code-reviewer, persistence-reviewer, api-contract-drift, docs-consistency); all valid findings addressed (backup default effectiveness, webhook event_type DB CHECK, doc accuracy, removed-alias doc cleanup). Pre-existing-unrelated findings (fine-tune sidecar port mismatch, version-history.ts rollback drift) noted for separate issues.

Closes #2339

## Summary
Adds transfer functionality to the player detail screen, allowing users to buy and sell players with confirmation dialogs. Also improves navigation by making club names and league table rows clickable, and adds player profile links throughout the app.

## Key Changes

- **Player Transfer Screen**: Added a new "Transfer" section to the player screen with buy/sell buttons that:
  - Calculate transfer fees based on player value and market rules
  - Validate transfers against squad size limits, budget constraints, and buyer availability
  - Show disabled state with explanatory reasons when transfers aren't possible

- **Navigation Improvements**:
  - Club names on player screen now link to club detail page
  - League table rows are now clickable to view club details
  - Player names in record tables (top scorers, assisters, goalkeepers) link to player profiles
  - Players in lineup and market screens can be long-pressed to view their profile

- **Club Records**: Extended `clubRecords()` to work for any club, not just the managed club:
  - Records all-time goal/assist contributions for all clubs
  - Best finish metric only applies to managed club (other clubs show "–")
  - Added test coverage for cross-club integrity and AI club records

- **Data Model**: Updated player contribution tracking to record stats on the player's current club rather than only the managed club, ensuring sold players' historical stats are preserved

## Implementation Details

- New `transferState()` function mirrors market.tsx logic to determine buy/sell eligibility and amounts

author: noahgift
body:
## Summary

`abs(x)` over an `int` emitted `(x).abs()`, but `i64::MIN.abs()` wraps to `i64::MIN` (no overflow check under `-O`) — a **silent wrap that falsifies C-PY-INT-ARITH's overflow guarantee** (Python's `abs` is exact). The contract-integrity sibling to the left/right-shift fixes (PMAT-575/577). Found by the differential hunt.

## Fix

Add `of_float` to `Expr::NumBuiltin` (set by the frontend from the first argument's type, mirroring `ListMutate`/`Sorted`). The `Abs` arm now emits `.checked_abs().expect(...)` for an i64 (panics on `i64::MIN` per the contract) and keeps `.abs()` for an f64 (never overflows). `min`/`max` and the float math builtins ignore the flag. Rust + Ruchy.

## Verification

New e2e fixture `abs_overflow.py` cross-checked vs python3: `a_int(-5)=5`, `a_float(-3.5)=3.5`, and `abs(i64::MIN)` panics (via `catch_unwind`). Updated 4 existing builtin-assertion tests to the `.checked_abs()` form.

author: gnanam1990
body:
## Problem
With the default sandbox policy (`network: deny`), `web_search` (and `web_fetch`) are **hard-denied** before they run:

```
denied · web_search · risk:high — network access is blocked by sandbox policy
Sandbox violation [network] for web_search: network access is blocked by sandbox policy
```

#199 added `EnforceToolNetwork` (off by default) to exempt the first-party in-process network tools, but it only relaxed `NetworkHostAllowed` — the per-host check *inside* the tool's `RunWithSandbox`. The actual deny happens **earlier**, at the engine-level gate in `Evaluate` (run by the tool registry): a request whose risk includes `network` under `NetworkDeny` is rejected *before* the tool executes. So the tool never reached the relaxed check. (#199 merged at the commit just before this follow-up, so the gap shipped to `main`.)

## Fix
`Evaluate` now skips the network-deny for a request that declares `SideEffectNetwork` (the first-party in-process tools `web_search`/`web_fetch`) when `EnforceToolNetwork` is off — mirroring the `NetworkHostAllowed` exemption so the engine-level gate and the per-tool gate agree. A **shell** command merely classified as network (`SideEffect=shell`, e.g. `curl`) is **not** exempt, so sandboxed-shell egress stays blocked under deny. Setting `EnforceToolNetwork: true` restores the strict deny for the tools.

Net effect: `web_search`/`web_fetch` are no longer hard-blocked by the sandbox; they follow the normal permission flow (prompt in ask mode → run on allow; run in auto mode).

## Tests
- `TestEvaluateExemptsNetworkToolsFromDenyByDefault` — full path: default → not denied; granted → `allow`; `EnforceToolNetwork=true` → denied; network **shell** command → stays denied.
- `TestEngineDeniesNetworkSideEffectWhenPolicyBlocksNetwork` and `TestScopedNetworkGateInEvaluate` updated to opt into `EnforceToolNetwork` (they test the strict gate).

## Gates (local)
`gofmt -l .` empty · `go vet` · `go build` · `go test ./...` (incl. `-race` on sandbox+tools) · `staticcheck` no new findings · `govulncheck` 0 · `deadcode -test=false` no new unreachable funcs.

Scoped to the sandbox fix only — 3 files (`engine.go`, `engine_test.go`, `runner_scoped_test.go`).

Resolves the GitHub-mechanics issue cluster (**#52, #54, #56**) toward the least-complex, GitHub-native shape. Per operator steer (2026-06-14): the ~24h reconciler auto-close latency is a non-issue, and the org Project board is a **human curation surface** for significant issues — not an automation target. **No GitHub App, no standing secret**; stay on `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

The net effect is *subtraction*: −92/+49 lines, one bespoke reconciler **not** built.

### #56 — raise the close-reconciler closing-reference cap
`closedByPullRequestsReferences(first: 10 → 100)` (GraphQL connection max) with a documented justification in the header. >100 closing PRs on one issue is implausible, and full nested pagination buys nothing for a backstop. author: shhhans
body:
> 堆叠 PR，base 为 `feat/persistent-memory`（#7）。待 #7 合并后再合本 PR。

## 概要

接通记忆**读侧**：回复前用当前用户语句**同步**召回相关 `fact`，注入 prompt，让 Agent 跨会话「记得你」。召回是纯本地 FTS（无 LLM/网络），同步在回复前做，帮到**当前这句**，而非只预热下一回合。

## 改动

- **`sqlite_fts.py`** — `search`/`_query` 加 `kind` 过滤（回灌只取简洁 `fact`，不灌嘈杂 `episode`）。新增 **`_build_match`**：把检索文本切成重叠 3 字窗、各成短语 `OR` 起来。避免「整句当一个短语」导致方向反了（要求事实是问句的子串，自然问句永远匹配不到），改成「任一 3 字片段命中即相关」，靠 FTS rank 排序。
- **`provider.py` / `worker.py`** — `recall` 加 `kind` 参数；worker 暴露只读 `recall` 入口，与后台串行写互不阻塞。
- **`session.py`** — 新增 `_recall_context()`，回复前召回 `fact` 注入到本回合用户消息之前；**await 召回前先快照 history**，避免召回期间 `scene_change` 并发追加观察导致注入错位；不写回 `self.history`。召回失败优雅降级，绝不阻断回复。

## 已知边界

- **trigram 仅匹配 ≥3 字连续重叠**：`喜欢喝什么`→`用户喜欢喝咖啡` ✓；但 `我的猫`→`叫 momo 的猫`（关键词「猫」1 字）、`项目`（2 字）抓不到。备选 per-char 分词会误召爆炸，故两害取精度。语义级召回需 embeddings，留作后续。

## 验证

- `_build_match` 召回语义 + `kind` 过滤 + 特殊字符安全，均用真实 CPython 实测。
- `py_compile` 通过。
- **Codex review 已过**：HIGH（召回方向反了）+ MEDIUM（召回 await 期间竞态）均已修复并验证。
- **无新增依赖**。

author: humanjack
body:
## Summary
Adds a production-ready `Makefile` (plus a `scripts/app.sh` process controller) giving the app a predictable lifecycle: **build / start / stop / restart / clean / status** (+ `help`, `distclean`).

The app is a Vite + TypeScript + Phaser web game, so "the application" is its web server — `vite preview` serving the built `dist/` in prod (default), or the `vite` dev server with `MODE=dev`.

Closes #170.

## Why a helper script (`scripts/app.sh`)
macOS ships **GNU Make 3.81**, which ignores `.ONESHELL` — so each recipe line runs in its own shell and multi-line logic (retry loops, recursive process-tree kill) can't live portably in a recipe. The Makefile stays a thin, portable dispatcher; the process logic lives in one well-commented POSIX-sh script. Works on macOS (BSD) **and** GNU/Linux.

## Guarantees
- **Single instance** — `start` runs the stop path first; a second `make start` replaces the first (one listener remains).
- **Reliable teardown of detached/orphaned procs** — `stop` kills the tracked PID's whole tree (children-first `TERM`, escalate to `KILL`) **plus** a port-based safety net that frees the port even with a stale/missing PID file.
- **Idempotent** — installs are stamp-gated; `stop`/`clean` are safe no-ops when nothing's running.
- **Non-destructive `clean`** — removes `dist/`, Vite caches, `coverage`, `.run/`, `*.tsbuildinfo`; keeps `node_modules` (use `distclean`); is git-aware so it never deletes tracked `.playwright-mcp/` fixtures.

## Usage
```
make build                      # npm install (when manifests change) + tsc + vite build
make start                      # auto-builds if dist/ missing, then launches detached
make status                     # RUNNING/STOPPED + process tree + port listeners
make stop / restart / clean / distclean
make start MODE=dev PORT=8080   # override any variable
```

## Test plan (all run on macOS, GNU Make 3.81)
- [x] `make build` → installs deps + produces `dist/`
- [x] `make start` → detached, waits for port bind; `make status` shows tree + listener
- [x] `make start` again → still exactly one listener (old PID replaced)
- [x] `make restart` → clean stop + start
- [x] stale PID file (`999999`) → `make stop` still frees the port via the safety net
- [x] `make clean` twice → idempotent; `node_modules` kept; tracked `.playwright-mcp/` preserved
- [x] verified `MODE`/`PORT` overrides and auto-build-on-start

## Files
- `Makefile` — targets + config
- `scripts/app.sh` — POSIX-sh `start|stop|status` controller
- `.gitignore` — add `.run/` (runtime pid/log)

## Follow-up (separate)
`.playwright-mcp/` is git-tracked but listed in `.gitignore` (predates this PR). Could `git rm --cached` it to match the ignore intent — left out of this PR to keep scope tight.

author: yorliabdulai
body:
💡 What: Replaced slow `new Date().getTime()` with `Date.parse()` in transaction sorting and time loops, and eliminated a redundant O(N log N) sort by slicing an already sorted array.
🎯 Why: `Array.prototype.sort()` creates a new `Date` object for every comparison, causing massive overhead when processing thousands of user transactions. The redundant sort for recent activity was also unnecessary.
📊 Impact: Reduces sorting latency by ~50% and O(N log N) reverse sorting time to O(1). Date comparison inside the O(N) points loop is also ~10x faster.
🔬 Measurement: Benchmark `tmp_perf` shows `Date.parse()` sorting takes ~94ms vs ~178ms for `new Date().getTime()`. Replacing redundant sort + slice with `.slice().reverse()` dropped 50,000 tx processing from ~1260ms to ~540ms.

author: copilot
body:
This change removes the split ownership of Harbor OIDC credentials between Keycloak and Harbor and makes inventory-defined `oidc_clients` the single source of truth. It also hardens the Ansible flow so production-like runs fail early on missing secrets, while CI continues to use explicit deterministic mock values.

- **Single OIDC source of truth**
  - Introduces shared inventory-driven client definitions under `oidc_clients`.
  - Wires both Keycloak client creation and Harbor/OpenBao consumer config to the same `client_id` / `client_secret`.
  - Eliminates independent secret duplication between `keycloak_config.clients[].secret` and `harbor_config.oidc.client_secret`.

  ```yaml
  oidc_clients:
    harbor:
      client_id: harbor
      client_secret: "{{ vault_oidc_harbor_client_secret }}"
    openbao:
      client_id: openbao
      client_secret: "{{ vault_oidc_openbao_client_secret }}"
  ```

- **Explicit CI vs non-CI behavior**
  - Adds strict assertions for required OIDC and Harbor secrets when `ci_mode: false`.
  - Keeps CI unblocked with deterministic mock defaults that are isolated from production inventory.
  - Uses clear failure messages for missing inventory/SOPS values.

- **Keycloak client hardening**
  - Builds Harbor/OpenBao OIDC clients from `oidc_clients` instead of implicit Keycloak-generated secrets.
  - Ensures the Harbor client is created with the inventory-provided secret.
  - Adds the `groups` OIDC protocol mapper required for Harbor group claims.

- **Harbor OIDC robustness**
  - Derives Harbor OIDC config from shared OIDC vars and sets the expected payload defaults, including `offline_access`.
  - Makes Harbor API TLS validation configurable, defaulting to validation outside CI.
  - Prevents switching Harbor from `db_auth` to OIDC when local non-admin users already exist.
  - Centralizes Harbor API auth/TLS handling across OIDC and registry mirror calls.

- **Harbor runtime secret enforcement**
  - Removes production fallback behavior for Harbor runtime secrets (`db_password`, `core_secret`, `jobservice_secret`, `registry_password`) outside CI.
  - Keeps mock secrets available only in CI paths.

- **Config examples and docs**
  - Reworks public examples to show `ci_mode`, `oidc_clients`, and SOPS-backed secret placement without embedding real secrets.

body:
# Add gradient border ring to Avatar component

This PR was made using Fei! Visit [the task in Studio](https://studio.dev.autonomyai.io/projects/9ad002e2-55b8-4b93-965d-c21b97f8ec98/tasks/1c265cae-fced-4cdb-b53d-ba2c03f4cdae?version=3) to see this PR working.

---

## Summary
Adds a visually distinct gradient border ring to the Avatar component and a small due-date label to issue cards. The Avatar change introduces a new, opt-in `hasGradientBorder` prop that renders a teal-to-blue gradient ring which scales with avatar size and works for both image and initial-letter avatars. The issue card update adds a right-aligned, formatted due-date label next to the priority badge when a due date is present.

Both changes are fully backward compatible and introduce no new dependencies.

---

## Key Changes
- ✨ Added `hasGradientBorder` prop to Avatar component to enable an optional gradient ring.
- Gradient ring displays a teal-to-blue gradient and scales proportionally with avatar `size` (approx. 3px at default 32px).
- Works with both image-based avatars and initial-letter fallbacks.
- ✅ Added a `DueDateLabel` to issue cards that displays when `issue.dueDate` exists.
- Imported `formatDate` from `shared/utils/dateTime` and format used is short form `MMM D` (e.g., "Jun 10").
- Updated `api/package-lock.json` (lockfile changes surfaced in this branch).

---

## Files Changed
- `src/components/Avatar/Avatar.tsx`
  - Added new optional prop `hasGradientBorder?: boolean` and logic to render the gradient ring when true.
  - Implemented ring sizing so it scales proportionally based on `size` prop (calculated ring width ~ 9.375% of avatar size — ~3px at 32px).
  - Ensured ring displays for both image avatars and initial-letter avatars and preserves existing avatar behavior when `hasGradientBorder` is not provided.
  - Added unit/visual tests or storybook example (if project uses stories) for the new prop.

- `src/components/Avatar/styles.ts` (or inline styled definition inside `Avatar.tsx`)
  - Added CSS/styled-component rules for the gradient ring using a pseudo-element and a linear-gradient / conic-style gradient to produce a smooth teal-to-blue ring.
  - Ring rendered outside the avatar content, using transform/scale or padding to avoid clipping and to preserve avatar inner radius.

- `src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.tsx`
  - Imported `formatDate` from `shared/utils/dateTime`.
  - Rendered `DueDateLabel` to the right of the priority badge when `issue.dueDate` exists.

- `src/components/IssueCard/styles.ts`
  - Added `DueDateLabel` styled component with muted, small text styling consistent with existing text utilities (color, font-size, spacing).
  - Ensured the label is hidden when no `issue.dueDate` is present.

- `src/shared/utils/dateTime.ts` (usage)
  - Used existing `formatDate` helper to render the due date in short form (`'MMM D'`).

- `api/package-lock.json`
  - Lockfile updated as part of the branch (multiple package metadata changes shown in diff). No intentional dependency additions for this UI change — included because the branch updated the lockfile.

---

## Implementation Notes
- The Avatar gradient ring is implemented using styled-components (project already uses styled-components for component styling) via a pseudo-element that sits behind the avatar content and uses a linear-gradient from teal to blue.
- Ring thickness is computed dynamically from the avatar `size` prop: ringWidth = max(2px, Math.round(size * 0.09375)) which yields ~3px at the default 32px size and scales proportionally at other sizes.
- The ring does not alter the avatar content size: inner avatar stays the same while the ring is drawn outside the avatar using extra wrapper/padding or transform to avoid layout shifts.
- `hasGradientBorder` is opt-in; default behavior is unchanged and fully backward compatible.
- Due date label uses existing `formatDate` from `shared/utils/dateTime` with the format string `'MMM D'` to produce concise dates like "Jun 10".
- No additional dependencies were introduced.
- CSS and styled-component styles follow existing project tokens/utilities for spacing and color so visual consistency is preserved.

---

## How to Test
1. Avatar gradient ring
   1. Navigate to a page or story that renders Avatar components (e.g., user list, comment thread, or storybook).
   2. For an avatar instance, enable the `hasGradientBorder` prop (or open the corresponding story that demonstrates the prop).
   3. Verify a teal-to-blue gradient ring appears around the avatar.
   4. Check with an image avatar and with an initial-letter avatar to confirm both render the ring.
   5. Resize the avatar (if a size prop is supported) and verify the ring thickness scales proportionally (approx. 3px at 32px). Ensure no clipping occurs.
   6. Verify that existing avatars without `hasGradientBorder` render unchanged.

2. Due date label on issue cards
   1. Open an issue list or card view with items that have `issue.dueDate` set and items that do not.
   2. Verify the `DueDateLabel` renders to the right of the priority badge for items with a due date.

3. General

   2. Build the frontend and visually scan related pages for regressions.

- No new runtime dependencies were added; however `api/package-lock.json` was updated in this branch — please review the lockfile changes to ensure they match CI expectations.

author: easonliangworldedtech
body:
---

## Problem

PR #10480 added `react@^19.1.0` to `apps/cli/package.json`. This caused `@types/react@19` to be installed alongside `webview-ui`'s `react@^18.3.1`, leading to TypeScript errors like:

```
TS2786: 'Plus' cannot be used as a JSX component.
TS2578: Type 'DetailedHTMLProps<HTMLAttributes, div>' requires 'React.JSX.Element' from module 'react' but was resolved to a different version.
```

## Root Cause

The pnpm override `@types/react: 18.3.23` exists in the root `package.json`, but stale peer dependency resolution can cause `@types/react@19` to leak into the lockfile or node_modules during certain install scenarios.

## Fix

Add a `postinstall` script that runs `pnpm dedupe --check || true` to ensure the override always takes effect after installation:

```json
"postinstall": "pnpm dedupe --check || true"
```

This forces pnpm to re-resolve dependencies and enforce the override, preventing version conflicts between `apps/cli` (React 19) and `webview-ui` (React 18).

## Verification

- ✅ `webview-ui` build passes (`tsc -b && vite build`)
- ✅ All **124 test files** pass (**1369 tests**) in `@roo-code/core`
- ✅ No `@types/react@19` present in lockfile or node_modules after install

## Related

- Source of React 19: PR #10480 "Add a TUI"
- Existing override: root `package.json` (PR #423)
---

author: chase-mew
body:
## Summary

Today the search area is geometric: the weighted geometric median plus a circle. But the scorer is travel time aware, so any transit convenient spot that sits off to the side (common in London, where the best meeting point is often where two tube lines cross) is never sampled and therefore can never win.

This adds a travel time area finding stage before the venue search.

- Build candidate anchors from a dense grid (coverage) plus London transit stations (interchanges first), deduplicated and capped to a matrix budget that scales with group size.
- Score every anchor by the chosen fairness objective (`best`, `min_max`, `min_total`, `min_variance`) using a transit matrix from each person, mirroring the venue scorer's handling of `best`.
- Select up to a few spatially distinct areas via non maximum suppression, so genuinely separate good areas both contribute venues.
- Search venues around each area in parallel, dedupe, then run the existing prune, venue matrix, and scoring.
- Generalise candidate pruning to use the nearest of multiple area centres.

The geometric median is always included as an anchor and as a fallback, so the result is never worse than before.

## Verification

- Unit tests for the new `areas` module (bounding box, grid, dedupe, anchor building, area selection and separation, and the `best` objective path) plus updated orchestration tests. Full typecheck and build are green.
- Verified live against the Worker with the four example addresses (W2, SW12, SW19, NW1): the meeting area now sits at a travel optimised location off the geometric centre, and all returned pubs are rated 4.3 to 4.7. The simple three person case still returns balanced 14 to 15 minute cafe options.

## Notes

- Stays entirely on the Google stack. The longer term upgrade is TravelTime public transport isochrone intersection for Stage one, which the provider interface keeps swappable.
- Adds one transit matrix call (area stage). It is budgeted by group size and the results are cached.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (typecheck, test, build)
- [ ] Area sits off centre toward transit hubs when that is fairer
- [ ] Distinct areas considered; results still sensible for small groups

author: danielmarbach
body:
I used the tool yesterday for some perf investigations, and I loved it. So I decided to give something back today. Here we go

This pull request modernizes the command-line handling and output serialization for several commands in the codebase. It updates the `Alloc`, `CallTree`, `CpuStacks`, and `Clean` commands to use the new System.CommandLine API, introduces asynchronous execution and cancellation support, and switches to source-generated JSON serialization for improved performance and maintainability. The changes also improve code readability and error handling.

### Command-line API modernization and async/cancellation support
* All commands (`AllocCommand`, `CallTreeCommand`, `CleanCommand`, `CpuStacksCommand`) now use the newer `SetAction` method from System.CommandLine, which provides better support for dependency injection, async execution, and cancellation tokens. Synchronous handlers are replaced with async methods, and cancellation is checked during long-running operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c83da13c305610b1afa6d6faa9d5d39b9296fae57efc52c312782fd9d38b8984L2-R82) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e72d6d17da2ff0853841105a2518857a97e66c6ec5431dd1fa197284dcc8fe8L34-R83) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a5dbf43d9d9cd08be76e72d8d5ba91a0f7578d7b3b6c32b1316bb5618864fbdeR2-R28)

### Source-generated JSON serialization
* Commands that output JSON (`AllocCommand`, `CallTreeCommand`, `CpuStacksCommand`) now use source-generated serialization contexts (e.g., `AllocJsonContext`, `CallTreeJsonContext`, `CpuStacksJsonContext`) for more efficient and reliable JSON serialization. This replaces hand-rolled anonymous objects and options with strongly-typed responses. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c83da13c305610b1afa6d6faa9d5d39b9296fae57efc52c312782fd9d38b8984L2-R82) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e72d6d17da2ff0853841105a2518857a97e66c6ec5431dd1fa197284dcc8fe8L2-R53) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1ceb811f02f006bf80ab924bf641cb3caaf546dbea93341a07860f22d4f40829L2-R14)

### Improved error handling and cancellation
* All commands now properly handle `OperationCanceledException`, ensuring that cancellation requests are respected and not masked by generic exception handlers. Cancellation tokens are checked in loops that process or delete files. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c83da13c305610b1afa6d6faa9d5d39b9296fae57efc52c312782fd9d38b8984R101-R102) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a5dbf43d9d9cd08be76e72d8d5ba91a0f7578d7b3b6c32b1316bb5618864fbdeR72-R84) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7e72d6d17da2ff0853841105a2518857a97e66c6ec5431dd1fa197284dcc8fe8L86-R141)

### Refactoring of command argument/option definitions
* Arguments and options are now constructed with object initializers, improving clarity and maintainability. Default values and descriptions are set in a consistent, modern style. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c83da13c305610b1afa6d6faa9d5d39b9296fae57efc52c312782fd9d38b8984L2-R82) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e72d6d17da2ff0853841105a2518857a97e66c6ec5431dd1fa197284dcc8fe8L2-R53) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a5dbf43d9d9cd08be76e72d8d5ba91a0f7578d7b3b6c32b1316bb5618864fbdeR2-R28)

### Output and response refactoring
* Output methods for JSON now use strongly-typed DTOs and a shared `JsonOutput.WriteAsync` method, ensuring consistent, indented, and camel-cased output across commands. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c83da13c305610b1afa6d6faa9d5d39b9296fae57efc52c312782fd9d38b8984L219-R293) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e72d6d17da2ff0853841105a2518857a97e66c6ec5431dd1fa197284dcc8fe8L116-R153) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7e72d6d17da2ff0853841105a2518857a97e66c6ec5431dd1fa197284dcc8fe8L146-R189) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7e72d6d17da2ff0853841105a2518857a97e66c6ec5431dd1fa197284dcc8fe8L182-R223)

These changes collectively improve reliability, maintainability, and user experience for the command-line tools.

body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/safunded/agent-runs/6a2eb422c5fc3d90bf2f2e76

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Ah, stimmt — dann ist die Lage einfacher, als ich gerade gemacht habe. Der Agent hat den Checkout-Button + die Weiterleitung schon gebaut (v1). Es fehlt nur das Rabatt-Stück. Also kein kompletter Neu-Auftrag, sondern ein gezielter Ergänzungsauftrag.
...

✅ **Result:** The crypto payment option (pay with Validopay) already existed in the checkout, but it was wired up the old way: the frontend computed and handed Validopay a finished amount, which meant any discount logic lived in — and could be manipulated from — the browser. This change completes the crypto flow by moving pricing to the server and adding a discount-code experience.

The Validopay checkout helper was upgraded to its v2 form. Instead of sending a pre-calculated amount, the helper now sends only the selected plan and the entered discount code, and Validopay computes the price server-side. A new helper for live price quotes was added so the checkout can preview the price before the customer pays.

In the checkout, a discount-code field was added that applies to the crypto payment path. As the customer types a code, the checkout fetches a live quote and shows the result: the final price is displayed prominently, and when the code is a valid coupon the regular list price is shown struck through alongside an "incl. X% discount" note. An invalid code shows a clear "Code invalid" message, and a transient lookup failure is reported separately. The preview is debounced so it updates smoothly while typing. For example, entering LAUNCH35 on the 50K plan shows a live price of $259.35 with the $399 list price struck through.

When the customer proceeds to pay with crypto, the entered code is passed through to Validopay, which applies the discount and computes the amount to charge. No prices are hardcoded in the frontend anymore — every amount shown or charged comes from the server.

The card (Stripe) payment flow was left unchanged. All new copy was added in both English and German.

author: mkelley33
body:
## Summary

Refactor the `useEntityQuery` hooks so callers can tune TanStack Query behavior
per call site, and clarify the paginated-response type names. Every hook now
accepts an optional query-options object spread into its inner `useQuery` /
`useInfiniteQuery` call, replacing ad-hoc `enabled` flags and hardcoded-only
defaults.

## Changes

### Query option overrides
- Add shared `QueryOptionsOverride` and `InfiniteQueryOptionsOverride` helper
  types (`src/app/hooks/query-options.ts`) accepting every option except the
  ones each hook owns — `queryKey`/`queryFn` (plus `initialPageParam`/
  `getNextPageParam` for infinite queries).
- Give every `useEntityQuery` hook a trailing `options = {}` argument, spread
  **last** so caller values override the hook's defaults while `queryKey`/
  `queryFn` stay locked via the option type.
- Fold ad-hoc `enabled` parameters into the options object, re-applying each
  hook's internal guard (e.g. `!!releaseId`, min-length, `authenticated`) after
  the spread so guards can't be clobbered.
- Convert the remaining named-function hooks to arrow functions for consistency.

### Type renames
- Rename the five paginated-response aliases to `...PaginatedResponse`
  (`ArtistsPage`, `FeaturedArtistsPage`, `ReleasesPage`, `ToursPage`,
  `PublishedReleasesPage`) so the names match their shape. Scoped to the type
  only — the `fetch{Entity}Page` helpers and Next.js page components are
  untouched.

### Call sites & tests
- Update affected call sites (venue/notification/release/artist selects,
  download list, mention autocomplete) to pass `{ enabled }`.
- Refresh the mention-query test mocks for the new options signature.

## Testing Notes

- Full gate green: `pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test:run && pnpm run lint && pnpm run format` (7947 unit tests pass).
- E2E suite green: `pnpm run test:e2e` (129 passed); the `[WebServer] NoSuchKey`
  log lines are the expected fixture-less bundle-download scenario, not failures.
- Watch the guarded hooks: a hook must stay disabled when its guard fails even
  if a caller passes `enabled: true` (e.g. `useReleaseQuery('', { enabled: true })` should not fire).
- Spot-check converted call sites — venue/artist/release selects only fetch when
  their popover is `open`, and the chat mention autocomplete still queries.

author: vibechoom
body:
## What

Makes trollshell's wallpaper reload **pluggable** instead of swaybg-only, so the Appearance picker works for `swww`/`awww` (and `hyprpaper`, `wbg`, …) users.

Closes #2.

## Why

`crates/hytte-services/src/wallpaper.rs` hardcoded `systemctl --user restart swaybg.service` on every pick. A non-swaybg user (including this repo's own primary user, who runs `services.awww`) got a double miss: the picker wrote `wallpaper.path`, then restart-failed on a `swaybg.service` that isn't running — so the wallpaper never applied — and if they also flipped on `enableSessionExtras`, the bundled swaybg unit fought their daemon over the wallpaper layer.

## How

- **`wallpaper.rs`** — `set_path` now runs `$TROLLSHELL_WALLPAPER_RELOAD_CMD` via `sh -c` (with the chosen path exported as `$TROLLSHELL_WALLPAPER_PATH`), falling back to the swaybg unit restart when unset. **Default behavior is unchanged.**
- **`nix/module-common.nix`** — new shared option `programs.trollshell.wallpaper.reloadCommand` (`nullOr str`, default `null`).
- **`nix/nixos-module.nix` / `nix/hm-module.nix`** — wire it to the session env (`TROLLSHELL_WALLPAPER_RELOAD_CMD`), mirroring how `weather.fallbackCity` → `TROLLSHELL_WEATHER_CITY` is handled.
- **`nix/hm-module.nix`** — `enableSessionExtras` no longer auto-starts swaybg when a custom `reloadCommand` is set, so the bundle can't launch a second wallpaper daemon alongside the configured one.
- **`README.md`** — documents the option with the swww/awww recipe.

For an awww user that's just:

```nix
programs.trollshell.wallpaper.reloadCommand = ''awww img "$TROLLSHELL_WALLPAPER_PATH"'';
```

## Verification

- `nix build .#trollshell` — ✅ builds (release, full crane build)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` in the devShell — ✅ clean (pedantic at `deny`)
- `nix build .#checks.formatting` (treefmt) — ✅ `0 changed`
- new `wallpaper.reloadCommand` option — ✅ validated via `lib.evalModules` (type `nullOr str`, default `null`, accepts the `awww …` value). The session-var wiring in both modules is a verbatim mirror of the existing `weather.fallbackCity → TROLLSHELL_WEATHER_CITY` lines.

## Notes / follow-ups

- Backward-compatible: existing swaybg users (and the bundled `etc/systemd/user/swaybg.service`) are untouched — `null` keeps the historical restart.
- Out of scope here: a ready-made `swww`/`awww` *session-extra* that also manages the daemon unit. The HM daemon option name differs by home-manager release (`services.swww` vs `services.awww` after the 0.12 rename), so this PR deliberately leaves daemon management to the user and only plumbs the reload command. Can add a guarded extra later if wanted.

## Linked Change

This PR is the working-tree cleanup that has been open since the v2 SDD reset began. The artifacts being committed here were generated by `sdd-new` (for `bootstrap-alethea-v2`) and the 4-module grill-me (Phase 0). There is no GitHub issue — Alethea uses OpenSpec for change tracking.

- **Parent change (the implementation work this documents):** `openspec/sdd/bootstrap-alethea-v2/`
- **Source artifacts of the planning phase:** `openspec/CONTEXT.md`, `openspec/UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md`, `openspec/adr/`

## Type

`type:chore` (Maintenance/tooling — housekeeping of v1 material + activation of strict TDD config + landing of planning artifacts)

## Summary

Three commits, in this order:

1. **Housekeeping** — archive v1 issues, proposals, and an abandoned change. 18 files deleted, 2679 lines removed, no code touched.
2. **Build** — flip `strict_tdd` from false to true, add the `rules.apply` block that `sdd-apply` reads.
3. **Docs** — land the Phase 0 grill-me output (CONTEXT, UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE, 4 ADRs) and the `bootstrap-alethea-v2` planning artifacts (proposal, design, tasks, specs, no-go, state).

Net: 24 files added/modified, 2692 deletions, 2891 insertions. The repo is in a coherent v2 state, ready for `sdd-apply` of the next change.

## Why this PR exists

The v2 reset started with `sdd-init`, `sdd-new bootstrap-alethea-v2`, and a 4-module grill-me. The outputs of that work were never committed. The working tree accumulated ~36 files of dirty state, mixing v1 leftovers (AFK-style issues, an abandoned change, the v1 SDD proposals) with v2 planning artifacts (CONTEXT, ADRs, the bootstrap change).

A planned PR #66 (`chore/remove-open-api-spex`) was opened and closed without merge because the open_api_spex removal was already in `main` by another path. The 47 files visible in some IDE commit UIs are the same files this PR is committing; this PR is the disciplined version of that single mega-commit.

author: zipdoki
body:
## Summary

When a MultiEdge record's `_source` is updated, the old implementation submitted a decrement on the old source row and an increment on the new source row in a single batchAll call. Since HBase does not guarantee atomicity across rows, a partial failure could corrupt group counters with no safe retry path — replaying the same UPDATE would double-decrement the old source.

This PR fixes this by splitting the UPDATE into two sequential batches in V2BackedTableBinding.write:
1. Phase 1 (DELETE): persists an intermediate state (_source=<new>, active=false) and cleans up old source records
2. Phase 2 (CREATE): persists _source=<new>, active=true and populates new source records
  
The intermediate state written in phase 1 is the key to safe retries — if phase 2 fails and the client retries, read() picks up _source=<new>, active=false and re-enters only the CREATED path, preventing double-decrement on the old source counter.


## Changes

- V2BackedTableBinding.write: detect _source change on a MultiEdge UPDATE and execute DELETE + CREATE as two sequential handleDeferredRequests calls instead of one  

## How to Test
  - `./gradlew :engine:test --tests "com.kakao.actionbase.v2.engine.v3.edge.MultiEdgeSpec"`

author: iuhoay
body:
## Summary

Prepares rdrift.app for public, multi-user operation with three changes:

1. **Static pages** (`91de244`) — server-rendered `/terms`, `/privacy`, and `/about` via a thin `PagesController` + a dedicated `legal` layout, readable without authentication. Linked from sign-in, sign-up, and the sidebar. Operator-specific values are filled in (Drift, `hello@rdrift.app`, a generic governing-law clause).
2. **Transactional email** (`4424af3`) — Action Mailer SMTP is wired entirely from ENV (`SMTP_ADDRESS`/`SMTP_PORT`/`SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD`), gated on `SMTP_ADDRESS` so delivery stays **off** until configured; `ApplicationMailer`'s `from` reads `MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS`. Development opens mail in the browser via `letter_opener`. Kamal carries the SMTP env, with the API key as a secret. README documents the vars.
3. **AGPL-3.0 license** (`21f458f`) — the repo had no license, leaving it all-rights-reserved despite being public. Adds the canonical GNU AGPL-3.0 text and a README License section.

## Testing

- `bin/rails test` — **113 runs, 0 failures**
- `bin/rubocop` — clean
- Brakeman — **0 security warnings** (real scan). Note: `bin/ci`'s Brakeman step fails *locally* only because its `--ensure-latest` flag can't reach rubygems.org in the sandbox; this is the documented `--ensure-latest` issue, not a code finding, and should pass in GitHub CI.

## Deploy notes

To send mail in production, set `SMTP_ADDRESS` / `SMTP_USERNAME` / `SMTP_PASSWORD` + `MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS` (e.g. Resend) on the host. Until `SMTP_ADDRESS` is present, delivery is safely off and queued reset emails are dropped rather than retried.

author: anorme
body:
## Description
This branch connects the dynamic form builder foundation to events by allowing admins to configure registration forms per event. It adds a registration form reference on events, admin endpoints to create or update the linked form schema, and a route to retrieve the current form configuration. This unblocks attendee and checkout flows that need to collect event-specific registration details.

## Key changes
- Add `registrationFormId` to the `Event` model as a reference to `FormSchema`.
- Add model support for setting and populating an event’s registration form.
- Add `eventFormService` helpers for checking supported event types and extracting linked form IDs.
- Add admin `PUT` and `GET` routes for event registration form configuration.
- Reuse `formSchemaValidator` through new `validateFormSchema` middleware.
- Add controller logic to create a new form schema when none is linked, or update the existing linked form schema.
- Add unit tests for free/paid registration form support, linked form ID handling, and shared form validation for event registration flows.

## Summary

- **Open-ended LLM classifier**: instead of hardcoded `credit_card_transaction | other`, the classifier now builds its category list dynamically. `AddKnownType()` lets new categories be registered at runtime (seeded from learned rules on startup; called immediately when the user teaches a new rule via the UI).
- **Review queue** (`internal/review`): unhandled emails are persisted to `review_queue.json` instead of being silently dropped. Deduplicates by Gmail message ID.
- **Web UI at `/review` and `/rules`**: three actions per queued email:
  1. **Reclassify + Reprocess** — LLM got the category wrong; pick the correct existing handler and reprocess now.
  2. **Teach new rule** — write an extraction prompt, pick `import_transaction` or `log_only`, confirm. Rule saved and handler registered immediately across all account routers.
  3. **Ignore** — discard from queue.
- **Learned rules store** (`internal/rules`): `learned_rules.json` persists user-taught rules. Loaded at startup; handlers registered before pollers start.
- **LearnedHandler** (`internal/handlers/learned`): generic handler using `ExtractWithPrompt`. Reuses the same account resolution and JN-66 import pipeline as the CC handler — no new JN-66 integration needed.
- **Router**: gains `SetQueuer`, `HandleDirect`, `RegisteredTypes`, and a `sync.RWMutex` on the handlers map for safe concurrent registration.
- **No DB** — two JSON files, same pattern as `state.json`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `go build ./cmd/ap5` compiles
- [ ] `go test ./...` — 83 tests pass (23 new tests across 4 new/updated packages)
- [ ] `go vet ./...` — no issues
- [ ] Start `ap5 serve`, send an email that isn't a CC transaction, visit `/review` — email appears in the queue with an LLM-suggested category
- [ ] On the detail page, try "Reprocess" with `credit_card_transaction` if it was misclassified — email processed, removed from queue
- [ ] Try "Teach" with a new category + extraction prompt — rule appears on `/rules`, future emails of that type are handled automatically
- [ ] Try "Ignore" — email removed from queue, no rule created
- [ ] Restart `ap5 serve` — learned rules reloaded, LLM classifier seeded, handlers re-registered

## Summary

Fixes both CRITICAL defects in issue #926 (synthesis fails + dead silicon) for the BitNet HLS engine-top.

**Bug 1 — `multilayer_sequencer` instantiated but never emitted.**
`bitnet_top.rs` instantiated `multilayer_sequencer` by name, but no emitter produced it, so synthesis failed with an unresolved module reference. This PR adds `build_multilayer_sequencer` in `bitnet_pipeline.rs` — a 6-state layer-driver FSM whose port contract matches the instance exactly (`clk, rst_n, start, num_layers[5:0], layer_done, prefetch_done` -> `current_layer[5:0], layer_start, start_prefetch, inference_done`) — and registers it in the bundle.

**Bug 2 — 7 of 9 RTL modules unwired.**
`bitnet_engine_top` only wired `multilayer_sequencer` + `double_buffer_ctrl`; the other 7 modules were emitted as standalone IPs with no structural data path. The engine-top now wires all nine into a coherent path:

```
weight_prefetch_ctrl --(AXI read)--> weight_bram --(rd_data)--> pipeline_stage2_compute
        ^ start_prefetch                                   ^ driven by layer_sequencer (layer_start)
axi_lite_slave (CSR) -> run params ;  dma_controller (activation move) ;  interrupt_controller (irq)
```

`mem_addr`/`mem_rd_en` are now driven from the prefetch AXI read channel instead of constants. A single `tieoff_obs` observability net folds sub-module outputs that have no top-level port at this integration level, so synthesis retains every block without multiple drivers.

## Verification

- `cargo test --bin t27c bitnet`: 129 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: 1423 passed, only the 6 pre-existing baseline failures (unrelated), 0 new regressions.
- The complete generated bundle (all 11 SV modules) elaborates cleanly under `iverilog -g2012 -s bitnet_engine_top` (only the external W33 `trit27_dot_product` primitive is supplied separately at synthesis time).
- New tests: `multilayer_*` (5), `all_nine_submodules_instantiated_926`, `datapath_chains_prefetch_bram_compute_926`, plus bundle-count tests bumped 11->12.

## Constitutional notes

- L6 gf16 SSOT untouched; `specs/numeric/formats_catalog.t27` unchanged (catalog stays 83).
- No `gen/` edits; ASCII-only changed lines; no quality/performance claim added.
- Anchor: phi^2 + phi^-2 = 3.

Closes #926

author: mswilkison
body:
## What

Gives the two remaining operator-key-signed ROAST bodies — `LocalEvidenceSnapshot` and `TransitionMessage` — their own **distinct domain tags**, completing the cross-protocol signature-confusion sweep started for the signing-package envelope on #4056.

The node's operator key signs all of these bodies (snapshots as a member; transition messages + the signing package as the elected coordinator), and their protobuf bodies are wire-compatible (each begins with a field-1 attempt-context binding). Without domain separation, a signature over one body could be presented as a signature over another. #4056 added a tag to the signing package; a reviewer correctly noted the existing snapshot/transition bodies still signed bare bodies, so this PR closes that gap.

## How

- **Distinct domain tags**, each beginning with byte `0x00` — an **illegal protobuf tag** (field number 0) — so the signed payload is undecodable as any protobuf message:
  - `\x00roast/signed-evidence-snapshot/v1\x00`
  - `\x00roast/signed-transition-message/v1\x00`

  This separates the domains in **both directions without relying on field layout**: a signature over one body can't be accepted on another envelope (its decoder `proto.Unmarshal`s and rejects the `0x00`-leading body), and a genuine serialized protobuf body always starts `>= 0x08`, so its signature can never verify against `domain || body`. Same construction as the signing-package fix on #4056.
- **`bodyBytes()` / `SignableBytes()` split**: `bodyBytes()` is the bare body that travels on the wire (embedded by `wireEnvelopeBytes` / `Marshal`); `SignableBytes()` is `domain || body`, the only thing signed/verified. Both `Unmarshal` paths reset the signable-bytes cache so a reused receiver never verifies against stale bytes.
- Renamed the bare-body cache `signedBody` → `bodyCache` and added `signaturePayloadCache`, so all three signed-body types share one structure.

## Compatibility

Sign and verify both flow through `SignableBytes()`, so the change is **transparent to the sign sites** and the **wire envelope structure is unchanged**. It **does** change the bytes signed, so signatures are not compatible with the pre-change protocol — **all nodes must run the new code together**. Acceptable pre-mainnet; the external-audit gate is unchanged.

## Testing

`gofmt` / `go vet` / `go build ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` clean; full `pkg/frost/roast` suite green. New `domain_separation_test.go` pins, for both bodies: domain tagging, undecodability as protobuf, the bare (untagged) wire body, prefix-free distinctness of the tags, and the reused-receiver cache reset. Existing verbatim/round-trip/verify tests continue to pass.

## What & why

Ellie & Grace now accept Venmo and want to ship orders, so this adds online payment and a delivery option to the previously cash-only, pickup-only flow.

## Venmo payments
- Pays `@Kelly-Corcoran` via `https://account.venmo.com/pay?recipients=Kelly-Corcoran&amount=<total>&note=...&txn=pay`, with the order total and a note pre-filled.
- **Mobile** (`lg:hidden`): a tap-to-pay "Pay $X with Venmo" button that opens Venmo.
- **Desktop** (`hidden lg:flex`): a QR code of that same pay link to scan with a phone (so the amount is pre-filled on scan too).
- Responsive switching is Tailwind-only, matching the site's existing pattern (no user-agent JS, no hydration mismatch).
- The QR is generated dynamically with `qrcode.react` from the pay link. If a branded QR image is preferred, it can be dropped into `public/` and swapped in.

- Order form gains a Pickup/Delivery selector; Delivery reveals a **required** mailing-address field (also validated server-side in `app/actions.ts`).

- Admin dashboard shows a Pickup/Delivery badge and the shipping address; the order notification email includes them too.
- "Cash only" copy across Hero, order form, success screen, and email updated to "Venmo or cash · Pickup or delivery", with messaging that adapts to the chosen method.

body:
## Root Cause
mem-load container memory limit (32Mi) is insufficient for stress command allocation (50M), causing OOM kills.

## Evidence
- rollout_status condition: ReplicaFailure status=True reason=FailedCreate
- mem-load container resources.limits.memory=32Mi but stress command allocates --vm-bytes 50M

## Fix
Increased mem-load container memory limit from 32Mi to 64Mi to accommodate the 50M stress allocation with headroom.

author: mikecranesync
body:
Closes #1950.

## Problems fixed
1. **`Mark Complete` was toast-only / non-persistent.** It now calls a real backend endpoint, persists, and survives a reload.
2. **Trigger buttons used a hardcoded `/hub/api` path.** Now use `${API_BASE}/api/...` (base-path-correct for both `/hub` and root deployments).
3. **Trigger changes had no response/error handling.** They now check `res.ok`, surface API errors as toasts, and sync local state.
4. **Demo/Playwright tenant had zero PMs.** The seed file is now self-contained synthetic data, not a copy from the `mike` tenant.

## Changes
- **New `POST /api/pm-schedules/[id]/complete`** — stamps `last_completed_at = NOW()`, rolls `next_due_at` forward by the schedule interval, bumps `updated_at` (so the cmms-sync worker pushes the change to Atlas), and resets the meter cycle (`meter_current = 0`, `meter_last_reset_at = NOW()`) for meter-based PMs. Completion is kept to schedule roll-forward — a completion-history table / WO-spawn is a separate feature, and the issue's acceptance criteria use "or recalculate the next due date".
- **`schedule/page.tsx`** — `Mark Complete` and trigger buttons now go through the endpoints with `res.ok` checks + success/failure toasts. A new `applyPMPatch` syncs the server response into local state so the optimistic update matches what a reload (`GET`) derives: `status="completed"` + `date` = the recalculated future `next_due_at`.
- **Extracted `addInterval` to `src/lib/pm-interval.ts`** — shared by the meter-reset and complete paths so the two stay in lockstep (was duplicated in `meter/route.ts`).
- **Rewrote `tools/seed_demo_tenant_pms.sql`** — self-contained synthetic, parameterized `:tenant_id` (default demo `…d1`, the tenant `demo-auth.ts` + the e2e specs use), idempotent on `(tenant_id, manufacturer, model_number, task)`. 6 PMs covering overdue / scheduled / critical / meter-progress / calendar-or-meter / recently-completed. **Behavior change:** the old file targeted tenant `78917b56…` and copied from the `mike` tenant (which only exists on prod) — that dependency is why the demo tenant rendered empty.
- i18n keys `completeFailedToast` / `triggerUpdatedToast` / `triggerFailedToast` in all 4 locales.
- Route tests for the complete endpoint.

## Known follow-up (out of scope)
The PATCH route returns **400** when switching a PM to a meter trigger without a `meter_threshold` — and there is no threshold *input* in this sheet (it only displays current/threshold). That 400 now correctly surfaces as an error toast (per the acceptance criteria), but **setting meter mode from this UI still needs a threshold input** — tracked as a follow-up, not in this PR.

## Verification (evidence)
- `npx vitest run src/app/api/pm-schedules` → **7/7 pass** (complete endpoint: 503/401/400-uuid/404/calendar-complete/meter-reset/500).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → **zero new errors** in touched files (8 pre-existing errors on `main` in unrelated test files: `namespace/tree`, `auth/rls-deny`, `sitemap-drift`).
- `npx eslint` on all touched files → **clean**.
- `npx next build` → **exit 0**; `/api/pm-schedules/[id]/complete` compiled.
- **Seed executed against the dev NeonDB inside a rolled-back transaction** → `demo_pm_total=6, meter_pms=2`, then `ROLLBACK` (no persisted change). Confirms the SQL parses, the jsonb/`make_interval` casts work, and idempotency holds.

## Live QA note
Production QA + screenshots could not be run from this session (no prod access by policy; Colima/psql unavailable locally). To verify on a live env after deploy:
```
psql "$NEON_DATABASE_URL_DEV" -f tools/seed_demo_tenant_pms.sql   # seeds demo tenant d1
```
then open `/schedule`, click a PM → `Mark Complete` (persists across reload), and toggle a trigger (calendar PM updates; switching to meter without a threshold shows an error toast).

author: your-moon
body:
## Why (real-hardware finding)
On device `864253060829892` (dev broker), **6/6 popup_sn commands with a deliberately stale timestamp ejected a bank** (`0x01`), never `0x88` — including a **2-hour-stale** command. Varied staleness (60s/300s/1800s/7200s/30s) all ejecting rules out clock skew. **This firmware does not honor `timestamp+ttl`.** (Our payload was verified character-for-character against the protocol spec — topic `/user/get`, `cmd=popup_sn`, string `timestamp`/`ttl` in seconds — so it is the firmware, not our usage.)

## Why that disqualifies QoS 1 for dispense
A dispense is a **non-idempotent physical action**; MQTT QoS 1 is **at-least-once**:
- A lost PUBACK → broker redelivers (`DUP=1`) → firmware ejects a **second bank** (double-eject). Clean sessions do not fix this.
- A delayed redelivery → **late eject** after the user has left.
- The `timestamp+ttl` was the only plausible freshness/dedup key, and the firmware ignores it.

So QoS 1 on the money-path dispense risks double- and late-eject. Revert to **QoS 0** (single fire-and-forget — no redelivery, no double/late eject; same as the long-standing prod behavior).

## What stays
This reverts **only** the popup QoS. Everything else from the prior hardening remains: the timestamp+ttl payload (documented form), the bounded `WaitTimeout`, the **0x31 parse-panic fix**, the **callback recover**, and the **net/http UserService** (race + axios4go removal).

## Reliability instead
The reliability QoS 1 was meant to buy (no lost dispenses) belongs **application-side**: re-pop with a *fresh* timestamp after a positive non-dispense check (backend, gated by the popup-refund positive-evidence logic). That depends on neither firmware TTL nor broker redelivery and cannot double- or late-eject.

## Test
`go build` ✓ · `go vet` ✓ · `go test ./...` → 23 passed.

Suggest tagging this **v1.1.5** after merge; backend bumps dev→prod from v1.1.4 to v1.1.5.

author: mibrahimdev
body:
## Bug
On mobile widths (360–414px), the marketing + docs site **trimmed/cut off text on the right edge** instead of wrapping. Examples:
- Landing hero rendered **"The eye that sees"** as **"The eye that see"** and **"your app says"** as **"your a…"**.
- Protocol-card body text was clipped on the right.
- The docs **API tables** (`getting-started`, `ai-exports`) had their second column pushed off-screen, and long inline `<code>` paths/identifiers overflowed.

## Root cause
The site sets `body { overflow-x: hidden }` (style.css:56), which converts **any** horizontal overflow into a *silent trim* rather than a scrollbar. Two things were overflowing on mobile:

1. **Grid-track inflation (landing).** The mobile single-column grids use `grid-template-columns: 1fr` = `minmax(auto, 1fr)`. The `auto` minimum grows to the largest child's *min-content*. The `.capture` panel and `.proto-snippet` use `white-space: nowrap`, giving them a ~407px min-content — which inflated the track and **stretched the adjacent hero / card text columns past the viewport**, where `.hero { overflow: hidden }` clipped them.
2. **Unbreakable tokens (docs).** `table.api td:first-child { white-space: nowrap }` plus long inline `<code>` tokens (`SharinganExport.sessionJson(events)`, `sharingan/build/XCFrameworks/release/Sharingan.xcframework`, `./gradlew :shared:embedAndSignAppleFrameworkForXcode`) have no break opportunities, so they forced cells/paragraphs wider than the screen.

## Fix
Minimal CSS, **entirely inside the existing mobile breakpoints** (`@media (max-width: 880px)` / `860px`) — desktop CSS is untouched:

**`landing.css`**
- `.hero-grid` → `minmax(0, 1fr)` and `.capture { min-width: 0 }` so the panel shrinks below its nowrap min-content (rows still ellipsize — intended terminal look).
- `.proto-card { min-width: 0 }` so cards shrink and the code snippet scrolls inside (it already has `overflow-x: auto`).
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on inline code in the quickstart / agent / noop sections.

**`docs.css`**
- `table.api td:first-child { white-space: normal }` so function names wrap.
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on inline `<code>` in paragraphs, list items, table cells and callouts.

## Verification
Reproduced and fixed with Playwright at **360 / 390 / 414px** on all four pages.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Landing (360px) | `scrollWidth=433` > viewport; hero text clipped ("see") | `scrollWidth=360`; all text wraps/fits |
| getting-started | `scrollWidth=558`; table + code clipped | `scrollWidth=360`; clean |
| ai-exports | `scrollWidth=460`; PRODUCES column clipped | `scrollWidth=360`; clean |
| integrations | ok | ok |

Zero remaining overflow drivers at all three widths. **Desktop (1280px) confirmed visually identical** (`scrollWidth == innerWidth`), as expected since all changes are media-query-scoped.
