The focused row is also kept in view during keyboard navigation.

## Root-cause fix (the enabler)

The columns used `VerticalScrollBarVisibility = Disabled`, which in Avalonia pins the content to the viewport — i.e. **the columns were never actually scrollable** (`Extent == Viewport`, any offset clamps to 0, and rows past the visible ~3–4 were unreachable). Changed to `Hidden` (scrollable, no visible scrollbar). The auto-centering rides on top of that.

## Implementation

- `Open()` captures both column `ScrollViewer`s (via a `captureScroll` callback added to `BuildColumn`).
- `ScheduleScrollToSelection` centers the target row: `offset = clamp(rowCenter − viewport/2, 0, extent − viewport)`. If the column is already laid out it centers immediately; otherwise it hooks a one-shot `EffectiveViewportChanged` and centers once the viewport/bounds are valid, then unsubscribes. The handler is `static` (captures the scroll viewer and row, not the picker — no leak), and the fields are nulled on close.
- Row `GotFocus` calls `BringIntoView()` for keyboard navigation.

## Quality

Put through an adversarial multi-agent review (3 dimensions, per-finding verification). The correctness-timing and regression dimensions came back **clean**. Three confirmed **test-quality** gaps were fixed before this PR:
- Tests only checked `Offset.Y > 0` → now assert the selected row is actually **visible** in the viewport, and that a mid-list selection (`12:30`) lands **centered** (±3px).
- The column-lookup helper was child-order-fragile → now finds a column by its **heading** text.
- Added a null-`Time` default test and a `MinuteStep` rounding test (`18:50` step 15 → the visible minute-`45` row).

## Verification

- Build **0 warnings / 0 errors** (solution).
- Full suite **503 passing** (+6 TimePicker tests; updated 1 pre-existing assertion `Disabled` → `Hidden`).
- Gallery: "Opens at selected time" sample. Docs: pickers.md behavioral note; changelog 3.11.0.

author: charlesangus
body:
Fixes #11 — the palette hitches on Tab, worst on the first invocation of a session.

## Root cause

Two GUI-thread costs land together on the first open, and the existing preload/fingerprint/row-op machinery targeted neither:

1. **Eager colour resolution across every candidate.** `NodeModel.update()` called `color_fn` (`nuke.defaultNodeColor`) for *every matched item* before sorting and capping to `num_items`. Colour is never used for scoring — only the ≤18 visible rows are painted. On the first invocation the input box is empty, so **every** menu item matches and colour was resolved for the entire menu set (hundreds–thousands of host API calls) to show 18 rows. This is exactly why the hitch is "at least on first invocation": every later open pre-fills a narrow filter.

2. **An unconditional forced full re-walk on every open.** `_refresh_fresh` ran `invalidate_cache()` + `get_items()`, re-walking with `.script()`/`.shortcut()` per item (~100–400ms) on every open regardless of the fingerprint cache — and on first open could stack with the first tick's walk. It also wiped the colour cache mid-open, so cost (1) couldn't amortize.

## Fixes (one commit each)

- **Resolve colour only for the visible window.** Cap the sorted list to `num_items` first, then resolve colour for those survivors — O(num_items) per update instead of O(matches). Icons were already lazy; colour now matches.
- **Stop forcing a per-open re-walk.** The forced walk only existed to catch deep menu changes the shallow depth-2 fingerprint missed. `_menu_fingerprint` now recurses the full tree (names only — still far cheaper than a real walk), so `get_items()`'s own change detection reliably catches deep installs and the popup trusts it: an unchanged menu set reuses the preloaded cache and pays no walk on open. Colour/preference edits (which don't change menu structure) are handled by a new lightweight `invalidate_color_cache()` hook called each open — cheap now that colour is lazy.

## Alternatives considered

- *Preload harder/earlier* — already done; doesn't touch the per-open refresh that re-walks and recolours regardless.
- *Background-thread the walk/colour* — Nuke's menu API and the Qt model are main-thread-only; unsafe.
- *Cache colour permanently* — reintroduces staleness on default-colour preference edits; the lazy-visible approach is fast and fresh.
- *Drop `_refresh_fresh` entirely* — loses the deep-change safety net; the deeper fingerprint keeps it while removing the cost.

## Tests

`pytest tests/` → 31 passed (was 25). New coverage:
- colour resolved at most `num_items` times for a broad/empty filter, and exactly per-match below the window;
- full-depth fingerprint detects a change below the old depth-2 bound;
- `invalidate_color_cache` clears only colour; `invalidate_cache` clears everything.

Consolidates the two markdownlint config files into a single `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`:

**Why this is safe (answers the issue's "why two?"):** CI runs `markdownlint-cli2-action`
inline (`lint-md-links.yml`) — the org `lint-md-links` reusable workflow is not callable
from this repo's Actions settings, so there is no separate tool that needs to detect a
standalone `.markdownlint.jsonc`. markdownlint-cli2 auto-discovers `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`
and honors its `config` key for rules; `make docs-lint` passes globs explicitly on the CLI.
Deleting the standalone file is required (cli2 merges both and the standalone copy wins for
conflicting rules).

Lint behavior is identical: `make docs-lint` passes (0 markdownlint errors, 0 lychee errors).

author: joelteply
body:
## Seam #3.2 (IDENTITY-SCOPE-PEER-LIVENESS-MODEL) — the liveness spine, slice 1

The trust store records **who** a peer is (pubkey), **how much** we trust it (tier), and **where** to reach it (endpoints) — but never **when** we last had contact. Without recency the substrate cannot age a peer out: a friend who enrolled a year ago and one we exchanged a beacon with this minute are indistinguishable, so liveness-based eviction (`airc peer prune`'s age dimension) has nothing to read.

This is the **substrate dimension only**, mirroring how the `tier` column (card 34942ec1 Sub-A) landed as the column first, with detection/policy on top. The beacon/dial *touch* wiring and the age-based *eviction classifier* are follow-up slices that build on this column.

### What's in this slice
- **migration `m20260614_000017`** — additive nullable `last_seen_ms`. NULL is the pre-migration state; the read layer floors it to `added_at_ms` (enrolment is the oldest defensible "last contact"), so **no backfill** and no pre-migration friend reads as instantly stale.
- **`StoredPeer.last_seen_ms: u64`** — concrete recency floor, never `None`.
- **`add`** seeds `last_seen` to the enrolment instant; **`replace` (rotation)** preserves it — a key-material event is not fresh contact — same invariant as tier/endpoints across rotate.
- **`touch_peer_last_seen(peer_id, seen_at_ms)`** — **monotonic** write path: an older timestamp is a no-op so clock skew / out-of-order beacon import never rewinds recency. `Ok(None)` on an un-enrolled peer (no implicit insert — recency without a trust anchor is meaningless).
- **`airc_trust::touch_last_seen`** passthrough for the higher layer.

### Tests (5, all green)
`add_peer_trust_seeds_last_seen_to_added_at`, `touch_peer_last_seen_advances_and_is_monotonic`, `touch_peer_last_seen_unknown_peer_returns_none_no_row_inserted`, `replace_peer_trust_preserves_last_seen`, `stored_last_seen_ms_floors_null_to_added_at`.

### Follow-up slices (stacked on this)
1. **Touch wiring** — call `touch_last_seen` from beacon import + successful dial.
2. **Age-based eviction classifier** — extend `classify_peer_prune` (#1186) with a staleness dimension reading `last_seen_ms` against a TTL.

author: jakechampion
body:
## What

Slice 1 of **block-expressions**: `{ stmt; …; tailExpr }` runs the statements in a fresh child scope, then the trailing expression (written **without** a `;`) is the value. Enables multi-statement value-position branches:

```fern
var x: i32 = if (e > 0) { var k = e + 1; k } else { 0 };
var s: string = match (t) { 0 => { var v = lookup(t); v }, _ => "x" };
```

**Interpreter-only** in slice 1; compiled backends reject cleanly (mirrors the `dyn`/`as?` interp-first cadence).

## Why a node, not a desugar

Two facts ruled out the cheap "desugar to IIFE" path: Fern **lambdas don't infer return types** (can't carry the tail's type), and Fern **requires `;` on every statement** (so a trailing-expr-without-`;` is a *new* grammar form). Hence a real `BlockExpr` node + a small grammar addition. **Scope: `if`/`match` expression branches only** — the position where `{` is unambiguous; general value-position blocks (struct-literal clash) + codegen + self-host are later slices.

## How

- **`ast.go`**: `BlockExpr{Stmts, Tail}` (`Tail==nil` ⇒ value-less/void).
- **`parser.go`**: `parseBranchBody` + `branchStmtStart`, wired into `parseIfExpr` (then/else) + match-expr arms. Keyword-led items → statements; a non-keyword item is an `ExprStmt` if `;` follows else the trailing tail. `if`/`match`/`switch` are **not** statement-starts → nested if-expr-as-tail + `else if` chains stay byte-identical; a no-statement single-expr branch collapses to a bare expr (existing branches unchanged). Statement-position `if`/`match` untouched.
- **`checker.go`**: `checkBlockExpr` (child scope → stmts → tail type); new **E061** for a value-less block in value position; numeric-tail flow (`settleInt`/`settleFloat`/`postSettleType`); branch-type unification flows through the tail.
- **`interp.go`**: child env → stmts → `Tail`; `return`/`break`/`continue` inside a value-block errors cleanly.
- **`ir.go`**: `rejectBlockExpr` + guard arm — clean message, no panic on any backend.
- **13 walkers** wired (walk, monomorph, closureconv, boxcapture, modload, shadowrename, treeshake, printer, format, constfold, checker walkers).
- **`docs/BLOCK-EXPRESSIONS.md`**: spec + rationale + later slices.

**Drive-by fix:** the formatter dropped literal-pattern arms in match-*expressions* (`0 => …` → `=> …`, failed to re-parse) — fixed + guarded.

## Tests / verification (local)

- Parser (5), checker (2), IR reject (1), interp e2e `TestBlockExprInterp` (6 sub-cases) + `TestBlockExprCompiledReject{,CLI}` (wasm/x86-64/arm64 reject, no panic), format round-trip + literal-arm regression.
- Green: `go build ./...`; parser/checker/ast/interp/ir/monomorph/printer/constfold units; `BlockExpr|IfExpr|MatchExpr|Format|FeatureDifferential` e2e (183s) — single-expr + statement-position `if`/`match` unaffected.

## Next slices

Compiled codegen (the self-host `irlower` already lowers multi-statement value bodies — this unblocks it), then self-host parser support, then optionally general value-position block-expressions.

author: astraldev
body:
# v5

Rewrite of GGate (formerly GLogic) onto GTK 4 / libadwaita. New simulation playback,
a themed component icon set, runtime theming, a meson build, and CI/packaging.

## Runtime / platform
- GTK 4 + libadwaita app with a Cairo-rendered canvas. Requires Python `>=3.10`,
  GTK `>=4.16`, libadwaita `>=1.6.8`. Runtime deps: pygobject, pycairo, python-igraph,
  shapely, packaging.
- App id `org.astralco.ggate` (`.Dev` in the development profile).
- Dialogs moved to libadwaita equivalents (`Adw.Dialog`, `Adw.AlertDialog`, `Adw.HeaderBar`).

## Simulation engine + playback
- The simulation now runs in two phases. First it computes the whole run to completion in
  small background slices so the UI stays responsive, recording every timestep
  (`CircuitManager.begin_compute`/`compute_slice`, frames in `component_state_history`).
  Then it plays those recorded frames back — playback never re-runs the engine.
- Playback lives in its own class, `CircuitPlaybackAnimation`. It owns the transport state
  (`computing → playing ⇄ paused → ended/idle`) and the play/pause/restart/seek/stop actions.
  `CircuitManager` stays the engine and data layer.
- Playback speed targets a total duration rather than a fixed frame delay, clamped to a
  16–200 ms/frame range. The target is a new "Animation duration" preference.
- Circuits that don't change over time (e.g. no oscillator) skip playback and just show the
  final state; the playback bar doesn't appear for them.
- Editing a property or flipping a switch mid-run throws away the recorded run and recomputes
  from the start with the new value (`MainFrame.recompute_simulation`), so what you see always
  matches the current circuit. A switch keeps its toggled state across that recompute.
- The original synchronous run path is still available for non-GUI use.

## UI
- New floating playback bar (`PlaybackControls`). `DrawArea` changed from a scrolled window
  into an overlay that wraps the scroller, so the bar stays pinned over the canvas while the
  content scrolls underneath. Controls: Stop · Restart · Play/Pause, then a seek slider and a
  fixed-width time readout that doesn't jitter as it updates. The bar's Stop ends the run.
  The header simulation control is now just Play/Stop.
- Component sidebar with search and categories.
- Preferences rebuilt as an `Adw.PreferencesDialog` (Appearance / Simulation / Canvas);
  its widgets are built once and reused.
- Timing diagram rebuilt as a dialog with scale/range/save controls, scroll-synced panes,
  drag-to-scrub, theme-aware waveforms, and a warning when the diagram hits Cairo's width limit.

## Theming + icons
- Built-in light and dark themes (Classic, Space, Frappé, Mocha) defined as JSON in
  `data/themes/` and loaded at runtime; switchable from Preferences (logic in `Themes.py`).
- Hand-drawn component icons in two symbol sets (ANSI and IEC); icon spec documented in
  `data/images/components/spec.md`.

## Build / packaging / CI
- meson build (resource compile, install, generated `config.py`, desktop + AppStream files).
  In development, `run.py` regenerates and registers the dev resource bundle on each launch so
  it can't go stale.
- GitHub Actions (Fedora container) produce a `meson dist` tarball; flatpak/snap/deb workflows
  run only on releases. Version unified to 5.0.0.

## Docs / assets
- README (requirements, run steps, screenshots, v1→v5 history), NEWS 5.0.0, INSTALL, TODO.
- `gallery/`: screenshots captured by `build-aux/capture_screenshots.py` (themes, playback,
  timing, preferences, properties) and a 1080p demo clip produced by `build-aux/make_demo.sh`.

## Notable fixes
- Oscillators now produce timing history.
- Unconnected input pins no longer crash the simulator.
- `.glc` files load their property values with the correct types.
- libadwaita styling, property-dialog behaviour, running-mode crashes, first-paint centering,
  and a zoom clamp (0.5–20).

## Known / deferred
- `pytest` and its config are present but there is no `tests/` directory yet.
- Long playbacks run past the target duration (no frame subsampling); there's no playback speed
  control beyond the duration preference, and no progress indicator during compute.
- Switch toggles during a run aren't recorded in undo history and don't mark the file modified.

body:
## What this is

Reconstructs the **Market Pulse** weekly newsletter as a repeatable, auto-fetching generator — matching the layout/styling of `market_pulse_june2_2026.html`. Previously the issue was hand-built in a terminal session; nothing in the repo built it. This makes it reproducible.

## Pipeline

1. **Fetch** live market data from free APIs.
2. **Merge** curated manual figures from `data/overrides.yaml` (the stats no free API exposes).
3. **Narrate** with Claude (optional) — News headlines, Quick Read, section intros, "Bottom Line" bullets. Falls back to `overrides.yaml` prose when no API key.
4. **Render** the house-styled HTML, and optionally a PDF.

## Live vs. manual

| Live (auto) | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks (S&P, Dow, Nasdaq, Russell, VIX), oil (WTI/Brent), commodities (gold, silver, copper, corn, soy, cattle), world (Japan, China) | Stooq |
| Crypto (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP) | CoinGecko |
| Rates (2y/10y/30y, 30y mortgage) | FRED (free key) |

Manual (`overrides.yaml`): Fed policy rate, Savings & CD specials, gas prices, Crop Weather, Real Estate distress, Household Finance, Europe/EM, Upcoming Events.

## Editorial color logic

Each metric carries a `polarity` (`GOOD` → a rise is favourable/green; `BAD` → a rise is unfavourable/red), reproducing the sample exactly (e.g. VIX↑ red, S&P↑ green, gold↓ red, cattle↑ red).

## Try it

```bash
cd automation
pip install -r requirements.txt
python generate.py --no-fetch --no-narrative   # reproduces the seeded June 2 issue, fully offline
python generate.py --pdf                        # live data + PDF
```

## Notes / decisions
- Data source = **auto-fetch** (per request).
- Narrative defaults to **Claude** when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, else templated fallbacks — so it still produces a complete issue offline.
- Data hosts must be reachable; on a restricted egress allowlist add `stooq.com`, `api.coingecko.com`, `api.stlouisfed.org`, `api.anthropic.com`. GitHub Actions runners have open egress.
- Weekly `.github/workflows/market-pulse.yml` (Mondays + manual) commits issues to `automation/output/`; needs `FRED_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as Actions secrets.

## Open questions for review
- **Gas prices** (national/CA/Indiana) are currently manual. I can wire these to the EIA API (free key) if you want them auto too.
- **Crop progress** could be auto-fetched from the USDA NASS QuickStats API — left manual for now since it needs section-by-section mapping.

author: jperla
body:
Follow-up to #553 (the manifest unblock, now merged). Once the Linux/macOS lanes finally compiled, `swift test` ran for the first time in weeks and exposed pre-existing latent test-suite issues that had been masked by the compile failures.

## Fixes

1. **`macos-ci.yml` — cap the best-effort test step.** The `Build all 4 apps + test` required check kept getting *cancelled*: its final `swift test` step is `continue-on-error: true`, which tolerates a step failure but **not** a step that never returns. A post-suite hang (a test or spawned subprocess that doesn't exit) burns the 30-min job budget and cancels the job, turning the check red despite every build passing. A step-level `timeout-minutes: 15` kills only the hang.

2. **Serialize `DownloadCacheTests`.** `DownloadCache` observes the **global** `.appDidGoToBackground` / `.lowMemory` on `NotificationCenter.default` and responds with `removeAll()`. Two tests in the suite post those notifications; Swift Testing runs them in parallel, so one test's post fires another's cache observer and clears `cache["k"]` before its `#expect`. `.serialized` scopes each post to the test that intends it.

## Still open (documented, not in this PR)

The Linux `Swift Linux Backends` job was observed hanging ~2h+. It does **not** reproduce locally (the full suite builds+tests in <55 min, exit 1, even under `--cpuset-cpus="0-1"`), so it's environment-specific — most likely a post-suite spawned subprocess (GTK/Xvfb) that never exits, or runner memory thrash during the huge cold build. `linux-swift-test.sh` has no step timeout; a similar cap there is the likely next step. The `SourceHygieneTests` git-128 seen locally is a worktree-`.git`-not-mounted artifact (green on a normal CI clone).

body:
Restyle `ant serve` into a console-looking surface: one monospace face throughout, square corners everywhere, and flat panels on a tinted canvas with no shadows, no dividing rules, and no rounding.

## What changed
- **Font.** Embed Geist Mono (variable, latin subset) and serve it from the binary, so the console stays a single static artifact with no CDN. The face is preloaded and registered as `font/woff2`; `--sans` now points at the monospace stack, so headings, body, and chrome all share it.
- **No rounding.** `--radius`, `--radius-sm`, and `--radius-lg` are all `0`, and every literal corner (pills, chips, inputs, buttons, the brand mark) is squared. The only curve left is the loading spinner, which has to be a circle to read as a spinner.
- **No shadows, no borders.** Every `box-shadow` and the shadow tokens are gone. Inputs, chips, badges, folders, cards, and hovers separate by background fill rather than rules. The topbar's `border-bottom`, the sidebar's `border-right`, and the table cell rules are removed.
- **Type.** 14px base, dropped the Inter feature settings and the negative tracking that looked cramped on a fixed-width face.

## Verification

author: tobenhair
body:
## Summary

Quest kill and loot counters now **start from zero when you accept the quest**, instead of inheriting your lifetime totals. Previously a quest like "kill 15 Slimes" could be instantly (or partly) complete because `isQDone`/`qProg` read the global lifetime `G.kills` and current inventory — so prior kills/loot counted, and accepting a quest you'd already over-progressed showed it done immediately.

### How
- New per-quest progress state `G.questProg[id] = {kills:{}, items:{}}`, **reset to zero by `acceptQ`** on acceptance.
- `killM` and `addItem` call a new `questCredit('kill'|'col', key)` that advances every *active* quest with a matching task.
- `qCount(id, task)` reads the per-quest count; `isQDone` and `qProg` both go through it (no longer reading lifetime `G.kills` / inventory qty).
- A nice side effect: because collection now counts at **loot time** (in `addItem`), relics that auto-route to the Storage Chest on a full bag still count toward the quest — fixing the earlier caveat.

### Persistence
- `questProg` added to the `G` initializer, `saveGame()`, and `applySave()`.
- **Migration:** pre-`questProg` saves seed each *active* quest's progress from the legacy lifetime-kills / inventory counts (capped at the requirement), so a quest you're mid-way through isn't wiped by the update. From then on, every accept resets to zero.

### Tests
- New: "accepting a quest resets its counters — prior lifetime kills/loot do not count" and "killing and looting credit active quests (counters advance from zero)".
- Updated the q1/q14 completion tests to drive the per-quest counters.
- Full suite: **75/75 pass** locally. `CLAUDE.md` updated.

Bounties already reset per-acceptance (`genBounty` sets `p:0`), so they were unaffected.

author: sergio-salcedo-dev
body:
Closes #254.

## What

Maps the existing `StoredObject` value object as a Doctrine `#[ORM\Embeddable]` and replaces `Bank`'s four inline `stored_object_*` columns with a single `#[ORM\Embedded(columnPrefix: 'stored_object_')]` property. A logo is an attribute of the aggregate (a value object), not an entity — and future aggregates (avatars, supplier/company logos…) now adopt the cluster with one declaration instead of four columns.

## Why no migration

Each embeddable field pins an explicit column `name` (`key` / `mime_type` / `byte_size` / `content_hash`); `columnPrefix + name` reproduces the existing column names exactly. `make db.diff` reports **No changes detected** — zero schema drift, no migration. Verified as a mandatory mapping checkpoint right after the mapping change.

## Changes

- `StoredObject` → `#[ORM\Embeddable]`; fields nullable with defaults (Doctrine always instantiates an embeddable, even for an all-NULL row) + `isEmpty()`.
- `Bank` → single `#[ORM\Embedded]`; `getStoredObject(): ?StoredObject` via `isEmpty()`; the four individual getters removed; `create()`/`rename()` adjusted.
- Readers updated to the embeddable: `DoctrineBankRepository` DQL `b.storedObject.contentHash` (2 sites) + chained getter, `BankStoredObjectRemoveListener`, `BankLogoUrlNormalizer`.
- `config/packages/doctrine.yaml` → register `SharedStorage` mapping for the embeddable's namespace (required, else `MappingException`).
- `docs/rules/architecture.md` → passive-metadata exception extended to `#[ORM\Embeddable]` value objects.
- **Out of scope (intentionally untouched):** `$media` / `logo_media_id` (still needed for raw-bytes serving); `StoredObjectWriteResult`; the search/sort allow-list.

## Test plan

- [x] `make db.diff` → No changes detected (no migration)
- [x] `make php.quality` → PHPStan max, Rector 0, cs-fixer 0/412, PHPMD 0/0, PHPCS 0, lint.doctrine OK, bounded-context/error-contract OK
- [x] `make php.test` → PHPUnit 954/954, Behat 128 scenarios / 908 steps
- [x] New unit tests: `StoredObject::isEmpty()` and `Bank::getStoredObject()` (null vs populated)
- [x] New functional keystone test: an imageless bank **reloaded from the DB** serializes `storedObjectUrl: null` (locks the all-NULL embeddable hydration invariant)

## Security review

No new attack surface. No SQL string interpolation (DQL stays parameterised); no auth/route/serialization-group changes; no secrets; no client-exposed audit fields. The `storedObjectKey` filter remains rejected by the search allow-list (`search.feature` unchanged).

## Notes

- Reviewed adversarially by three agents (blind / edge-case / acceptance). The only escalation — all-NULL embeddable hydration against the non-nullable `Bank::$storedObject` — is refuted by Doctrine's always-instantiate behavior and now pinned by the keystone test.
- Pre-existing follow-up (not in this PR): `api/features/backoffice/bank/create_with_stored_object.feature` is fully commented out; superseded by the functional test.

## Summary

- Adds `--ranking` to `python -m scripts.cli summarize` with `rmse`, `mae`, `c`, `willmott_d`, and `composite` options.
- Defaults summaries to the composite rule and writes `rank` plus `selection_rule` into summary outputs.
- Regenerates `outputs/reports/summary.csv`, `outputs/reports/summary.md`, and `outputs/tables/summary_rankings.csv` with the selected ranking rule.
- Documents the ranking behavior in the README and reproducibility notes.

## Ranking rule

The composite ranking is deterministic and transparent. Within each site/scale group it sorts by:

1. highest `c`;
2. lowest `rmse`;
3. lowest `mae`;
4. highest `willmott_d`;
5. lowest `abs(mbe)`;
6. method name as a final stable tie-breaker.

Single-metric rankings sort ascending for `rmse` and `mae`, and descending for `c` and `willmott_d`.

This PR reconstructs the missing service, mirroring the existing `storyService.ts` pattern (an exported interface + a per-chapter data map + a getter):

```ts
export interface Question {
  id: string; question: string; options: string[]; correctAnswer: string;
  explanation?: string; category: string; chapterId: number; isBoss?: boolean;
}

export const CHAPTER_QUESTIONS: Record<number, Question[]> = { /* 5 chapters */ };

export const getQuestionsForChapter = async (chapterId: number): Promise<Question[]> =>
  CHAPTER_QUESTIONS[chapterId] || [];
```

Content/shape decisions are driven by how the page and `QuestionView` consume the data:
- `getQuestionsForChapter` is `async` because the page `await`s it.
- The `Question` shape matches `QuestionView`'s props (`correctAnswer` compared as a string against an `options` entry; optional `explanation`/`isBoss`).
- Each chapter has 8 standard questions + 1 boss question = 45 total, matching the PRD (`PRD.md`: "8 Standard Questions, 1 Boss Question" per chapter) and the page's interleaving logic (`standardQuestions[0..7]` + one `bossQuestion`). Questions are themed per chapter (Geography → Ancient History → Legends & Leaders → Culture & Traditions → mixed World Challenge).

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `next build`: now compiles and prerenders all routes successfully (requires Firebase env vars in `.env.local`; without them the build fails later at static export with `auth/invalid-api-key`, which is unrelated to this fix).
- No new lint issues introduced in the changed file (the remaining lint errors are pre-existing in other files).

Closes Stage-2 idiomatization **Sprint 2 (stdlib / Phase 2)**. The pure→cold→hot module set is complete and merged:

author: onur-tellioglu
body:
## What

Implements the `--bench` performance harness (milestone **M6a**). The flag was
already referenced by `AGENTS.md` and the design spec (§10 M6) but was never wired
up — running `cargo run --release -- --bench` previously just launched the game.

`cargo run --release -- --bench` now runs a **deterministic** fixed-vantage flythrough
at the full 384-block render distance (frozen at noon, fixed `1280×720` window, seed
`1337`), warms up until streaming goes idle, records a window of frames, and prints
frame-time / GPU-time percentiles with a PASS/FAIL verdict against the 120 fps budget:

```
=== git-craft --bench ===
render distance:  12 columns (24-chunk diameter, 384 blocks)
frames recorded:  600
target:           120 fps (8.33 ms/frame)
                    min   mean    p50    p95    p99    max
CPU frame ms       1.06   4.66   4.62   7.01   8.93  10.33
GPU frame ms       8.89  13.12  13.25  15.03  18.65  21.09
verdict: FAIL (GPU p99 18.65 ms vs 8.33 ms budget)
```

`--bench-frames N` overrides the recorded window (default 600).

## Why these choices

- **GPU time is the verdict metric**, not CPU frame time. Interactive present is
  `Fifo` (vsync), which would cap frame-to-frame timing to the display cadence. The
  per-pass GPU timestamps (reused from the F3 HUD) are vsync-independent. Bench also
  prefers `Immediate` present when the surface offers it so CPU frame time is still
  meaningful, but the PASS/FAIL is driven by GPU p99.
- **Deterministic + steady-state**: fixed seed, window size, frozen noon, fixed orbit
  route, and an idle-gated warmup (records only after streaming is quiet for 30
  consecutive frames, capped so it can't hang) make the baseline reproducible.
- **Engine-core discipline**: all non-trivial logic (percentiles, orbit route, the
  warmup→record→done state machine, the report text, CLI parsing) is pure and lives in
  `src/bench.rs` with tests written first; `app.rs`/`gpu.rs` hold only winit/wgpu glue.

## M6 baseline (this is the deliverable, not a regression)

At `1280×720`, render-scale 1.0 the verdict is **FAIL**: the full M5 shader stack
(CSM, GTAO, TAA, froxel volumetrics, water SSR, bloom, exposure, post) costs ~13 ms
median on the GPU, above the 8.33 ms budget. M6a's job is to *establish* this number;
the render-scale safety valve (§11) and per-pass tuning are the follow-up perf work
this baseline now measures against.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` — all clean (230 tests, 11 new in `bench.rs`).
- `cargo run --release -- --bench` runs end-to-end: warms up, records 600 frames, prints the report, exits 0.

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-14-git-craft-m6a-bench.md`.

Bug fixes
---------

- `12444 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12444>`_: Fixed :func:`pytest.approx` which now correctly takes into account :class:`~collections.abc.Mapping` keys order to compare them.


- `13634 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13634>`_: Blocking a ``conftest.py`` file using the ``-p no:`` option is now explicitly disallowed.

  Previously this resulted in an internal assertion failure during plugin loading.

  Pytest now raises a clear ``UsageError`` explaining that conftest files are not plugins and cannot be disabled via ``-p``.


- `13734 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13734>`_: Fixed crash when a test raises an exceptiongroup with ``__tracebackhide__ = True``.


- `14195 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14195>`_: Fixed an issue where non-string messages passed to `unittest.TestCase.subTest()` were not printed.


- `14343 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14343>`_: Fixed use of insecure temporary directory (CVE-2025-71176).



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `13388 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13388>`_: Clarified documentation for ``-p`` vs ``PYTEST_PLUGINS`` plugin loading and fixed an incorrect ``-p`` example.


- `13731 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13731>`_: Clarified that capture fixtures (e.g. ``capsys`` and ``capfd``) take precedence over the ``-s`` / ``--capture=no`` command-line options in :ref:`Accessing captured output from a test function <accessing-captured-output>`.


- `14088 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14088>`_: Clarified that the default :hook:`pytest_collection` hook sets ``session.items`` before it calls :hook:`pytest_collection_finish`, not after.


- `14255 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14255>`_: TOML integer log levels must be quoted: Updating reference documentation.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `12689 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12689>`_: The test reports are now published to Codecov from GitHub Actions.

New features

- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

body:
## Integrity Issue: Section Drift (undercoverage + misalignment)

**Proof**: `mean-value-theorem-oq-02-oq-04-oq-01`
**Problem**: meta.json `sections` froze on an early ~280-line layout. The recorded §3 (242–270) and §4 (272–280) point at the wrong place — in the current 771-line file the real markers are **§3 @286, §3b @407, §3a @695, §4 @754**. Lines 281–771 (64% of the file) were unsectioned and invisible to the gallery source renderer, including the corrected complex-disk Cauchy bound lemmas (§3b) and the existential geometric approximation (§3a).

## Evidence

- `max(section.endLine) = 280`, but `wc -l = 771` and `meta.meta.lineCount` recorded `758` (also stale).
- The old "§3: Corrected Complex-Disk Statement" claimed lines 242–270; the actual `## §3` marker is at line 286, and `## §4. Verification` is at line 754 (not 272).

## Fix

- Rebuild **7 sections** aligned to the actual `§`-markers:
  - `1–142` Header / Imports / Refutation summary
  - `143–203` §1 Runge function
  - `204–285` §2 Refutation of the OQ-04 axiom statement
  - `286–406` §3 Corrected statement + off-by-one fix
  - `407–694` §3b Corrected explicit Cauchy bound lemmas
  - `695–753` §3a Existential geometric approximation
  - `754–771` §4 Verification (#check block)
- Fix `meta.lineCount` 758 → 771 (actual `wc -l`).

## Counts

- `sorries` (0): confirmed accurate — no tactic-level `sorry` remains (the §3b Cauchy lemmas were discharged at S7; the 14 `sorry` tokens are historical docstring narration).
- `axiomCount` (1): **left unchanged**. The file has 0 `axiom` declarations and states it adds no new axioms (line 209), so this may be an overcount — but `#print axioms` could not be run in this environment to rule out a transitive parent-axiom dependency. Flagged here for a build-verified follow-up rather than flipped to 0.

author: hsin-kuo
body:
## 根因
`align_segments_to_punctuated_text` 要求 `punctuated_text` 與 segments **嚴格 1:1 內容字元相同**才對齊，否則 fallback 回**原始無標點** segments。但實際上：
1. Gemini 會**改字**（不只加標點）
2. diarization 在 full_text 內嵌 `[SPEAKER_XX]` 標籤

→ 幾乎必然對不上 → segments 永遠拿不到標點（實測：full_text 標點完整、segments 全無標點，diarization 任務必中）。這是**既有 bug、與 turbo 無關**，也是「段沒對齊句子」的真因。

## 修法
- 先剝 `[SPEAKER_XX]`，再用 `difflib.SequenceMatcher` **模糊對齊**內容字元（容忍增/刪/改）
- 異常 → fallback 回原始（不打斷轉錄）；完全相同時行為同舊版
- 修好「segments 沒標點」根本問題；B（依句末標點切段）才真正能運作

6 單元測試（精準/剝 speaker/改字/插字/空輸入/回歸）；本地 272 pytest + ruff 綠。

### Motivation

- Ensure supplier owner lookup resolves accounts where the user record is keyed by Mongo `_id` while the supplier stores that value in `ownerUserId`/`userId`/`accountId`, so public profiles and safe routes show the correct owner avatar. 
- Preserve existing legacy matching (by email and legacy id fields) while handling mixed record shapes used by older accounts.

### Motivation
- Establish a complete MVP foundation for Sellora as a modular-monolith with workspace tenancy, RBAC, authentication, and auditability.

- Added the Import Center implementation including Excel parsing/normalization, mapping suggestion/validation, dry-run/execute flows, product catalog and historical imports, demo seed scripts, and strong workspace-scoped duplicate/validation checks.

author: zackees
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #3022. Eliminates ~13 KB of libgcc soft-FP cascade from the LPC845 / no-FPU ARM `fl::json` code path by gating the `float` and `fl::vector<float>` alternatives out of `json_value::variant_t` when `FL_JSON_HAS_FLOAT=0` (defaults to `FL_PLATFORM_HAS_LARGE_MEMORY`, the canonical name from #3019 / #3000).

Closes #3022 (phase 1 — the structural gate). The `fl::json_number` packed-tagged-union design from the issue body lands in phase 2; see the in-flight design-clarification comment for the parser-truncation placeholder.

## Verification (LPC845-BRK, `examples/AutoResearchLpc/AutoResearchLpc.ino`)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
|--------|--------|-------|---|
| `text` | 64 204 B | 51 280 B | **−12 924 B** |
| Flash usage | 64.20 / 64.00 KB (~98 %) | 50.44 / 64.00 KB (78.8 %) | **+13.6 KB margin** |
| `__aeabi_d*` / `__aeabi_f*` symbols | dadd, dmul, d2f, fadd, fsub, fmul, fdiv, fcmp*, f2iz, __eqsf2 | **none** | — |

Verification command (now documented in `CLAUDE.md`):

```
fbuild build -e lpc845brk
arm-none-eabi-nm -C .fbuild/build/lpc845brk/release/firmware.elf \
  | grep -E '(aeabi_d|aeabi_f|__[gle]q?[ds]f|scalbn|lround|fmod|atan|acos)'
# (empty output — goal met)
```

Or via fbuild's wrapper that auto-resolves the cross `nm`/`c++filt` from `build_info.json`:

```
fbuild symbols .fbuild/build/lpc845brk/release/firmware.elf
```

## What changed

- **`FL_JSON_HAS_FLOAT`** macro in `fl/stl/json/types.h`, defaulting to `FL_PLATFORM_HAS_LARGE_MEMORY`. Users can force `-DFL_JSON_HAS_FLOAT=1` on a Low-memory part to re-enable floats (paying the soft-FP cost).
- **Variant gating:** `float` and `fl::vector<float>` drop out of `variant_t` on `FL_JSON_HAS_FLOAT=0`. All `visit_fn<float, Visitor>` instantiations vanish, breaking the chain that pulled the unused `operator()(const float&)` visitor overloads (and their FP arithmetic) into the link.
- **Parser gating** in `fl/stl/json.cpp.hpp`: `JsonTokenizer::scan_array_lookahead`, `JsonBuilder::parse_float_array`, `JsonToken::ARRAY_FLOAT`, `JsonToken::NUMBER` (float path), `canBeRepresentedAsFloat(double)`, `optimize_array`'s `ALL_FLOATS` arm, `classify_array`'s `has_float` check. `fl::parseFloat` is no longer reachable.
- **Public constructors preserved.** `json(float)` / `json(double)` / `operator=` / `set(key, float)` stay available; on `FL_JSON_HAS_FLOAT=0` the library takes over the conversion by truncating to `i64` storage. Cost: a single `__aeabi_f2iz` / `__aeabi_d2iz` (~64 B) helper at the call site, gc-sectioned away when not used.
- **`as_float()` / `as_double()` bodies unchanged.** With `float` gone from the variant, the visitor naturally dispatches through the `i64` arm via `static_cast<FloatType>(value)`. Sketches that actually call `as_float()` pay one `__aeabi_l2f` helper; sketches that don't (like `AutoResearchLpc.ino`) pay zero.
- **ScreenMap:** `ParseJson` / `toJson` use float coordinates and a float diameter, so they extend the existing `FASTLED_NO_JSON` early-bail to also bail on `!FL_JSON_HAS_FLOAT`. A 16 KB-SRAM part has no business deserializing 2D map metadata.
- **CLAUDE.md** gains a short pointer to `fbuild symbols <elf>` and the `build_info.json` toolchain-path schema, so future agents stop hunting for `arm-none-eabi-nm` under PlatformIO package dirs.

- [x] `fbuild build -e lpc845brk` succeeds on `examples/AutoResearchLpc/AutoResearchLpc.ino`

author: azaldaniel
body:
## What (PR-6a — the upload path)

Wires the existing resumable browser-upload engine (15-state WAL ledger, CDP attach, crash-resume) to a user-facing command — migration's last-resort route, filing reconstructed charts into a destination EHR through its web UI when no vendor API or C-CDA import exists. First production driver of the upload subsystem; the GUI console driving is PR-6b.

### Manifest persistence (`deliver/browser/persist.py`)
A browser upload is a separate, operator-driven step (often a different machine, against a session the operator logs into by hand), so the driver can't re-run the pipeline — it needs the render run's `UploadItem` manifest + the `Patient` demographics on disk. `write_upload_manifest` builds items via the existing `build_manifest` and writes `<out>/upload_manifest.json`; `read_upload_manifest` reads it back. **Deterministic** (sort_keys, items sorted) and **loud on malformed** (missing/version-mismatch/bad-key → `ManifestError`, never a raw traceback). **PHI:** it carries demographics, so it lives ONLY in the 0700 dir, stores `file_path` as a **basename** (no absolute-path leak), and the writer logs an item **count** only.

### Render integration (additive)
`PipelineCommand.write_manifest` (off by default → a manifest-off `pipeline run` is byte-identical); a `STAGE_MANIFEST` event prints `manifest: N item(s)` only when on. `anast pipeline run --upload-manifest` opts in; `anast migrate` writes it by default (a migration intends to deliver) into `<out>/charts`.

### `anast upload <out_dir> --to <dest> --cdp <loopback-url> [--skiplist --max-attempts --pack-dir --yes]`
Strict safety order: read manifest (pre-attach) → **loopback `CdpEndpoint` gate before any browser is touched** → print `SHARED_MACHINE_WARNING` + confirm (unless `--yes`) **before** attaching → pack-readiness gate (names the wizard) → attach via the single injectable seam (`_make_destination`) → under the output lock with the ledger in the 0700 dir, `begin_run → recover → UploadEngine.run → finish_run → write_run_report → summary_line`. Resume is sound (re-run resumes from the ledger; the duplicate scan prevents double-filing). It **never stores EHR credentials** and **never closes the operator's browser**. Exit codes: 2 = preconditions, 1 = wrong-patient abort or any non-clean terminal, 0 = all clean.

## Verified
Orchestrator-reviewed (safety ordering, PHI containment, resume/no-double-file, exit codes, byte-stable back-compat — by reading the diff + the green gate); a separate objective review of the full snapshot raised no findings in this path. Exercised end-to-end against `FakeDestination` with no browser (the real Playwright/CDP attach is the `# pragma: no cover` seam). 28 new tests. Existing `pipeline run`/GUI/e2e back-compat unchanged. Gate: **884 passed, 1 skipped, PHI scan clean**; mypy --strict clean.

Deferred (flagged): parallel multi-session upload (needs a CDP page-pool design) and shipping a registry browser-pack destination (upload works today against any operator-discovered pack via `--pack-dir`); the GUI upload console is PR-6b.

author: daler91
body:
## Why

Spoonacular's grocery *search* data proved thin for many items (missing serving weights, then placeholder records with all-zero amounts), so it added little over USDA. **Edamam** is a better structural fit: its Food Database parser returns each food's macros **already on a per-100g basis** ([docs](https://developer.edamam.com/food-database-api)) — so there's no serving-weight to recover, which is the exact wall that hampered FatSecret Basic and Spoonacular.

## Changes

- **New `edamamClient.ts`** — parser search (one call returns every hit with per-100g nutrition inline, no N+1), UPC barcode lookup, refresh-by-name, and a straight per-100g mapper (`ENERC_KCAL`/`PROCNT`/`CHOCDF`/`FAT`/`FIBTG`). Picks the "Serving" measure as the default serving weight; drops foods with no positive macro; never throws (degrades on bad key/plan/unavailability).
- **Wiring:** Edamam ranks ahead of USDA in search and ahead of Open Food Facts in barcode; `refresh` gains an `edamam` re-fetch path. Replaces Spoonacular in the active path.
- **Schema/config:** `edamam` added to `FOOD_SOURCES` + `foods_source_check` (migration `0071`); new optional `EDAMAM_APP_ID` + `EDAMAM_APP_KEY` (both-or-neither guard).
- Spoonacular/FatSecret adapters remain in the tree but are no longer wired into search/barcode (`.env.example` notes this).

Everything degrades to USDA/Open Food Facts when Edamam is unconfigured or unavailable. Diagnostics (`Edamam search diagnostics`, `food search result mix`) carry over so the next deploy is easy to verify.

## Testing

- `npm run check` (tsc) — clean
- `eslint` on changed files — clean (only the pre-existing `tables.ts` file-length warning)
- `npm test` — **174 nutrition + 402 route/shared passing**, incl. new `edamamClient` specs (per-100g mapping, "Serving" weight, all-zero drop, knownAs fallback, bad-key degrade, UPC lookup).
- `drizzle-kit check` — migration journal consistent.

## Deploy steps

1. Sign up at [developer.edamam.com](https://developer.edamam.com) for the **Food Database API**, then set `EDAMAM_APP_ID` + `EDAMAM_APP_KEY` in Railway.
2. Migration `0071` applies automatically on boot (the app self-migrates).
3. Optional: remove `SPOONACULAR_API_KEY` (no longer used).

Then search a few foods and check the `Edamam search diagnostics` (`mapped` count) + `food search result mix` log lines.

body:
💡 What: Converted the parallel loop processing API payload nodes in `Readdir` to a sequential loop, removing `sync.WaitGroup`, `sync.Mutex`, and semaphore channels.
🎯 Why: `Readdir` is a hot path. The processing for each node consists of lightweight CPU-bound string manipulation, parsing, and map assignments. The synchronization overhead of spinning up goroutines and acquiring locks for these tasks causes substantial latency, making the concurrent approach much slower than processing them sequentially.
📊 Impact: A local micro-benchmark demonstrated a ~3x speedup when running this specific loop sequentially vs in parallel (0.39ms vs 1.28ms per operation for 1000 nodes).
🔬 Measurement: Verified by evaluating local benchmark results. Also ensures cache safety is maintained and standard build checks pass.

## What
Fixes #19. Terminal/retry writes updated `transfer_jobs` with `WHERE id=$1` only. If a transfer overran the sweeper threshold and the row was reclaimed + re-leased, the original worker's late write **clobbered** the re-leased state (lost update / double-send) and wrote an event for a job it no longer owned.

body:
This PR updates [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **5.4.3** to **9.1.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.0.3
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `12444 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12444>`_: Fixed :func:`pytest.approx` which now correctly takes into account :class:`~collections.abc.Mapping` keys order to compare them.


- `13634 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13634>`_: Blocking a ``conftest.py`` file using the ``-p no:`` option is now explicitly disallowed.

  Previously this resulted in an internal assertion failure during plugin loading.

  Pytest now raises a clear ``UsageError`` explaining that conftest files are not plugins and cannot be disabled via ``-p``.


- `13734 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13734>`_: Fixed crash when a test raises an exceptiongroup with ``__tracebackhide__ = True``.


- `14195 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14195>`_: Fixed an issue where non-string messages passed to `unittest.TestCase.subTest()` were not printed.


- `14343 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14343>`_: Fixed use of insecure temporary directory (CVE-2025-71176).



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `13388 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13388>`_: Clarified documentation for ``-p`` vs ``PYTEST_PLUGINS`` plugin loading and fixed an incorrect ``-p`` example.


- `13731 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13731>`_: Clarified that capture fixtures (e.g. ``capsys`` and ``capfd``) take precedence over the ``-s`` / ``--capture=no`` command-line options in :ref:`Accessing captured output from a test function <accessing-captured-output>`.


- `14088 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14088>`_: Clarified that the default :hook:`pytest_collection` hook sets ``session.items`` before it calls :hook:`pytest_collection_finish`, not after.


- `14255 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14255>`_: TOML integer log levels must be quoted: Updating reference documentation.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `12689 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12689>`_: The test reports are now published to Codecov from GitHub Actions.
  The test statistics is visible `on the web interface
  <https://app.codecov.io/gh/pytest-dev/pytest/tests>`__.

  -- by :user:`aleguy02`
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.2
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress feature added in pytest 9.0.0 has been disabled by default, except on Windows, due to compatibility issues with some terminal emulators.

  You may enable it again by passing ``-p terminalprogress``. We may enable it by default again once compatibility improves in the future.

  Additionally, when the environment variable ``TERM`` is ``dumb``, the escape codes are no longer emitted, even if the plugin is enabled.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the :confval:`tmp_path_retention_count` settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13946 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946>`_: The private ``config.inicfg`` attribute was changed in a breaking manner in pytest 9.0.0.
  Due to its usage in the ecosystem, it is now restored to working order using a compatibility shim.
  It will be deprecated in pytest 9.1 and removed in pytest 10.


- `13965 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13965>`_: Fixed quadratic-time behavior when handling ``unittest`` subtests in Python 3.10.



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `4492 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4492>`_: The API Reference now contains cross-reference-able documentation of :ref:`pytest's command-line flags <command-line-flags>`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.1
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13895 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13895>`_: Restore support for skipping tests via ``raise unittest.SkipTest``.


- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress plugin added in pytest 9.0 is now automatically disabled when iTerm2 is detected, it generated desktop notifications instead of the desired functionality.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the verbosity settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13910 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13910>`_: Fixed `UserWarning: Do not expect file_or_dir` on some earlier Python 3.12 and 3.13 point versions.



Packaging updates and notes for downstreams
-------------------------------------------

- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `13891 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13891>`_, `#13942 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13942>`_: The CI/CD part of the release automation is now capable of
  creating GitHub Releases without having a Git checkout on
  disk -- by :user:`bluetech` and :user:`webknjaz`.


- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------


- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

  This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in `pytest-subtests <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests>`__, but since then has been merged into the core.

  .. note::

      This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.


- `13743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743>`_: Added support for **native TOML configuration files**.

  While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in ``pyproject.toml`` files under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]``,
  it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings.
  Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

  In ``pyproject.toml``, the native TOML configuration is under the ``[tool.pytest]`` table.

  .. code-block:: toml

       pyproject.toml
      [tool.pytest]
      minver

author: bonega
body:
## Summary
In the **no-alloc** build there's no bulk decoder, so the UTF-8 decode table is only needed to derive a codepoint table at compile time. Store that table directly (`[char; 256]` / `[Option<char>; 256]`) and make `decode_byte` a single indexed load instead of decoding UTF-8 on every call. The `alloc` build is unchanged.

## Why it's free
- **Same size.** `char` and `Option<char>` are 4 bytes (niche-packed) — identical to the `Entry`/`Option<Entry>` they replace. The table stays 1 KiB.
- **Smaller code, not just faster.** The `match`/shift decode logic leaves `.text`, and the UTF-8 table is *replaced*, not added: it's consumed at const-eval and never emitted in this build.

## Verified
- **~2× faster** `decode_byte` (criterion):

  | | 256 B | 4096 B |
  |---|---|---|
  | complete (CP437) | −48% | −51% |
  | incomplete (CP874) | −44% | −50% |

- **Single load.** Under `--no-default-features`, both complete and incomplete `decode_byte` lower to `mov eax, [table + 4*rax]; ret`.
- **One table.** In a single-codepage no-alloc binary, rodata contains the codepoint-table entry for `0xDB` (`88 25 00 00` = U+2588) and **not** the UTF-8-entry signature (`e2 96 88 03`) — the UTF-8 table is gone.
- **Identical output.** The same crate built with and without `alloc` produces identical `decode_byte` results for all 256 bytes across a complete and an incomplete codepage.

## How
Only under `#[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]`: a `const DECODE_TABLE_CHAR` derived from the existing UTF-8 table via const-eval (`decoder::entry_to_char`), and `decode_byte` indexes it. Under `alloc`, `decode_byte` keeps the field-read form (the UTF-8 table is already in memory for bulk decode).

## Notes
- No public API change; the no-alloc and alloc tiers return the same values. No version bump included.
- Codegen templates updated and all 25 pages regenerated (idempotent + fmt-clean).

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test` (144 pass)
- [x] clippy `-D warnings`: all-targets + no-alloc + alloc lib
- [x] bare-metal `thumbv7em-none-eabi` builds (no-alloc and alloc)
- [x] no-alloc vs alloc `decode_byte` output diff: identical

author: baldpanda
body:
## Summary
Extends the cue-card system to the rest of the page so the whole scorecard reads as one designed object instead of just the hero + review. CSS-only — no `app.py` change needed; the new rules target Gradio's existing ids/classes.

- **Card labels.** Every `.scorecard-card h2` (Step up to the mic, How it's going, Pacing, Crutch words) becomes a small typeset mono label: burgundy, 0.72rem, 800, letter-spacing 0.12em, uppercase.
- **Review heading as a tab.** `#review-card h2` becomes an inline-block burgundy pill (cream text, soft shadow) — a bookend to the hero's green file tab.
- **Lined transcript.** `#transcript-output textarea` gets ruled lines + a burgundy margin rule painted directly on the textarea, with `background-attachment: local` so the ruling scrolls with the text.
- `.scorecard-card { position: relative }` so labels/tabs can anchor.

Handwriting stays rationed to the coach's voice only — everything else stays Georgia + mono.

## Risk
Low. Purely additive CSS at the bottom of `assets/scorecard.css`. No Python logic changes, no new dependencies, no DOM changes. Easy to revert.

## Not included (deliberate)
- Circling individual crutch words inside the transcript — needs the transcript rendered as Markdown/HTML spans instead of a `gr.Textbox`.
- Rebuilding the pacing gauge / crutch chips as bespoke widgets — they stay as the model's markdown output.

## Test plan
- [ ] Load the app and confirm every card heading reads as a small burgundy mono label.
- [ ] Confirm the honest-review heading renders as an inline burgundy pill.
- [ ] Run a speech through and confirm the transcript textarea shows ruled lines + burgundy margin rule; lines stay aligned while scrolling.
- [ ] Hero and honest-review (existing cue-card surfaces) still render correctly.
- [ ] Mobile width (≤760px) — labels and lined transcript still look right.

author: t-benze
body:
## REPRODUCTION EVIDENCE

The test `test_revisit_roundtrip_creates_new_root_and_completes` failed **10/10** on origin/main @ 8815853 with:

```
AssertionError: 'resolved_superseded' != 'blocked'
at tests/integration/test_end_to_end.py:503
```

The `_supersede_predecessor_locked` call is synchronous under `org.db_lock`, so this is a **deterministic failure**, not a timing race.

## ROOT CAUSE

THR-018 tier #3 (commits fc3e21e → a613624) added auto-resolve of blocked(escalated|delegated) predecessors to `RESOLVED_SUPERSEDED` (with `block_kind` cleared) in `revisit_from_notification`. This integration test's expectation (`status=='blocked'`, `block_kind=='escalated'`) was **never updated** and went stale.

## THE FIX

Test-only correction in `tests/integration/test_end_to_end.py` (+6/-5):
- Predecessor expectation: `status=='resolved_superseded'` / `block_kind is None`
- Docstring updated to cite THR-018 tier #3 auto-supersede

Steps 1-3 of the test are **unchanged**:
1. Predecessor reaches `blocked`
2. `POST /revisit` returns `predecessor_status=='blocked-escalated'` + `predecessor_root_task_id`
3. New root reaches `completed`

**No production logic changed.** Nothing was skipped, xfailed, quarantined, or deleted. The assertion was **not** loosened to mask a race — exact status and block_kind are still asserted, only the values corrected.

## GREEN SUITE / DETERMINISM

- **50/50 passes** including a pytest-randomly order-randomized sweep (QA TASK-343)
- Full integration suite: **41 passed**
- Full unit suite: **2048 passed** / 1 pre-existing unrelated skip
- GitNexus impact: **LOW** (0 upstream callers, test-only symbol)

author: lucasmccomb
body:
## Summary

Hardens `tests/test-no-personal-data.sh` so a contributor pasting a **new** secret or personal email is caught, not just the maintainer-name allowlist.

## Changes

- **Generic secret/PII detection.** Added regex shapes for `sk-`, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`, `re_` (Resend), `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`, PEM `-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----` blocks, and email addresses. These fire on any new value, not a fixed list.
- **Tightly-scoped allowlist** to avoid false positives on illustrative content: `__PLACEHOLDER__`, angle-bracket placeholders, regex-class pattern definitions (the autoheal/audit modules describe these shapes literally), `redacted` docs, the AWS official `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`, obvious fake test tokens, RFC-2606 / `example.com` / single-letter fixture emails, and an explicit `ccgm-allow-secret` line marker.
- **Widened scan surface.** The secret/PII scan now covers the **whole repo** (including `docs/`), minus `.git`, `node_modules`, caches, and `docs/audits/`. The maintainer-identity scan keeps its historical narrow target set, because the public GitHub owner handle appears legitimately throughout `docs/`, Go import paths, `FUNDING.yml`, and `LICENSE`.
- **Self-test (`--self-test`).** Plants a fake `ghp_` token and a PII email in a temp dir, asserts the detector FAILs on them and PASSes a clean file. Wired into both CI jobs so the detector itself is regression-tested.
- **`.gitignore`:** added `docs/audits/` so local audit artifacts are never published.

## Test Plan

```
$ bash tests/test-no-personal-data.sh --self-test
SELF-TEST PASS    (detects planted ghp_ token + PII email; passes clean file)

$ bash tests/test-no-personal-data.sh
PASS: No personal data or secret/PII shapes found

# Integration: plant AKIA... key in docs/ -> full scan FAILs as expected, PASSes again after cleanup.
```

Closes #664
Part of #659

body:
# `jarvis prompt` agent fallback

- Intent: `v2/spec/2026-06-14T17-01-11Z-prompt-mode-agent-fallback/intent.md`
- Index: `v2/spec/2026-06-14T17-01-11Z-prompt-mode-agent-fallback/index.md`

<!-- jarvis:narrative:start -->
This is a plan-mode PR — the deliverable is the spec, not the implementation. Here's the PR description:

---

Drafts a spec to fix `jarvis prompt` agent fallback. Prompt mode is documented as trying `modes.prompt.agentOrder` in order until one agent succeeds, but the code `break`s on the first quota result, so a configured `claude → codex → cursor` fallback never reaches later agents. The spec changes the `quota` branch from break→continue, pins the terminal exit policy (exit 2 only when *every* agent returned quota; exit 3 otherwise), adds a testing seam, and aligns docs with the implemented behavior.

Decisions:
- Only `quota` gains fallthrough — `model_config`/`error`/`watchdog` keep their current halting behavior, so real per-agent failures aren't masked.
- Terminal exit is computed from "did any attempted agent fail for a non-quota reason," not "was quota ever seen" — a `model_config → quota` chain exits 3 (`telemetryKind=error`), only an all-quota chain exits 2 (`all-agents-quota`). Avoids last-write-wins mislabeling the mixed chain.
- New terminal logic replaces both the in-loop `exit 2` and the generic post-loop `return 3`; otherwise the all-quota chain falls through to the catch-all and silently breaks the exit-2 criterion.
- Per-agent quota fallthrough emits the shared harness rotation line (augmenting, not replacing, raw stderr) and exhaustion emits `HARNESS_ALL_AGENTS_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` — matching patch-mode for log consistency.
- Terminal-agent and `configured_model` telemetry update on every attempt (including each quota `continue`) so the single all-quota row names the last agent tried, not `unknown`.
- Telemetry stays one row per command; no per-attempt rows or redesign — the existing row already represents the terminal result.
- Adds `agents?: Partial<Record<AgentName, Agent>>` to `PromptRunOptions` (mirroring patch's `buildActiveAgents`) so agent-order behavior is testable without fake binaries on PATH.
- Scoped to one subspec; docs updates land with it (`v1/docs/specless-prompt.md` fallback policy, `v2/docs/v1-behaviors.md` prompt entry).

body:
## Per-stock next-month return forecast (ARX) + leakage-free backtest

Adds a new `vantage.forecast` module and a **Forecast** tab.

**Model.** For each of the 28 constituents, an autoregressive model with exogenous inputs (ARX) predicts the **next month's** return from:
- autoregressive lags of the stock's own monthly returns,
- the macro indicators (YoY-transformed, lagged one month for publication delay),
- trailing sector- and market-index momentum.

**No look-ahead.** Features at month `t` use only data through `t`; the target is the `t→t+1` return. The backtest is walk-forward: at each step it fits only on months whose target had already been realised, and standardises features with training-window stats only (ridge, closed-form numpy).

**Honest scoring.** Predictions are compared to a random-walk baseline (predict 0). Reported per stock: out-of-sample R², directional hit rate, RMSE-vs-baseline, and `beats_baseline`. The tab says plainly that monthly stock returns are mostly noise and that across 28 names some will look good by chance — not investment advice.

**Tests.** `tests/forecast/test_arx.py` — ridge recovers a known linear relationship; features target the next month with no leakage; the backtest **detects a genuine AR(1) signal** and shows **no skill on white noise**. Full suite: **45 passed**, `ruff` clean. Also exercised the full DB→leaderboard→per-stock path against a seeded store.

Merging auto-deploys to the droplet.

author: copilot
body:
Plan 019 requires **human-led security decisions** for three audit-flagged auth items (plus confirmation of a fourth), with an explicit constraint: **no auth code changes** — only investigation, threat modeling, and follow-up specs. This PR delivers that as docs-only.

## Key finding (revises the issue's assumption)
The two flagged endpoints are **LIVE, not legacy/dead**. `infra/cognito.tf` wires `/api/auth/cognito/token` and `/api/auth/cognito/user` as the GitHub identity provider's `token_url`, `attributes_url`, and `jwks_uri` — they are a **Cognito↔GitHub OIDC shim** invoked **server-to-server by Cognito**, not the browser:

```hcl
token_url      = "${api_endpoint}/api/auth/cognito/token"
attributes_url = "${api_endpoint}/api/auth/cognito/user"
jwks_uri       = "${api_endpoint}/api/auth/cognito/token"
```

This trips the plan's escalation condition ("relay actively used → escalate before removal"), so item A's decision is **harden in place, do not remove**.

## Changes
- **`docs/auth-hardening-decisions.md`** — ADR-style decision record; usage determination with evidence; per-item decision, OWASP mapping, and severity:
  - **A** (Medium — A04/A07, SSRF-adjacent): open relay forwards caller-supplied `client_id`/`client_secret`/`code`. Decision: pin credentials server-side (constant-time check), stop reflecting upstream errors, add edge rate-limiting. LIVE → keep.
  - **B** (Medium — A01 login-CSRF/A04): `state` carries only `redirect_url`, is never server-bound, and the code is exchanged *before* `state` is validated. Decision: signed state nonce + validate-before-exchange.
  - **C** (closed): `validateRedirectUrl` is allow-list backed; documented the fail-closed empty-list deploy caveat.
  - **D** (low/info): confirmed no tokens/secrets/cookies logged.
- **`docs/auth-oauth-relay-hardening-plan.md`** — follow-up implementation plan for A (steps, tests, human + Security Engineer review gate).
- **`docs/auth-state-nonce-plan.md`** — follow-up implementation plan for B (frontend + backend, review gate).

## Notes for reviewers
- No auth route/controller/middleware or infra was modified — remediation lands in the linked, human-approved follow-up plans.
- **Action item surfaced:** verify `ALLOWED_FRONTEND_ORIGINS` is non-empty in every deployed environment (defaults to `[]`, fail-closed).

author: keddie
body:
> 🤖 This PR was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Two phase-2 `MeshSeam` hardening fixes.

**#419 — cross-node dedup agreement.** The simultaneous-dial dedup branched on a *self-relative* `selfId < remoteId` comparison to choose which of two duplicate links to keep. The two endpoints shared no per-link identity, so on a genuine simultaneous dial (two physical links between the same pair) each node could keep a *different* link, leaving one half-open. This was a real bug — `simultaneousDialDedupAgreesCrossNode` fails on the old rule and passes on the fix. Each side now draws a per-connection nonce in the mesh preamble; the canonical link identity is an order-independent function of both nonces, so both ends pick the same survivor with no coordination. Nonce RNG is injectable (`Random.Default` in production, seeded in tests).

**#420 — dynamic peer-join.** `meshSeam` now returns a `Mesh : Seam` exposing `suspend fun addLink(conn: Conn)` — admit a peer that dials in after construction: handshake, canonical dedup against existing links, roster update, readLoop launch, all under the existing `links` lock (no confinement).

Thread-safety preserved: atomics + `reentrantLock`, peers published inside the lock and before state on teardown. New `addLinkIsRaceFreeAgainstConcurrentClose` real-threaded probe (200 iterations) covers the new lock paths.

Closes #419, closes #420. Part of #387.

body:
## What

Extends Productive Frogs' in-game Patchouli guide (`productivefrogs:guide`, shipped in PF 1.21) with a pack-specific **Sky Frogs (Pack)** category, merged into the same book via the resource-pack system - no second book. Closes #182.

## Entries (focused reference, not a parallel guide)

Four entries covering what the quest book does poorly and what stock PF cannot know:
- **Welcome to Sky Frogs** - the void-skyblock premise (no mining; frogs are the whole economy).
- **The Dissolution Chamber** - the pack's slime engine and its recipe pattern (100 mB latex + prior resource + 4 tier-filler + 3 Sweetslime), chamber-only from Tide on.
- **Pack Changes to Know** - the overrides that would surprise a player: quartz-free storage, the redstone Teeming catalyst (not glowstone), and the per-tier Spawnery primers.
- **The Singularity Endgame** - Quantum Compressor -> per-resource Singularities -> Ultimate Singularity -> the Master Frog.

## How it merges

PF's `book.json` is `use_resource_pack: true` + `i18n: false`, so the pack drops inline-text entries (matching PF's own format) into the book's namespace via KubeJS assets:

```
pack/kubejs/assets/productivefrogs/patchouli_books/guide/en_us/categories/sky_frogs.json
pack/kubejs/assets/productivefrogs/patchouli_books/guide/en_us/entries/sky_frogs/*.json
```

Category `productivefrogs:sky_frogs`, sortnum 1000 (after PF's, which top out at 500).

## Correctness

- Every mechanic claim ground-truthed against the pack scripts (`catalyst_recipes.js`, `spawnery_primer/*` tags, `dissolution_slime_recipes.js`) and the EC/IF jars - not memory.
- All 5 JSON files lint clean; ASCII-only; plain text (no Patchouli macros), matching PF's entry style.
- New doc `docs/patchouli_guide.md` documents the extension path, the **new-entries-not-pages** limitation, and the dev caveat: **`kubejs/assets` is NOT junctioned** into the dev instance, so book edits need an export/sync to test in-game (unlike the live quest-edit loop).
- No automated validator exists for Patchouli (the `validate_quests` gate is FTB Quests only); it stays clean (333 quests).

## Hold for playtest

Content change. Because assets aren't junctioned, verifying in-game needs an asset sync/export first - then open the PF guide and confirm the Sky Frogs category renders with all four entries.

author: joelstobart-moj
body:
## Summary
Fixes a timezone normalisation issue affecting documentGeneratedTimestamp.
Inbound HMCTS messages are currently deserialised as LocalDateTime, which strips timezone semantics. As the input represents UK local time (BST/GMT), it is persisted as if it were UTC, resulting in a consistent ~1 hour skew in the database.

## Changes
### Ingestion fix

* Change inbound documentGeneratedTimestamp from LocalDateTime to Instant
* Treat timestamps without an explicit offset as Europe/London
* Convert to UTC before persistence

### Data fix (Flyway)

Apply migration to correct existing records:

`update public.court_documentset document_generated_timestamp = document_generated_timestamp - interval '1 hour'`

Verified via analysis that all rows exhibit ≥1 hour offset, so safe to correct globally

## Tests

Add unit test to verify BST → UTC conversion
Prevents regression of timezone handling


## Why
Production data analysis showed:

- ~94% of records have a consistent ~1 hour offset
- Remaining records show additional latency on top of the same offset
- No records exist with <1 hour difference

This confirms a systematic timezone misinterpretation, not a partial or upstream inconsistency.

## Impact

- Existing data corrected and aligned
- New ingested data stored correctly as UTC
- Frontend display and ordering will be consistent

author: jakechampion
body:
## What

Closes the **single largest reachable IR-coverage gap** in the self-host (an empirical census measured **188 bails** in the flattened compiler — the compiler's own AST-walking idiom). A union type `type Node = Num | Add;` matched as `match (n) { Num(x) => x.value, … }` previously kicked the **whole module** to the legacy AST backend; it now lowers via IR.

## Root cause

The match-arm payload bind only handled the `enum E { V(T) }` desugar (a synthetic `__ev` field read at offset 8). A **union** variant `Num` is a pre-existing struct with its *real* fields and no `__ev`, so `ev_ty` was `""`, the bound var's slot was never typed, and a later `x.value` bailed at `expr_struct_type(x) == ""`.

## Fix (`irlower.fern`, +25 lines, additive — no `LowerState` field)

Discriminate union-member vs enum-variant by `decl_field_type(structs, vname, "__ev") == ""` (the exact complement of asmcore's `is_enum_variant`). For a union member, bind the **whole scrutinee box pointer** (`op_load_local(scrut)` → `op_store_local(bind)`; no `struct_get`/offset — the variant box pointer *is* the value) + `mark_struct_type(slot, vname)` so `x.field` resolves. Mirrors the legacy AST emitter's split at `asm.fern:3677-3693`. The enum `__ev` offset-8 path is unchanged.

## Tests / verification (local)

- `self_host_union_irpath_test.go` (new) + `union-*` cases in the asm/wasm IR-path corpora — **6 differential** x86-64 + wasm programs (basic eval, multi-field members, field-read-in-expr, nested match, method dispatch on a bound member field, `_` wildcard), each asserting **AST==IR** exit codes **and** routing flip to `"ir"`.
- Verified: routing + regression (`SelfHostUnionIRPath|AsmIRPath|BlockExpr|DynTrait`) green (185s); **true enum-payload matches still route IR** (no `__ev` regression); **byte-identical fixpoint** GREEN (334s); `go build` clean.

## Roadmap note

The census found that after this, the next-largest self-host bails (~109, the #2–5 constructs) are **all RC-sensitive Perceus guards** ("bail to AST to preserve RC behaviour") — *not* closeable as pure `irlower` work. So this is likely the **last large pure-IR-lowering widening** before goal-1 on the compiler's own modules becomes gated on the **goal-2 Perceus port**.

body:
## What

A new **/today** landing page — a daily command centre that pulls everything date-driven into one place, so the team doesn't rely on catching a push notification in the moment.

This is **Phase 1 (page)** of a "page first, then alerts" plan. It answers the original question — *"can it remind us when vehicles are due for inspections?"* — by surfacing it on a standing page. Phase 2 (the alerting half) is a morning cron that scans the same expiry dates and fires notifications + push.

## Sections

- **Fleet compliance** — equipment registration (rego), Certificate of Fitness, and scheduled service dates, **including overdue items**. Note: the existing `GET /api/equipment/expiring` only covers the next 30 days and skips both already-expired and service-due dates, so this needed its own aggregator.
- **Today's schedule** — jobs running on the NZ calendar day (honours multi-day `scheduled_dates` sets via `jobRunsOnNZDate`).
- **Summary tiles** — needs-attention / due-soon / jobs-today counts.

## How it's built

- Backend: new read-only `GET /api/today-overview`, computed entirely from existing `storage` (equipment + jobs), business-scoped via the same RLS connection as every other route. **No schema change, no migration.**
- Frontend: `client/src/pages/TodayDashboard.tsx`, lazy-routed at `/today`, with a "Today" sidebar link above Dispatch Board.
- Compliance dates use NZ-calendar whole-day math; severity = overdue / critical (≤7d) / warning (≤14d) / info (≤30d).

## Test notes

- Add registration / CoF / service dates to equipment on the register, then open `/today` — items due within 30 days (or overdue) appear, most-urgent first.
- Empty states guide the user to populate dates.

## Not in this PR (planned follow-up)
