author: kdeyarmin
body:
## Problem

Audit finding **B3** — several admin views silently swallow a failed fetch and render a "success-looking" empty state, so an operator can't tell the difference between "there's genuinely nothing here" and "the request failed."

- **System Configuration → Recent activity** (`admin-system-configuration.tsx`): `RecentActivity` destructured only `data` from `useQuery`, so a failed activity fetch rendered *"No configuration changes recorded yet."* as if the load had succeeded — no spinner, no error, no retry.
- **Abandoned carts / Insurance leads / Fitter leads**: the empty-state table row was gated only on `!isPending && rows.length === 0`. On a failed fetch `rows` is empty and `isPending` is false, so the empty row rendered *at the same time* as the `ErrorPanel` above the table — a contradictory "error + nothing here" view.

## Fix

- `RecentActivity` now destructures `isPending / isError / error / refetch` and renders `Spinner` while loading and `ErrorPanel` (with Retry) on failure, matching the page's primary query.
- The three lead/cart tables gate their empty-state row on `!isError` as well, so a failed load shows only the error panel.

No behavior change on the success path. Pure frontend.

## Verification

- `typecheck` (tsc -b) clean
- `eslint` clean on all four files

author: dammianmiller
body:
The opencode+UAP terminal-bench harness produced **zero tool calls** for any model other than the hardcoded Qwen3.5 — surfaced while benchmarking qwen3.6.

## Root causes (two, stacked)
1. **`ProviderModelNotFoundError`** — `_make_opencode_config` hardcoded the model id `qwen35-a3b-iq4xs`, so harbor `-m llama.cpp/qwen3.6-a3b-iq4xs` couldn't resolve and the opencode session died before running. **Fix:** derive provider + model id from `self.model_name` (the harbor `-m` value) — model-agnostic.
2. **Deprecated GBNF tool-choice proxy** broke native OpenAI tool calls for modern local models (Qwen3.6+). **Fix:** opencode points directly at the model endpoint; `UAP_BENCH_PROXY=1` restores the old proxy path.

## Validation (live, not synthetic)
qwen3.6 on `terminal-bench@2.0` via opencode+UAP:
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| tool calls | none (session died / GBNF) | native ✓ |
| quick (6) | 0% | **67% (4/6)** |
| full (15) | 0% | **53% (8/15)** |

body:
Closes #712.

## Problem

Packaged builds (macOS `.app`, Linux `.deb`, Windows) launch the binary with **no arguments**, so `--midi` / `--mcp` never reached the installed app — MIDI and the MCP server only ever came up under `cargo` with the flags. A freshly installed OpenRig had MIDI dead out of the box (surfaced via the M-Vave Chocolate: ports opened, but no control reached the app).

Enabling MIDI/MCP is a **per-machine** decision → system config (ADR 0003), not a launch argument every packaging script has to remember.

## What changed

- `config.yaml` gains master switches `midi_enabled` / `mcp_enabled` (both default `false`, `#[serde(default)]`). Distinct from the per-port `midi_devices[].enabled` selection — these gate the whole subsystem.
- Pure resolvers `resolve_mcp_addr` / `resolve_midi_map` fold config into the CLI result: a present `--midi` / `--mcp` flag wins as a dev override, otherwise the config switch decides. `DEFAULT_MCP_ADDR` extracted as the single source.
- `Command::SetMidiEnabled` / `SetMcpEnabled` (+ `*EnabledChanged` events) persist the switch to `config.yaml` — GUI/MCP/gRPC parity. MCP tool parity guard bumped 63→65.
- **Settings → System / Integrations** section with two toggles, dispatching the commands. i18n across all 9 locales. Takes effect on next launch (subsystem is wired at bootstrap); the section shows a restart hint.

## Persistence-clobber fix (caught in review with the user)

First cut persisted to `config.yaml` but the toggle came back **off** after a restart. Root cause: the GUI holds a boot-time `Rc<RefCell<AppConfig>>` that `recent_projects_wiring` / project-open paths re-save WHOLESALE; a toggle that only wrote disk got clobbered by the stale boot snapshot. Fixed by mirroring `settings::audio` — the wiring also mutates `app_config.borrow_mut()` so the wholesale save carries the new value.

## Tests (RED-first)

config serde defaults/roundtrip, resolver matrix, dispatcher persistence under `with_tmp_home`, MCP parity, i18n key coverage, and source-presence guards on the toggle wiring (dispatch + snapshot sync). `cargo test --workspace --lib` green.

## Out of scope

The BLE-MIDI rescan/drop churn seen in the original logs (separate concern; duplicate ports are already keyed by `port_key.instance`).

author: abgregs
body:
## Summary
Closes the gap found while planning release distribution: `git.md` claimed `main` was protected, but the repo had **no branch protection or ruleset at all**. This lands the maintainer-approval merge gate ([CODEOWNERS](.github/CODEOWNERS)) and corrects the docs. It's the doc/config half of the "once public" security items in [0005](docs/planning/0005_release-pipeline-security.md); the GitHub-side rulesets are applied via API around this PR (see Sequencing).

## Scope
One commit, 3 files (+13/−2): `.github/CODEOWNERS` (new), `docs/conventions/git.md`, `docs/planning/0005_release-pipeline-security.md`.

## Changes Made
- **`.github/CODEOWNERS`** — `* @abgregs`, so the `main` ruleset's code-owner-review rule gates every PR (including fork PRs) on the maintainer's approval
- **`git.md`** — rewrote "What touches `main`": the old "direct push permanently disabled" line was false. Now documents the real ruleset (PR required, force-push/deletion blocked, code-owner review required, admin self-bypass to avoid own-PR deadlock) and the `v*` tag ruleset (deletion/force-push blocked, no bypass, creation open)
- **0005** — marked the "once public" protection criterion done (rulesets active, private vulnerability reporting enabled); pipeline-hardening items still gate M11

## Sequencing (why config lands around, not in, this PR)
- ✅ Already applied via API: private vulnerability reporting **enabled**; `v*` tag ruleset **active** (id 17668311) — self-contained, no file dependency
- ⏳ The `main` branch ruleset is applied **after** this PR merges — its code-owner-review rule is vacuous until CODEOWNERS is on `main`. Arming it first would be a gate that looks active but enforces nothing.

## Impact
- After merge + main ruleset: fork contributors can open PRs but cannot merge; the maintainer's approval is required to merge; force-push and branch deletion blocked; `v*` tags immutable
- Admin bypass means the maintainer can still merge their own PRs (GitHub forbids self-approval); it guarantees *others* can't merge without approval, not that the maintainer must record one on their own PRs

## Testing
- [ ] Merge this PR (main not yet protected — normal merge)
- [ ] Apply the `main` ruleset via API; verify bypass actor resolves to the Admin role
- [ ] Verify enforcement: a test PR shows the code-owner-review requirement

author: milechy
body:
## 背景（再発防止 / Asana 1215691378757415）
i18n wave 系 PR が `messages/*.json` を全体上書きする運用のため、機能 PR で足した i18n キーが後続 wave に**巻き込まれて消える事故**が複数回発生（#730 緊急停止ボタンの生キー表示「Liff.home.emergencyStop」）。next-intl はキー未解決時に**例外を投げず生キーを描画**するため、`tsc` も `next build` も通過し検出できなかった。

## 追加
- **`frontend/scripts/check-i18n-keys.mjs`**: `app`・`components` 配下の `useTranslations(NS)` / `t("static.key")` を抽出し、各 `NS.key` が `ja.json`・`en.json` 両方に存在するか検証。
- **baseline ratchet 方式**: 既存の欠落（admin/web 画面の i18n 負債 **29 件**）を `i18n-missing-baseline.json` に固定し、CI では「**baseline に無い新規欠落**」だけを fail にする。既存負債で全 PR をブロックせず、「**存在したキーが消える**」事故（#730 型）は新規欠落として確実に検出。
- **`ci.yml`** frontend ジョブに Build 前ステップとして追加（早期失敗）。
- `npm run check:i18n` / `node scripts/check-i18n-keys.mjs --update-baseline`（負債を直した時に baseline 縮小）。

## 実証
`Liff.home.emergencyStop` を一時削除 → 検査 **FAIL**（`Liff.home.emergencyStop [ja:✗ en:✓]` を新規欠落として検出）、復元 → **pass** を確認済み。= #730 シナリオを正確に捕捉。

## タスク1（`1215690860479307` next build）について
調査の結果、**CI には既に `npm run build`（ci.yml frontend ジョブ）が push/PR 両方であり**、parse エラー（#726 重複 import 型）は CI build で検出される。#726 が通過したのは branch protection の「**require branches up to date before merging**」未設定で、PR が最新 base に対して再ビルドされなかったため。これは**リポジトリ設定**の問題のため、本 PR とは別に設定対応が必要（タスク notes に追記）。

## 既知の i18n 負債（baseline 29 件 / 別タスク化推奨）
admin/web 画面で実際に生キーが出る既存バグ（例: `AdminEvents.mockMsg1-8`、`AiMonitor.mockReason1-3`、web版 `EmergencyStop.*`）。liff-chat ローンチ動線には含まれないため本 PR では baseline 固定に留め、解消は別タスク。

Macht die Lightning-Integration (Phase 1, #239) auf dem Dashboard **greifbar — ohne Fake-Daten**. Ehrliche States: `disabled` / `unavailable` / `ok`.

author: sothiss
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/sothiss/ethopipe/security/code-scanning/13](https://github.com/sothiss/ethopipe/security/code-scanning/13)

The safest fix is to stop sending raw exception details to clients and return a generic error message instead, while logging full exception details on the server side for debugging.

In `.agents/skills/building-data-apps/examples/fastapi_chat.py`, update the `except Exception as e:` block inside `event_generator()` so it:
1. Logs the exception server-side (using Python’s standard `logging` with `logging.exception(...)` to include traceback).
2. Sends only a generic user-facing error string in the SSE payload.

This preserves existing functionality (client still receives a final error event + `[DONE]`) without leaking internals. Add a standard-library import `import logging` and a module logger definition (for example `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`).

author: weslley6216
body:
## Objetivo
Formalizar a mudança de schema já executada em produção (tornar liters e odometer_km opcionais) e cobrir com specs os guards de nil que evitam crashes em dois services, além de corrigir um bug crítico no componente de visualização.

## Execução

**Migrações e validações:**
- Migration formalizando `change_column_null` para liters e odometer_km (já executada no banco via console; agora parte do schema oficial)
- Model validations ajustadas: apenas `date` e `total_amount` obrigatórios; `liters` e `odometer_km` aceitam nil (importação de extratos bancários sem esses dados)

**Robustez dos services:**
- `Vehicles::Statistics#km_this_month`: guard contra nil odometer_km do primeiro refueling do mês (retorna 0)
- `Refuelings::VendorEfficiency#average_kml_for`: skip de readings com nil odometer_km ao calcular médias kml por vendor (filter_map com guard)

**Bug crítico no componente (encontrado por code review):**
- `TankBalanceCardComponent#last_fill_text`: renderiza liters/price_per_liter sem verificar nil
- Impacto: crashes ao renderizar um refueling importado com `full_tank: true` e `liters: nil` selecionado como last_fill
- Fix: guard `@last_fill.liters.present?` com fallback ao título genérico
- Coverage: spec adicionada cobrindo o caso de nil liters

**Outros ajustes:**
- Spec de request PATCH /refuelings/:id ajustada: trigger de inválido passa de `liters: ''` para `total_amount: ''` (liters agora opcional)

**Resultado:**
- 6 commits com Conventional Commits (feat, fix, refactor, test)
- 1144 exemplos RSpec, 0 failures, **100% coverage**
- 0 offenses Rubocop

author: nyldn
body:
Fixes all four bugs reported in #481 by L3ulll on Fedora / 9.44.0.

## Root causes and fixes

**1. `scripts/helpers/check-ollama-models.sh:16` — OCTO_ROOT resolves CWD's git repo**

`git -C "$(pwd)" rev-parse --show-toplevel` looks up the *caller's* working directory. Run from inside any other git repo it pointed there, failed to find `provider-versions.sh`, and exited 1.

Fix: derive root from the script's own location via `BASH_SOURCE[0]`.

```diff
-OCTO_ROOT="${OCTO_ROOT:-$(git -C "$(pwd)" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "${HOME}/.claude-octopus/plugin")}"
+OCTO_ROOT="${OCTO_ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
```

**2. `scripts/lib/doctor.sh:177` — stale_count unguarded under `set -eo pipefail`**

`stale_count=$(bash "$_check" --count-stale 2>/dev/null)` ran the helper that now exits 1 (bug #1), so the command substitution propagated that nonzero exit and aborted the entire `doctor` run before any report printed.

Fix: `|| echo "0"` (same pattern as the sanitize expression on the next line).

**3. `scripts/lib/agent-sync.sh` — no `mkdir -p` for `$RESULTS_DIR` in council path**

`debate.sh`, `research.sh`, and `spawn.sh` all call `mkdir -p "$RESULTS_DIR"` before their dispatch loops. The council dispatch path skips this, so every agent dies with "No such file or directory" on the `> "$temp_err"` / `> "$temp_out"` init and produces no report.

Fix: one `mkdir -p "${RESULTS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true` before the temp-file init block in `run_agent_sync`.

**4. Self-referential symlink in skill-doctor resolver**

`ln -sfn "$OCTO_PLUGIN_ROOT" "${HOME}/.claude-octopus/plugin"` was unconditional. When `$OCTO_PLUGIN_ROOT` resolved to the symlink path itself (e.g. `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set to `~/.claude-octopus/plugin`), it created a symlink pointing at itself → "Too many levels of symbolic links".

Fix: apply the same guard already present in `octo_ensure_stable_plugin_root` (plugin-root.sh lines 98–105) to the inline resolver blocks in `skills/skill-doctor/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/skill-doctor/SKILL.md`, and `.cursor-plugin/commands/octo-doctor.md`.

## Tests

- `bash -n` on all three shell scripts: clean
- Fixes are minimal one-liners / small guards; no logic changes beyond the specific failure mode

closes #481

author: brettstark73
body:
Review is machine-only (Claude finds, Codex verifies) on flat-rate subs, so the
real cost is wall-clock — yet the skill ran the full 6-agent + Codex pass on
every PR in the 23 repos that lack a per-repo gate (falling back to L95). That's
the 1hr+ slowness.

Adds scripts/risk-score.js: a zero-dependency, kit-native scorer that computes a
0-100 risk score from git diff in ANY repo (no per-repo setup) and emits three
depth knobs — Claude agent count (2-10), Codex effort (skip-xhigh), Codex rounds
(0-2). Inputs: path sensitivity (built-in security-floor globs + optional
harness-config.json:scorePolicy override), change nature (mechanical vs logic,
ported from the claude-setup gate), diff magnitude (raise-only), forced-logic
(deletions/renames/binaries/workflows/prompt-surfaces).

SKILL Step 0.5: kit score (primary) -> legacy gate tier -> L95 (graceful
fallback). Agent panel selected by count from a priority-ordered list; Codex
effort/rounds score-driven with a bounded re-verify loop under the 25-min cap.

Invariants (Moderate curve):
- Floor: every change gets >=2 Claude agents — never zero machine review.
- Security surface pinned >=75 regardless of nature — mechanical never beats floor.
- Large mechanical diff: magnitude cap prevents low score (addresses ~16%
  mechanical-FN risk from refactoring/SZZ research).
- Trivial change -> ~0 -> 2 agents, no Codex (~1min).

Proven: qa-architect #175/#176 (package.json/.husky) -> 92-96 -> full review
(correctly NOT downgraded); trivial diffs -> 0 -> fast. SOTA-checked vs Meta
RADAR; dropped its human-centric auto-approve (no human backstop here).

Tests: 30 cases. Full suite 171 green.

## Summary
- Fixes Discord issue #1007: Fractal Harness now attaches to the Fractal token it creates on ETB.
